items.title: The piezochiral effect
items.summary: The paper introduces a previously unrecognized physical phenomenon called the piezochiral effect, in which mechanical strain induces and controls chirality in solid-state materials. Through symmetry analysis, the authors show that uniaxial strain can generate chirality in a broad class of achiral crystals that contain structural fragments of opposite handedness within each unit cell, with the induced handedness tunable by changing the direction of strain or by switching between compressive and tensile strain. This theoretical framework was experimentally validated using optical activity measurements on a crystal under applied strain, confirming that strain can serve as a conjugate field that couples linearly to chiral structural order. The discovery addresses a longstanding challenge in materials science—the absence of a universal field for rational chirality control—and provides a continuous, bidirectional mechanism for switching handedness in solids. The authors suggest broad implications for applications spanning spintronics, asymmetric catalysis, and enantioselective biological interactions.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it introduces a previously unrecognized physical phenomenon—the piezochiral effect—whereby mechanical strain can be used to control chirality, expanding the known family of strain-responsive material properties. Its potential applications span a broad range of advanced fields, from photonics and spintronics to biosensing and quantum information.
items.citation: Z. Zeng, M. Först, M. Fechner et al.. The piezochiral effect. Nature. 2026

items.title: Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP
items.summary: The paper investigated how mitochondrial metabolism contributes to the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), an inflammatory programme driven by senescent cells that promotes tissue dysfunction. The researchers found that an upregulated mitochondrial pyruvate–citrate–acetyl-CoA axis in senescent cells increases acetyl-CoA availability, which supports histone acetylation at SASP gene loci and is required for robust transcription of those genes, working alongside mitochondrial DNA-driven activation of inflammatory transcription factors. Inhibiting SLC25A1, the mitochondrial citrate exporter, reduced histone acetylation at SASP loci and dampened the inflammatory programme in cell-based experiments. In aged mice, SLC25A1 inhibition decreased chromatin accessibility at SASP loci, reduced inflammation, and improved healthspan. Together, these findings describe a mitochondrial metabolic checkpoint that epigenetically enables innate immune signalling output in senescent cells, identifying a mechanism through which SASP can be selectively controlled.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals a mechanistic link between mitochondrial metabolism and the epigenetic activation of inflammatory genes in senescent cells. The finding that blocking a specific mitochondrial transporter can dampen this process highlights a potential therapeutic strategy for slowing age-related decline.
items.citation: Hélène Martini, Jodie Birch, Francisco Madeira Marques et al.. Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP. Nature. 2026

items.title: Avalanche-like intercalation and intraparticle correlations in graphite
items.summary: This paper investigated the lithium intercalation dynamics in graphite, the dominant negative electrode material in lithium-ion batteries, focusing on the poorly understood dilute staging regime where symmetry-breaking phase transitions occur. Using operando optical microscopy, the researchers directly observed that graphite particles undergo rapid, localized deintercalation–intercalation events in which micrometre-sized regions transform within seconds, rather than progressing smoothly. These events resemble "avalanches" seen in disordered materials, characterized by abrupt jumps between multiple metastable states. A modified random field Ising model was developed to link these avalanche dynamics to static structural disorder within the graphite, successfully reproducing both the apparently continuous stage transitions and the observed avalanche statistics. Spatio-temporal analysis of sequential avalanche events further revealed heterogeneous connectivity across particles, underscoring the critical role of local disorder in governing phase-transition behavior in layered battery materials.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it directly visualizes avalanche-like lithium intercalation and deintercalation events in real time, revealing how local disorder controls phase-transition dynamics and ion transport in battery electrodes—insights that could inform the design of more efficient lithium-ion batteries.
items.citation: Jiho Han, George Phillips, Alice J. Merryweather et al.. Avalanche-like intercalation and intraparticle correlations in graphite. Nature. 2026

items.title: Weight-four parity checks in a spin-shuttling architecture
items.summary: This paper investigates silicon spin-qubit devices as a platform for quantum error correction, focusing on a sparse array architecture where coherent spin shuttling provides long-range qubit connectivity. The researchers built a device featuring a shuttling bus with four interaction sites called bus stops, enabling dynamic qubit transport and interaction without relying on charge sensing across most of the device. Using shuttling and quantum non-demolition measurements, they achieved universal control over an effective five-qubit processor and configured the connectivity needed to implement surface-code stabilizer plaquettes supporting both X- and Z-type parity checks up to weight four. The parity checks were used to generate multi-qubit entanglement across all qubit combinations in the array, including a five-qubit Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger state representing one of the largest genuinely entangled states demonstrated with gate-defined semiconductor spins. The work establishes modular calibration and operational protocols for sparse spin-qubit arrays and argues for the near-term feasibility of quantum error-correction experiments using mobile spin qubits.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention because it demonstrates that incorporating a shuttling bus into a silicon spin-qubit device enables parity checks up to weight four, a key milestone for quantum error correction, while showcasing the broader feasibility of shuttling-based architectures in semiconductor quantum processors.
items.citation: Brennan Undseth, Nicola Meggiato, Yi-Hsien Wu et al.. Weight-four parity checks in a spin-shuttling architecture. Nature. 2026

items.title: Enzymatic glycosylation and amidation reshapes polyene bioactivity
items.summary: This paper investigated the biosynthetic pathways of polyene natural products, a class of antifungal compounds whose clinical utility is hampered by severe toxicity and poor aqueous solubility. The researchers discovered and characterized previously undescribed polyene biosynthetic pathways, identifying unusual glycosyltransferase enzymes capable of attaching sugars to polyene scaffolds and demonstrating that an amidotransferase enzyme could be repurposed to convert the problematic carboxylate group of polyenes into alternative chemical functionalities. By combining the introduction of a second sugar with carboxylate modifications, the team generated new polyene variants with enhanced antifungal potency and reduced toxicity. Crucially, these improved compounds are accessible through fermentation or enzymatic synthesis rather than the costly and inefficient total chemical synthesis routes previously required. The findings suggest that enzymatic tailoring of polyene scaffolds offers a cleaner and more practical route to next-generation antifungal therapeutics.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it uncovers new biosynthetic pathways and unusual enzymes that modify polyene scaffolds with additional sugars, yielding previously undescribed compounds with improved potential as safe and effective antifungal treatments producible through clean, efficient fermentation.
items.citation: Saadia N. Mirza, Alberto Carella, Joseph W. Thompson et al.. Enzymatic glycosylation and amidation reshapes polyene bioactivity. Nature. 2026

items.title: A digitally controlled silicon quantum processing unit
items.summary: This paper introduces a quantum processing unit built from silicon exchange-only qubits, designed with commercial scalability in mind. The system integrates a custom cryogenic CMOS controller, a high-density superconducting ribbon cable, and a low-noise qubit device featuring an array of exchange-coupled quantum dots configurable to host up to eighteen exchange-only qubits. By combining these components, the researchers demonstrated single-qubit and entangling gate performance that improves on the previous exchange-only state of the art by an order of magnitude. To validate the system, they implemented both a distance-five repetition code and a distance-two quantum error-detecting code, comparing experimental results against simulations. The work argues that this integrated approach, leveraging compatibility with advanced semiconductor manufacturing and simplified control signals, provides a viable pathway toward utility-scale quantum computing with manageable hardware and operational requirements.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it demonstrates a silicon quantum processing unit capable of high-fidelity multiqubit circuits in which all control signals are generated by an integrated cryogenic digital controller — a significant step toward scalable, fully integrated quantum hardware. The combination of digitally programmable cryogenic control electronics with a low-noise qubit device connected via a high-density superconducting cable addresses key engineering challenges in scaling up silicon-based quantum systems.
authors: Members of the HRL Quantum Team and Collaborators
items.citation: Members of the HRL Quantum Team and Collaborators, Michaël Abraham, Edwin Acuna et al.. A digitally controlled silicon quantum processing unit. Nature. 2026

items.title: A global view of human centromere variation and evolution
items.summary: This paper investigated the sequence diversity, population variation, and evolutionary dynamics of human centromeres, regions essential for chromosome segregation that have been difficult to study due to their highly repetitive nature. The researchers assembled thousands of complete human centromeres from a large, diverse cohort spanning multiple continental and population groups, and developed new bioinformatic tools specifically designed for centromeric sequence analysis. They discovered extensive previously unknown variation, including novel centromere haplotypes, new alpha-satellite higher-order repeat variants, mobile element insertions in a substantial fraction of centromeres, and a notable prevalence of di- and tri-kinetochore configurations. Comparative analysis revealed dramatic variation in mutation rates across chromosomes, evidence of archaic hominin introgression shaping some centromeres, and a finding that the kinetochore site itself is the most rapidly mutating region within the centromere. Based on these findings, the authors propose a model of an evolutionary arms race between centromeric sequence and the proteins that bind it, driving rapid and ongoing evolution of these genomic regions.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it provides the first comprehensive, fully sequenced view of centromere diversity across a large, globally diverse human cohort, uncovering structural features and unusually high mutation rates that illuminate how these essential chromosomal regions evolve.
items.citation: Shenghan Gao, Keisuke K. Oshima, Shu-Cheng Chuang et al.. A global view of human centromere variation and evolution. Nature. 2026

items.title: In situ structure of the poxvirus portal complex
items.summary: This paper investigated the structure of the portal complex in poxviruses, which are large double-stranded DNA viruses responsible for diseases including smallpox and mpox. Using cryo-electron tomography combined with subtomogram averaging and computational structure prediction, the researchers determined the molecular architecture and protein composition of this pore-like structure that spans the poxvirus core wall in vaccinia virus. They found that the portal complex is a hexameric assembly comprising three conserved poxviral proteins arranged in distinct layers, with one protein forming the central chamber, a second hexamer decorating the exterior, and a third binding as a hexamer of dimers on the interior side. Additionally, the viral helicase required for genome release was shown to associate with the portal complex by docking onto its exterior rim during infection, providing mechanistic insight into how the virus releases its genetic material and messenger RNA into host cells. The authors propose that this structurally defined portal complex represents a promising target for the development of antiviral therapeutics against poxviruses.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals the atomic-level architecture of a previously uncharacterized portal complex in vaccinia virus, captured in its native context using cryo-electron tomography. The findings illuminate how this conserved hexameric structure physically connects to core viral processes—including genome packaging, messenger RNA release, and uncoating—offering fundamental new insight into poxvirus biology.
items.citation: Thomas Calcraft, Miguel Hernández‐González, Michael Way et al.. In situ structure of the poxvirus portal complex. Nature. 2026

items.title: In situ structures of plant photosystem supercomplexes
items.summary: This study investigated the native structural organization of plant photosystems within intact chloroplast membranes, which had previously been unknown despite the availability of structures from isolated, purified components. Using in situ cryo-electron microscopy, the researchers directly imaged rice chloroplasts and determined the structures of photosystem supercomplexes in their natural membrane environment. They resolved a large PSII–LHCII supercomplex containing additional antenna trimers not seen in purified preparations, and excitation energy transfer calculations based on this native architecture closely matched in vivo measurements, supporting its physiological relevance. They also identified multiple asymmetric PSII–LHCII dimer configurations and higher-order assemblies, leading to the proposal that PSII forms a structural skeleton that shapes thylakoid membrane morphology and drives grana stacking. High-resolution structures of PSI-containing supercomplexes were additionally obtained, collectively providing the first molecular framework for understanding how native photosystem architecture achieves the remarkable efficiency of photosynthetic light-to-electron conversion.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it captures the plant photosystem supercomplex structure directly within its native membrane, preserving proteins and lipids that are typically lost during conventional purification—offering an unprecedentedly complete view of the intact photosynthetic architecture.
items.citation: Jiao Li, Eduard Elias, Kai Zhang et al.. In situ structures of plant photosystem supercomplexes. Nature. 2026

items.title: Over 20,000 precolonial earthworks in the Southwest Amazonia
items.summary: Using canopy-penetrating LiDAR technology flown over thousands of kilometers of flight in southwestern Amazonia, researchers investigated the true geographical extent and quantity of precolonial geometric earthworks that had previously been detectable only in deforested areas. The study combined existing earthwork data with new LiDAR documentation to overcome the longstanding limitation that forest cover concealed most of these structures from conventional detection methods. The findings reveal that the cultural area studied alone contains as many earthworks as had previously been estimated for all of Amazonia combined, suggesting the scale of monument-building civilization there was vastly underestimated. The researchers further propose that the total human population of this region during an early period of the first millennium was in the range of several million people. They conclude that if comparable results emerge from other parts of Amazonia, prevailing estimates of precolonial population density and its lasting influence on Amazonian soils, forest structure, biodiversity, and global climate models will need substantial revision.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because LiDAR technology has revealed a dramatically higher number of precolonial earthworks than previously thought, with one region alone containing as many such structures as had been estimated for the entire Amazon basin. The findings substantially revise the understood scale of ancient human landscape modification in Amazonia.
items.citation: Martti Pärssinen, Risto Kalliola, Alceu Ranzi et al.. Over 20,000 precolonial earthworks in the Southwest Amazonia. Nature. 2026

items.title: Miniaturizing and modifying natural proteins with Raygun
items.summary: Raygun is a generative artificial intelligence framework designed to miniaturize, modify, and augment natural proteins in ways that mimic the large-scale coordinated sequence changes seen in natural protein evolution. The core conceptual innovation is encoding each protein as a probability distribution in a fixed-dimensional space derived from protein language model embeddings, rather than as a variable-length sequence, making proteins of any length directly comparable and manipulable. Controlled by just two parameters governing substitutions and length changes, the framework can shrink or expand proteins while preserving predicted structural integrity and functional sites. In experimental validation, the approach successfully miniaturized fluorescent proteins and TurboID, a synthetic biotin ligase used in proteomics, and generated epidermal growth factor variants with enhanced receptor-binding affinity compared to the wild type. These results demonstrate that protein function can be faithfully captured in a length-agnostic representation, enabling computational access to the kinds of evolutionary sequence transformations that have previously been beyond the reach of protein design methods.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it introduces an AI-driven approach that can shrink and redesign natural proteins while preserving their original structure and function, opening new possibilities for engineering biological molecules.
items.citation: Kapil Devkota, Daichi Shonai, Yiwei Mao et al.. Miniaturizing and modifying natural proteins with Raygun. Nature. 2026

items.title: Cretaceous zhelestid mammals are zalambdalestoids
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it overturns a long-standing interpretation of zhelestid mammals, using new fossil evidence to reposition them away from placental mammal relatives and instead within a different ancient group. The finding fundamentally reshapes understanding of early placental mammal evolution and the origins of herbivory among Cretaceous mammals.
items.citation: Andres Giallombardo, Eva Hoffman, Maureen A. O’Leary et al.. Cretaceous zhelestid mammals are zalambdalestoids. Nature. 2026

items.title: Intestinal stem cells count self-renewal divisions to switch multipotency
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it reveals that intestinal stem cells actively count their own self-renewal divisions—rather than responding to random or external signals—to time a precise switch in cell fate, specifically transitioning from one cell type to another at a defined division number. The identification of an epigenetic counting mechanism underlying this switch offers a fundamentally new understanding of how multipotency is regulated in adult stem cells.
items.citation: Tong Dong, Anqi Li, Quanquan Jiang et al.. Intestinal stem cells count self-renewal divisions to switch multipotency. Nature. 2026

items.title: The past and future impact of climate change on childhood malaria in Africa
items.summary: This study investigated whether human-caused climate change has altered the burden of childhood malaria across sub-Saharan Africa, addressing a longstanding scientific debate about climate change and disease. The researchers analyzed the relationships between temperature, extreme precipitation, and malaria prevalence, and modeled both historical impacts and future projections under varying greenhouse gas emission scenarios. They found that while rising temperatures have likely increased malaria in East and southern Africa, this has been offset by a reduction in cases in West Africa, resulting in a negligible net continental impact to date. Looking ahead, climate change is projected to marginally accelerate malaria elimination in the highest-burden regions of West and central Africa, though high-elevation areas of East and southern Africa face meaningful increases in cases under higher warming scenarios. The study concludes that limiting future warming could prevent a notable number of excess malaria cases in vulnerable regions by the end of the century, while providing a methodological framework for quantifying the true global health burden of climate change.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it uses climate and econometric modelling to show that human-induced climate change is already reshaping where and how severely childhood malaria burdens fall across Africa, with implications for how that burden may shift in the future.
items.citation: Colin J. Carlson, Tamma Carleton, Romaric C. Odoulami et al.. The past and future impact of climate change on childhood malaria in Africa. Nature. 2026

items.title: How silicon-chip technology is being re-engineered for quantum computing
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it shows how established silicon-chip fabrication technology is being adapted to build quantum processors, with two separate demonstrations addressing the key engineering hurdles that stand in the way of scaling quantum computers up to practical sizes.
items.citation: Natalia Ares. How silicon-chip technology is being re-engineered for quantum computing. Nature. 2026

items.title: Quantum meets capitalism: how to pair long-term bets on technology with commercial speed
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it addresses the fundamental tension between quantum computing's need for long-term, high-risk investment and the short-term pressures of commercial markets, arguing that a hybrid of public and private support is essential to bring the technology to fruition.
items.citation: Charles Tahan. Quantum meets capitalism: how to pair long-term bets on technology with commercial speed. Nature. 2026

items.title: Papers with open peer-review reports are less likely to be retracted
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it suggests a link between open peer-review practices and lower retraction rates, implying that transparency in publishing may serve as an indicator of research quality. However, the researchers caution that further evidence is needed before drawing firm conclusions.
items.citation: Dalmeet Singh Chawla. Papers with open peer-review reports are less likely to be retracted. Nature. 2026

items.title: A guide to the Nature Index
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it explains the terminology, methodology, and online tools behind a major research-tracking resource, helping users understand and navigate the data it provides.
items.citation: A guide to the Nature Index. Nature. 2026

items.title: Polio will come roaring back if the task of eradicating it isn’t finished soon
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it warns that polio eradication is tantalizingly close yet at serious risk of reversal if global commitment falters. The framing underscores that the window to finish the job is urgent, making the stakes for public-health prioritization especially high.
items.citation: Polio will come roaring back if the task of eradicating it isn’t finished soon. Nature. 2026

items.title: The past is an open can of worms: a stimulated-memory exhibition
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention for its exploration of recovered or stimulated memories, framed as a kind of exhibition that opens up hidden or forgotten dimensions of the past. The evocative framing suggests it reveals something surprising or unsettling about how the past can be "reopened."
items.citation: Priya Chand. The past is an open can of worms: a stimulated-memory exhibition. Nature. 2026

items.title: Electric dipoles go sideways in thin ferroelectric film
items.why_notable: The work is attracting attention because it reveals that coupling between horizontal and vertical electric polarization in a thin ferroelectric film allows an unconventional ferroelectric material to be controlled using standard device geometry, potentially opening a practical path to incorporating such materials into existing technologies.
items.citation: Elzbieta Gradauskaite. Electric dipoles go sideways in thin ferroelectric film. Nature. 2026

items.title: Can long COVID be prevented? Two drugs finally show promise
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because, after years of uncertainty, rigorous clinical trials have finally identified drugs that can reduce the risk of developing long COVID following coronavirus infection. The findings represent a meaningful step toward preventing a condition that has affected many people long-term.
items.citation: Edward Chen. Can long COVID be prevented? Two drugs finally show promise. Nature. 2026

items.title: Three rising stars of nanoscience and nanotechnology
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it highlights emerging leaders whose research harnesses nanoscale building blocks to develop next-generation technological solutions.
items.citation: Anna Napolitano, Holly Else, Sandy Ong. Three rising stars of nanoscience and nanotechnology. Nature. 2026

items.title: Daily briefing: Ice-age art hints at how humans flourished
items.why_notable: The discovery of tiny bird figurines is drawing attention because they suggest Europe's earliest *Homo sapiens* possessed a level of sophistication previously underappreciated, offering new insight into how humans thrived during the ice age.
items.citation: Flora Graham. Daily briefing: Ice-age art hints at how humans flourished. Nature. 2026

items.title: How fruit flies track the edge of odour plumes
items.summary: This paper examined how fruit flies navigate toward the source of an odor plume. Using virtual-reality experiments with fictive odor plumes, the researchers investigated the neural and behavioral mechanisms underlying plume tracking in *Drosophila*. They found that fruit flies use a memory-guided navigational strategy similar to that used by ants and bees for locating fixed destinations, with neurons in the fly's brain encoding a spatial memory that directs the insect back toward the edge of the plume when it strays from it.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals that fruit flies employ memory-guided navigational strategies—previously associated with nest-finding in ants and bees—to track odour plumes, suggesting a broader shared toolkit for insect navigation than was previously recognized.
items.citation: How fruit flies track the edge of odour plumes. Nature. 2026

items.title: This AI Raygun can shrink and supersize proteins — opening the door to easy editing
items.why_notable: The work is attracting attention because it introduces an AI tool capable of both shrinking and enlarging proteins, using a probability-based approach that could make protein editing considerably more accessible and flexible.
items.citation: Gemma Conroy. This AI Raygun can shrink and supersize proteins — opening the door to easy editing. Nature. 2026

items.title: Intestinal stem cells count to eight divisions to maintain cell ratios
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals that intestinal stem cells use a precise division-counting mechanism — specifically alternating between runs of divisions producing one cell type and a single division producing another — to maintain the correct ratio of cell types in the gut.
items.citation: Joaquín de Navascués. Intestinal stem cells count to eight divisions to maintain cell ratios. Nature. 2026

items.title: How mosquitoes are conquering the world — in four charts
items.why_notable: Climate change and other human influences are enabling mosquitoes to spread into new regions, driving record-breaking outbreaks of mosquito-borne diseases worldwide.
items.citation: Mariana Lenharo. How mosquitoes are conquering the world — in four charts. Nature. 2026

items.title: To help children with rare diseases, we must solve drug delivery
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because nanoparticle-based delivery technologies could open up gene therapy options for children suffering from rare diseases that currently have few treatments available.
items.citation: Shadi Farhangrazi, S. Moein Moghimi. To help children with rare diseases, we must solve drug delivery. Nature. 2026

items.title: The first known cephalopod was only a millimetre long and lived about 520 million years ago
items.summary: The paper investigated the evolutionary origins of cephalopods, the group of molluscs that includes modern squid and cuttlefish, which rely on a buoyancy-controlling structure called a siphuncle for locomotion. Researchers examined small shelly fossils belonging to a genus called Eoceras, which preserve a distinct siphuncle structure. The fossils indicate that this organism was only about a millimetre in size and lived during the early Cambrian period, pushing back the known origins of cephalopods by a significant margin. This discovery suggests that the cephalopod body plan, including the defining siphuncle, had already evolved roughly half a billion years ago.
items.why_notable: The discovery is drawing attention because newly found fossils push back the origin of cephalopods into the early Cambrian, revealing that the defining buoyancy-control structure central to the group's locomotion had already evolved in a tiny, millimetre-scale ancestor some 520 million years ago.
items.citation: The first known cephalopod was only a millimetre long and lived about 520 million years ago. Nature. 2026

items.title: Amazonian earthwork survey indicates ancient population was much larger than thought
items.summary: Using aerial laser-scanning technology, this study surveyed a small fraction of the Greater Amazonia region to investigate the scale of ancient human occupation and landscape modification. The researchers identified more than twenty thousand human-made earthworks dating to a period spanning roughly the second and third centuries, attributing them to what they term the Aquiry civilization. These findings suggest that this single region alone supported a population far larger than previously estimated for pre-colonial Amazonia, prompting a fundamental reassessment of how densely inhabited and socially complex ancient Amazonian societies were. The study further implies that these large populations would have had substantial and lasting effects on the composition and character of present-day tropical soils and forests across the broader region.
items.why_notable: The work is attracting attention because aerial laser-scanning has revealed a far denser concentration of ancient earthworks and people in a small fraction of Amazonia than previously recognized, suggesting the region's pre-colonial populations have been substantially underestimated. This challenges long-held assumptions about early Amazonian civilizations and their lasting ecological influence on tropical soils and forests.
items.citation: Amazonian earthwork survey indicates ancient population was much larger than thought. Nature. 2026

items.title: Relatively few Black people benefited in the 1930s and 1940s from mortgages backed by the US government
items.summary: The paper examined the racial distribution of federally backed mortgage loans administered through two major government programmes during the mid-twentieth century, a period credited with shaping the American ideal of homeownership. Using newly digitized mortgage records across a large number of states, the researchers quantified who actually received these loans. They found that Black households were systematically and severely underrepresented among recipients, while immigrants — predominantly European at the time — received mortgages in proportion to their population share. The findings provide empirical documentation of the structural exclusion of Black Americans from wealth-building opportunities that were made broadly available to other groups, contributing to lasting racial disparities in homeownership and accumulated wealth.
items.why_notable: Newly digitized mortgage records have allowed researchers to quantify how thoroughly Black households were shut out of landmark federal mortgage programmes that shaped American home ownership culture, while immigrants received loans at rates proportional to their population. The findings reveal the deep racial inequity baked into the policies that built modern American middle-class wealth.
items.citation: Relatively few Black people benefited in the 1930s and 1940s from mortgages backed by the US government. Nature. 2026

items.title: Artificial algal blooms could remove atmospheric carbon — but can they be used responsibly?
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it explores a potentially powerful but double-edged climate intervention—deliberately triggering algal blooms to capture atmospheric carbon—while raising serious concerns that the ecological side effects could spread well beyond the area where the technique is applied.
items.citation: Sara Nawaz. Artificial algal blooms could remove atmospheric carbon — but can they be used responsibly?. Nature. 2026

items.title: Relapsed childhood cancers show genomic scars left by previous therapy
items.summary: Researchers used whole-genome sequencing of a large collection of childhood tumors, with a focus on pretreated, relapsed, and metastatic cases, to investigate how prior cancer therapies shape the genomic landscape of tumors. They identified distinctive mutational signatures representing patterns of DNA damage that accumulate as a direct consequence of treatment, particularly platinum-based chemotherapy. These genomic "scars" were acquired rapidly and were more pronounced following platinum-based regimens than other therapeutic approaches. The mutational signatures associated with prior treatment were linked to worse patient outcomes, suggesting they reflect therapy-driven tumor evolution. The findings indicate that these signatures could serve as biomarkers to detect relapse and inform subsequent treatment decisions in children with cancer.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals that cancer therapies—particularly platinum-based treatments—leave distinctive patterns of DNA damage in childhood tumours that are tied to worse outcomes. These mutational signatures could have practical clinical value by helping track disease relapse and inform future treatment decisions.
items.citation: Relapsed childhood cancers show genomic scars left by previous therapy. Nature. 2026

items.title: Underdog ‘spin qubits’ leap forward in race to a useful quantum computer
items.why_notable: Spin qubits, long considered underdogs in quantum computing, are gaining newfound credibility as four independent teams simultaneously report significant advances, including reduced error rates, that could accelerate their path to practical quantum computers.
items.citation: Dan Garisto. Underdog ‘spin qubits’ leap forward in race to a useful quantum computer. Nature. 2026

items.title: Early Detection and Surveillance of the SARS-CoV-2 Variant BA.3.2 — Worldwide, November 2024–February 2026
items.summary: The paper examined the emergence and early spread of a novel SARS-CoV-2 variant, BA.3.2, tracking its global and domestic detection from its initial identification in South Africa through early 2026. Researchers employed a multimodal genomic surveillance strategy incorporating traveler-based sampling, clinical specimens, airplane wastewater, and community wastewater monitoring across multiple U.S. states and international reporting networks. BA.3.2 carries a substantial number of substitutions and deletions in the spike protein relative to the antigens used in current vaccines, raising concern that these mutations may reduce protection conferred by prior infection or vaccination. Surveillance detected the variant in travelers, clinical patients, and wastewater samples spanning dozens of U.S. states, with detections reported by more than twenty countries globally. The authors conclude that continued genomic surveillance is essential to monitor the variant's evolution and assess its potential public health impact.
items.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
items.citation: Mila Shakya, Kevin C. Ma, Laura J. Hughes et al.. Early Detection and Surveillance of the SARS-CoV-2 Variant BA.3.2 — Worldwide, November 2024–February 2026. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2026

items.title: Wastewater Metagenomics for Antimicrobial Resistance and Pathogen Surveillance: A Bibliometric Analysis.
items.summary: This paper examined the global research landscape at the intersection of wastewater metagenomics, antimicrobial resistance, and pathogen surveillance using bibliometric methods. The authors retrieved over a thousand publications from a major scientific database and applied network analysis software to map publication trends, international collaborations, keyword evolution, and citation patterns from 2010 to 2025. They found that the field expanded dramatically, with the large majority of total output concentrated in the most recent years, likely accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic and growing adoption of the One Health framework. While certain countries led in publication volume, integration between environmental monitoring literature and public health literature remained limited, indicating that translating metagenomic surveillance data into health risk assessment is still nascent. The study concludes by identifying key priorities for the field, including standardizing methods, incorporating artificial intelligence for resistome analysis, improving geographic equity in research participation, and operationalizing One Health surveillance frameworks.
items.citation: Zheng Y, Ma N, Zhao B et al.. Wastewater Metagenomics for Antimicrobial Resistance and Pathogen Surveillance: A Bibliometric Analysis.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Validation of molecular detection of <i>Candida auris</i> from wastewater.
items.summary: This study investigated whether an existing quantitative PCR assay developed for clinical *Candida auris* colonization screening could be adapted to detect the pathogen in wastewater, given its classification as an urgent public health threat due to multidrug resistance and high transmissibility in healthcare settings. The researchers validated the qPCR workflow using a wastewater matrix, evaluating amplification efficiency, sensitivity, and reproducibility. The assay demonstrated high amplification efficiency, a very low limit of detection, and strong reproducibility across tests. These findings indicate that the clinical colonization assay can be reliably repurposed for wastewater surveillance, offering a more cost-effective approach to monitoring *C. auris* prevalence across entire healthcare systems without relying solely on direct patient screening.
items.citation: Rodríguez Stewart RM, Litvintseva AP, Chavez J et al.. Validation of molecular detection of <i>Candida auris</i> from wastewater.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: A Systematic Review of Gastrointestinal and Respiratory Pathogen Detection in Wastewater in Africa, with Focus on Rwanda: Implications for Early Warning and Public Health Surveillance.
items.summary: This systematic review examined the use of wastewater-based epidemiology for detecting gastrointestinal and respiratory pathogens in Africa, with particular attention to the context of Rwanda. The authors conducted a narrative systematic review drawing on peer-reviewed literature, global health reports, and surveillance studies published over more than two decades, ultimately synthesizing findings from a substantial pool of eligible studies identified through major academic databases. The review found that wastewater-based epidemiology offers a non-invasive and cost-effective means of capturing both symptomatic and asymptomatic infections, providing population-level surveillance coverage that traditional clinical reporting systems frequently fail to achieve in low- and middle-income countries. Key challenges identified include variability in sampling methodologies, environmental factors that accelerate pathogen decay, and inconsistencies in laboratory workflows across settings. The authors conclude that integrating wastewater surveillance into existing public health infrastructure, particularly in rapidly urbanizing settings like Kigali, could meaningfully strengthen epidemic preparedness and outbreak response, provided that investment in laboratory capacity, standardized protocols, and cross-sector collaboration is sustained.
items.citation: Bambara S, Isingizwe MC, Adegboyega TT et al.. A Systematic Review of Gastrointestinal and Respiratory Pathogen Detection in Wastewater in Africa, with Focus on Rwanda: Implications for Early Warning and Public Health Surveillance.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Wastewater Surveillance for Early Warning of Infectious Disease Outbreaks: A Systematic Review of Evidence and Implications for One Health Surveillance.
items.summary: This systematic review examined the role of wastewater surveillance as an early warning tool for infectious disease outbreaks, with a focus on its implications for One Health surveillance frameworks that integrate human, animal, and environmental health. The authors searched multiple major databases and screened hundreds of studies, ultimately synthesizing evidence from a subset that met their inclusion criteria. They found that pathogens detected in wastewater—predominantly those associated with respiratory and gastrointestinal infections—correlated positively with clinical case counts in communities, and that pathogen circulation displayed season-specific patterns. Importantly, the frequency and duration of sampling in socially vulnerable areas showed particular utility for early outbreak warning. The review concluded that while wastewater surveillance holds strong promise as a complementary epidemiological tool, standardization of methods remains lacking and explicit integration of One Health frameworks across human, animal, and environmental surveillance systems is needed in future programmes.
items.citation: Panigrahi S, Pattnaik M, Pradhan R et al.. Wastewater Surveillance for Early Warning of Infectious Disease Outbreaks: A Systematic Review of Evidence and Implications for One Health Surveillance.. Pathogens (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: Multi-Pathogen Wastewater Surveillance enables Real-Time Targeted Public Health Interventions During the 2025 African Nations Championship Football Tournament
items.summary: This study investigated whether multi-pathogen wastewater-based surveillance could serve as a practical public health tool during a major mass gathering event in a low- and middle-income country setting. During a football tournament in Uganda, researchers deployed Moore swabs across dozens of manholes at a national stadium on multiple match days, concentrating and analyzing collected wastewater samples for a broad panel of enteric and respiratory pathogens using quantitative PCR. The vast majority of samples tested positive for at least one pathogen, with enteric pathogens such as Shigella, Rotavirus A, and Enterovirus detected most frequently, while mpox virus was also detected in a substantial proportion of samples and respiratory pathogens including SARS-CoV-2 and Influenza B appeared at lower frequencies. Surveillance results directly informed real-time public health responses including enhanced sanitation, hygiene promotion, environmental disinfection, and strengthened on-site syndromic surveillance. The authors conclude that integrating multi-pathogen wastewater surveillance into mass-gathering preparedness frameworks is operationally feasible in low-resource settings and can provide actionable population-level intelligence to support outbreak detection and response.
items.citation: Nsawotebba A, Morunyanga I, Nakintu V et al.. Multi-Pathogen Wastewater Surveillance enables Real-Time Targeted Public Health Interventions During the 2025 African Nations Championship Football Tournament. 2026

items.title: Revealing the hidden burden: wastewater-based epidemiology for underreported and emerging infectious diseases in communities.
items.summary: Wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as a powerful surveillance approach that captures population-level infectious disease signals beyond what traditional clinical reporting systems detect. This review examines how wastewater analysis identifies underreported, novel, and emerging pathogens—including enteric, respiratory, and neglected agents—that are frequently missed by healthcare systems, thereby revealing the true community burden of infection. Sequencing-based studies have uncovered extensive diversity within the human virome and show that multiple viral taxa are often co-detected, suggesting that co-infections may shape viral evolution and disease dynamics. Despite challenges in quantification and biological validation, wastewater surveillance has demonstrated the ability to detect both known and novel pathogens before they are clinically recognized. The review concludes that advances in long-read sequencing, bioinformatics, and global data integration will strengthen wastewater genomics as a cornerstone of early-warning and One Health surveillance frameworks.
items.citation: Greaves JC, Rodriguez RA. Revealing the hidden burden: wastewater-based epidemiology for underreported and emerging infectious diseases in communities.. Environmental monitoring and assessment. 2026

items.title: Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating the transmission rates of different SARS-CoV-2 variants circulating simultaneously during the pandemic. The authors developed a statistical framework that jointly analyzes confirmed case counts and genetic sequencing data to infer variant-specific effective reproduction numbers, going beyond approaches that rely on sequence frequency data alone. By applying this method to data from US states spanning early 2021 through early 2022, they were able to estimate both how transmissible each variant was over time and how its prevalence changed relative to co-circulating variants. The model also allows structured relationships between reproduction numbers to be captured, enabling estimation of fixed growth advantages that particular variants maintain consistently across different geographic locations. This approach provides a richer epidemiological picture of variant dynamics than frequency-based methods and was used to characterize the transmission properties of multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and interest in the United States.
items.citation: Marlin D Figgins, Trevor Bedford. Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data. eLife. 2026

items.title: Bacterial defense mechanisms against bacteriophages: an evolutionary arms race
items.summary: This review examines the co-evolutionary arms race between bacteria and bacteriophages, focusing on the diverse mechanisms bacteria employ to resist phage infection at every stage of the infection cycle. The authors systematically surveyed surface-based defenses such as receptor modification, capsule production, and biofilm formation, as well as intracellular strategies including restriction-modification systems, abortive infection, and CRISPR-Cas adaptive immunity. Phages in turn counter these defenses through mechanisms such as anti-CRISPR proteins, receptor mimicry, and enzymatic degradation of capsules and biofilms. The review integrates current knowledge on these reciprocal evolutionary adaptations to illustrate how bacterial-phage dynamics shape microbial ecosystems. The authors conclude that understanding these interactions has practical implications for developing engineered phages and combination therapies to combat multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.
items.citation: Rafwana Ibrahim, Jesil Mathew Aranjani. Bacterial defense mechanisms against bacteriophages: an evolutionary arms race. Archives of Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Microbial engineering for pesticide degradation: current insights and future directions for sustainable agriculture
items.summary: This review examines the problem of pesticide contamination in agricultural soils and evaluates microbial-based strategies for remediation. The authors synthesize current knowledge on how pesticides affect crop physiology and metabolism, then survey both conventional and advanced microbe-mediated degradation approaches, including enzymatic pathways and the use of microbial consortia. A particular focus is placed on microbiome engineering techniques, such as targeted manipulation of microbial communities and genetic modification, as well as the combination of plant growth-promoting microorganisms with engineered microbes to simultaneously enhance pesticide breakdown and crop productivity. The review finds that microbial consortia and engineered strains can achieve substantial degradation of highly recalcitrant compounds, with synergistic microbial interactions and recombinant genome strategies demonstrating notable improvements over single-organism approaches. The authors conclude that integrative microbial engineering strategies represent a sustainable and ecologically sound pathway toward resilient agroecosystems, and they highlight emerging technologies, environmental and economic benefits, and recent patentable innovations in this field.
items.citation: S. Sangeeta Srivastava Srivastava, Rakeeb Ahmad Mir, Sofi Javed Hussain et al.. Microbial engineering for pesticide degradation: current insights and future directions for sustainable agriculture. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Evaluation of antimicrobial resistance governance across 193 countries to inform the 2026 Global Action Plan update
items.summary: This paper evaluated the effectiveness of national action plans and AMR governance systems across all United Nations member states over a multi-year period using a newly developed One Health governance index. The researchers constructed this index through expert consultation, integrating hundreds of policy documents, weighted indicators, and multinational surveillance datasets, then applied econometric methods to link governance quality to antimicrobial use, resistance prevalence, and AMR-related mortality. They found that while governance scores improved substantially over the study period, implementation and monitoring consistently lagged behind policy design, especially in animal and environmental sectors. Critically, meaningful reductions in AMR prevalence were only detectable approximately five years after countries adopted national action plans, highlighting a substantial delay between policy adoption and measurable impact. The findings emphasize that multisector engagement and robust antimicrobial use surveillance are the governance features most strongly associated with improved outcomes, and that sustained financing and integrated environmental and agricultural surveillance will be essential for the forthcoming update to the Global Action Plan.
items.citation: Weiye Chen, Yige Zeng, Jinxin Zheng et al.. Evaluation of antimicrobial resistance governance across 193 countries to inform the 2026 Global Action Plan update. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Climate change and antimicrobial resistance
items.citation: Erta Kalanxhi, Ramanan Laxminarayan. Climate change and antimicrobial resistance. Nature Reviews Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field
items.summary: This paper investigates the production of dark photons as a dark matter candidate through the perturbative decay of a dark Higgs field that is displaced from the minimum of its potential during inflation, a mechanism known as stochastic misalignment. The authors analyze the constraints on this scenario arising from structure formation, since the produced dark photons are initially relativistic, and from inflationary isocurvature fluctuations, which require the quartic self-coupling of the dark Higgs to be small. They identify a viable parameter space of dark photon masses and gauge couplings consistent with the observed dark matter relic abundance, and show that this region becomes more tightly constrained when kinetic mixing between the dark photon and the Standard Model photon is included. The favored parameter space could be probed by future cosmic microwave background or Lyman-alpha forest observations, and, if kinetic mixing is present, by direct detection experiments or diffuse soft gamma-ray searches.
items.citation: James M. Cline, Gonzalo Herrera, Jean-Samuel Roux. Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
items.summary: This paper studies the computational complexity of planted noisy k-XOR detection and recovery, as well as strong refutation of random k-XOR, problems that are central to understanding average-case hardness in combinatorics and cryptography. The conjectured optimal trade-off between the number of clauses, signal strength, and runtime is captured by a smooth curve parameterized by the level of the Kikuchi hierarchy, but all prior spectral analyses incurred polylogarithmic losses that degraded the running time exponent. The authors introduce a normalized variant of the Kikuchi hierarchy and prove it achieves the sharp conjectured trade-off at every arity without any logarithmic loss, establishing strong detection, weak and exact recovery, and strong refutation with sum-of-squares certificates. They also prove matching lower bounds in the same model, extend the results to more general planting laws and predicates, and provide a quantum algorithm achieving a quartic speedup over classical spectral methods for detection and weak recovery. The key technical contributions are a careful normalization of the sparse Kikuchi matrix and a sharp enumeration of closed walks in its trace expansion, which also resolves a longstanding hypergraph Moore bound conjecture.
items.citation: Alexander Schmidhuber, Matthew B. Hastings. The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of fragmented knowledge representation in fault detection and diagnosis for HVAC systems, where heterogeneous data sources and varied diagnostic outputs have hindered interoperability and broader adoption of FDD technologies. The authors developed FDD-ON, a modular and extensible ontology designed to formally represent variable air volume HVAC system components, fault types, symptom statuses, fault impacts, and their interrelationships through a well-defined controlled vocabulary. The ontology explicitly encodes contributing cause–fault–symptom–impact relationships, enabling machine-interpretable querying of diagnostic knowledge and the mapping of diverse FDD outputs to a common semantic framework. FDD-ON was evaluated using publicly available datasets and demonstrated through practical FDD development applications, showing its utility for digital twin-enabled and artificial intelligence-driven maintenance systems. The authors conclude that FDD-ON provides a foundational semantic infrastructure for scalable, transparent, and interoperable fault detection and diagnosis solutions across a range of building system applications.
items.citation: Yimin Chen, Brian Fricke, Bo Shen et al.. Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Sgoldstino Phenomenology at SND@HL-LHC
items.summary: This paper investigates the phenomenology of light scalar sgoldstinos, hypothetical particles arising from supersymmetry breaking, across a mass range from the dimuon threshold up to a few GeV. The study examines their production through meson decays and their detection prospects at the proposed SND@HL-LHC experiment, while also reviewing existing experimental constraints on the relevant parameter space. The authors analyze the kinematics of muon-antimuon pairs produced by sgoldstino decays within the detector volume, paying particular attention to the physical separation between the two tracks. For two representative choices of supersymmetry-breaking parameters, sensitivity estimates are derived, and the results demonstrate that the efficiency of resolving the muon-antimuon pair must be properly accounted for when designing searches for this dimuon signal.
items.citation: D. Kalashnikov, E. K. Karkaryan. Sgoldstino Phenomenology at SND@HL-LHC. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CodeShrink: Adaptive Visual Compression for Efficient Multimodal Code Understanding
items.summary: This paper investigates the efficiency of representing source code as rendered images for input to multimodal large language models, identifying that naive resolution scaling wastes tokens on blank whitespace and task-irrelevant code regions while relying on fixed compression ratios that cannot adapt to varying inputs. The authors developed CodeShrink, a framework combining three components: a compact rendering strategy that replaces whitespace-heavy layouts with structural markers, a reinforcement learning-trained agent that selects an appropriate compression configuration per input, and an instruction-aware mechanism that prunes visual tokens unrelated to the current task during inference. The framework was evaluated on code question answering, clone detection, and code completion benchmarks. CodeShrink achieved substantial reductions in visual token usage while matching or surpassing uncompressed text-only inputs and outperforming both text-based and visual compression baselines across all evaluated tasks. The results demonstrate that jointly addressing layout inefficiency, adaptive configuration, and instruction-aware token selection can substantially improve the efficiency of multimodal code understanding.
items.citation: Wenxin Tang, Jingyu Xiao, Zhenyu Liu et al.. CodeShrink: Adaptive Visual Compression for Efficient Multimodal Code Understanding. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Unwithered Majorana fermions in the bulk of a quantum chain
items.summary: The paper investigates Majorana fermion modes in a quantum spin chain by tuning system parameters to disorder lines, which are special parametric curves where the ground state becomes disentangled and certain correlation functions lose their dependence on spatial separation. Using the XY spin chain in a transverse field, equivalently described as a Kitaev chain in the Majorana representation, exact analytical results are derived for the behavior of Majorana modes under these conditions. Single Majorana modes are found to remain localized near the chain ends, consistent with behavior away from disorder lines, but multi-particle Majorana modes involving two or more particles are shown to penetrate into the bulk without any attenuation. This distinction between edge-localized and bulk-penetrating modes constitutes a novel bulk-edge effect arising specifically at the disentangled ground state. The authors propose that these effects could be experimentally observed in specially engineered optical chains and lattices.
items.citation: Gennady Y. Chitov. Unwithered Majorana fermions in the bulk of a quantum chain. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The paper developed and evaluated a loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of *Schistosoma mansoni* for detecting the parasite in its intermediate snail hosts. The assay was optimized under simple isothermal conditions and tested against laboratory-infected *Biomphalaria* snails as well as field-collected snails from two endemic countries, with performance compared to conventional microscopy, standard PCR, and real-time PCR methods. In laboratory settings the assay achieved complete specificity and high sensitivity, outperforming microscopy and matching real-time PCR, while in field surveys it detected a higher proportion of infected snails than conventional PCR, with microscopy failing to identify any positives at all. The results demonstrate that this LAMP assay is sensitive, specific, and deployable under field conditions, making it a practical tool for routine surveillance of schistosomiasis transmission in snail populations.
items.citation: Li HM, Qin ZQ, Lv S et al.. Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.. Tropical medicine and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: You Only Look Once (YOLO) based machine learning algorithm for real-time detection of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) diagnostics.
items.summary: The paper investigated whether a machine learning approach could automate the interpretation of loop-mediated isothermal amplification diagnostic results, which are typically read by eye and therefore subject to human error. The researchers applied the YOLOv8 object detection algorithm to digital images of LAMP reaction tubes, training it to locate individual tubes and classify them as positive or negative for DNA amplification. The trained model achieved high accuracy, precision, and recall for both positive and negative classifications on a test dataset. The authors conclude that this approach is suitable for real-time LAMP diagnostics, offering a rapid, automated, and more objective alternative to visual interpretation that could reduce false-positive and false-negative results.
items.citation: Mezgebo B, Chaffee R, Castellanos LR et al.. You Only Look Once (YOLO) based machine learning algorithm for real-time detection of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) diagnostics.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.
items.summary: This paper investigated nucleic acid amplification methods that can function across a wide range of temperatures rather than requiring precise thermal conditions. The researchers developed a LAMP-based amplification approach using a *Bst* polymerase with strong strand displacement activity and broad thermostability, enabling DNA synthesis across a temperature range from approximately 39 to 75 °C. They demonstrated that amplification could be initiated at both high and low starting temperatures and sustained even under dynamic, fluctuating temperature profiles. The system was validated for detecting SARS-CoV-2 and *M. tuberculosis* genomic DNA, confirming its diagnostic utility. The authors propose this broad-temperature amplification platform as a promising tool for point-of-care and field diagnostics where strict thermal control is impractical or unavailable.
items.citation: Hamidizadeh M, Bier FF. Broad-Temperature Polymerase in Nucleic Acid Amplification-Based Diagnostics: From Thermal Precision to Dynamic Conditions.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: DISCO-LAMP: a novel discontinuous LAMP assay for isothermal antigen detection.
items.summary: This paper developed a new method for detecting proteins using isothermal amplification rather than conventional PCR-based readout. The researchers combined proximity ligation assay, in which DNA-conjugated affinity reagents ligate when brought together by binding the same target protein, with loop-mediated isothermal amplification to create an assay called DISCO-LAMP that avoids the need for temperature cycling or wash steps. A central challenge was minimizing background amplification from unligated DNA fragments while preserving efficient amplification of the ligated product, which was addressed through careful template and primer design. The optimized assay achieved femtomolar detection limits for target DNA and demonstrated successful protein detection against Shiga toxin 2 as well as both ancestral and Omicron variants of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein using an engineered ankyrin repeat protein targeting a conserved epitope. The authors conclude that DISCO-LAMP offers a versatile, wash-free platform adaptable to diverse protein targets through pairing with appropriate affinity reagents.
items.citation: Thomas BM, Simeon RA, Yan KL et al.. DISCO-LAMP: a novel discontinuous LAMP assay for isothermal antigen detection.. Sensors & diagnostics. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in isothermal amplification techniques for detection of animal diseases.
items.summary: This review examines isothermal amplification technologies as diagnostic tools for detecting pathogens in livestock and companion animals. The authors surveyed recent advances in these nucleic acid amplification methods, which operate at a constant temperature and therefore do not require the thermocycling equipment central to conventional PCR-based approaches. The review covers innovations in assay design and analytical improvements, as well as integration of these methods into portable, field-deployable platforms suited to resource-limited settings. The authors conclude that isothermal amplification offers rapid, sensitive, and user-friendly alternatives to conventional diagnostics, with particular promise for veterinary field use and disease surveillance. The review also identifies remaining challenges and outlines future directions for incorporating these technologies into routine veterinary diagnostic and integrated surveillance programs.
items.citation: Tooryan F, Enyertornye B, Choudhury FJ et al.. Recent advances in isothermal amplification techniques for detection of animal diseases.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize, as it contains only a bibliographic reference to a report with no scientific content describing the study's methods, scope, or findings.
items.citation: V. Kotov. Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package. Dokumentenrepositorium der RUB (Ruhr University Bochum). 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, namely Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes, in the context of food safety and clinical diagnostics. The authors surveyed electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, analyzing how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity and specificity in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these biosensing systems, which enables real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexed detection. The review critically addresses persistent obstacles including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, scalability limitations, and the absence of regulatory standardization, proposing mitigation approaches such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI frameworks. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-based traceability, and standardized validation pipelines as key components of next-generation food safety monitoring platforms.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, commonly known as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their applications in laboratory medicine. The authors surveyed innovations in chip design and fabrication methods, including three-dimensional printing and flexible substrates, alongside the integration of advanced biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes in real time. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the development of smart diagnostic platforms that support self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support. The review finds that these combined advances have broadened clinical utility across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, and emerging areas such as neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The authors also address persistent challenges in manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration that must be overcome before next-generation microfluidic technologies can be routinely deployed in clinical and public health settings.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Taenia solium neurocysticercosis: Its current epidemiological, diagnostic, therapeutic, and control landscapes
items.summary: Neurocysticercosis, caused by the tapeworm *Taenia solium*, is the most prevalent helminthic infection of the human central nervous system and presents with highly variable clinical manifestations. This review examines the current state of knowledge regarding the disease's epidemiology, diagnosis, treatment, and control, noting its relevance not only in endemic regions but also in immigrant populations within industrialized nations. Over the past decade, advances have emerged across multiple fronts, including combination antiparasitic therapies, improved strategies to manage treatment-associated inflammation, novel surgical approaches, and more sensitive and specific diagnostic tools such as refined antigen and antibody detection methods and improved magnetic resonance imaging sequences. Despite these advances, significant diagnostic challenges remain and treatment strategies continue to vary depending on disease type, complicating clinical decision-making. The review is intended as a comprehensive and practical reference for clinicians in both endemic and non-endemic settings to navigate the complexities of clinical expression and optimize diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.
authors: for The Cysticercosis Working Group in Peru (CWGP)
items.citation: Javier A. Bustos, Christina M. Coyle, Kiran T. Thakur et al.. Taenia solium neurocysticercosis: Its current epidemiological, diagnostic, therapeutic, and control landscapes. PLoS neglected tropical diseases. 2026

items.title: Antimicrobial Resistance in the Food Chain: Bridging Knowledge Gaps for Effective Detection and Control
items.summary: This review examined antimicrobial resistance as a public health threat transmitted through the food chain, connecting animals, the environment, and humans through a One Health framework. The authors analyzed the major drivers of resistance spread across animal agriculture, aquaculture, and food processing sectors. They compared traditional culture-based phenotypic detection methods against emerging molecular approaches, including whole genome sequencing, metagenomics, and CRISPR-based diagnostics, finding that while molecular tools offer superior speed and resolution, persistent challenges such as matrix interference, the viable but non-culturable bacterial state, and disconnects between genotype and phenotype limit their utility. The review also described integrated mitigation strategies spanning antimicrobial stewardship on farms, biofilm control innovations, and consumer hygiene practices. The authors conclude that bridging technical and regulatory gaps in surveillance is essential for developing effective interventions and improving food system safety.
items.citation: Emílio Gomes, Tomás Gonçalves Mesquita, Patrícia Serra et al.. Antimicrobial Resistance in the Food Chain: Bridging Knowledge Gaps for Effective Detection and Control. Antibiotics. 2026

items.title: A Systematic Review of Methodological Approaches to SARS-CoV-2 Wastewater Surveillance
items.summary: This systematic review examined the methodological landscape of wastewater-based epidemiology as a surveillance tool for SARS-CoV-2 during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors conducted a reproducible literature search across two major databases, covering studies published over a four-year period, to synthesize findings on techniques used for sample collection, concentration, viral RNA extraction, and detection. The review found that the majority of studies demonstrated a meaningful correlation between SARS-CoV-2 RNA concentrations in wastewater and broader epidemiological trends, supporting the value of this approach for community-level disease monitoring. However, the review also identified persistent technical challenges, including the presence of inhibitors that interfere with RNA extraction and a notable lack of standardized protocols across studies. The authors present their findings as a framework intended to guide future research toward more uniform, reproducible methods that could be applied in responses to future infectious disease outbreaks.
items.citation: G Deak, Laura Lupu, Raluca Prangate. A Systematic Review of Methodological Approaches to SARS-CoV-2 Wastewater Surveillance. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents
items.summary: This paper investigates whether procedural knowledge accumulated from past software repairs can be reused to improve the performance of large language model-driven coding agents on new issues. The authors developed STAIR, a framework that converts historical repair trajectories into hierarchical, multi-level tree structures capturing everything from fine-grained diagnostic actions to high-level repair strategies. When a new issue arrives, STAIR retrieves relevant nodes from these abstracted plans, adapts them to the specific problem, and injects them into the agent's prompt as guidance. Evaluated on a standard software engineering benchmark, the approach achieves strong resolution rates and, notably, the generated plans transfer across structurally different agents without any code modification, substantially improving their performance. Ablation studies confirm that combining multiple abstraction levels outperforms using any single level, and that raw, unabstracted trajectories transfer considerably less effectively than the hierarchical representations.
items.citation: Yisen Xu, Jiayuan Zhou, Ruiqi Pan et al.. Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of fragmented and non-interoperable knowledge in HVAC fault detection and diagnosis, where heterogeneous data sources and diverse diagnostic outputs hinder effective system maintenance and energy efficiency. The researchers developed FDD-ON, a modular and extensible ontology specifically designed to formally represent variable air volume HVAC system components, fault types, symptom statuses, fault impacts, and their interrelationships using well-defined controlled vocabulary. The ontology explicitly encodes contributing cause–fault–symptom–impact relationships to create a machine-interpretable semantic framework capable of querying diagnostic knowledge and mapping heterogeneous outputs across different systems. FDD-ON was evaluated against publicly available variable air volume HVAC datasets and demonstrated through practical fault detection and diagnosis application development. The authors conclude that FDD-ON provides a foundational semantic infrastructure for building scalable, transparent, and interoperable fault detection solutions, including those leveraging digital twins and artificial intelligence-driven maintenance decision-making.
items.citation: Yimin Chen, Brian Fricke, Bo Shen et al.. Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations
items.summary: This paper develops the theoretical basis for an automated conversational assessment system called the "Socratic Test," which aims to overcome limitations of both traditional written exams and face-to-face oral examinations. The authors argue that static assessments punish academic ambition through deficit-based grading, while oral exams introduce construct-irrelevant variance through anxiety and power imbalances. Their proposed system integrates Dynamic Assessment principles, Bloom's Taxonomy for real-time monitoring, and the SOLO Taxonomy for evaluating response quality, using graduated scaffolding to map and quantify a student's Zone of Proximal Development. The framework also specifies a non-compensatory, additive grading architecture designed to reward demonstrated mastery rather than penalize errors, combined with human-AI alignment mechanisms intended to improve measurement reliability. The paper is primarily theoretical, formalizing the conceptual and taxonomic underpinnings of the system rather than reporting empirical results.
items.citation: Ilya Mikhelson. The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations. arXiv. 2026
