items.title: On the use of field RR Lyrae as Galactic probes:. IX. Radial velocities
items.summary: This paper presents a large, homogeneous catalog of radial velocity measurements for field RR Lyrae variable stars, drawing on both proprietary and publicly available spectroscopic data to assemble a sample of tens of thousands of stars pulsating in fundamental, first overtone, and double modes. Radial velocity curve templates for metallic and Balmer lines were applied to derive radial velocity amplitudes and barycentric velocities, with accuracy varying depending on how well sampled the radial velocity curves were. The study finds that metallicity dependence of radial velocity amplitudes is negligible for metallic lines but becomes significant for higher Balmer lines, and that scaling relations between photometric and radial velocity amplitudes are linear for first-overtone pulsators but nonlinear for fundamental-mode pulsators, suggesting convection differentially affects luminosity versus radial velocity amplitudes across the instability strip. The spectroscopic Bailey diagram reveals a smooth, low-scatter transition from metal-poor to metal-rich stars at fixed period. Additionally, the metallicity distribution of Blazhko RR Lyrae stars is found to be skewed toward more metal-intermediate and metal-rich compositions.
items.citation: K. Baeza-Villagra, V. F. Braga, M. Fabrizio et al.. On the use of field RR Lyrae as Galactic probes:. IX. Radial velocities. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Spindrift: Learning quantum degeneracy from thermal purity in restricted path integral Monte Carlo
items.summary: This paper addresses a fundamental challenge in simulating fermionic quantum systems at finite temperature: the nodal surface required by restricted path integral Monte Carlo must be supplied externally and, unless exact, introduces systematic fixed-node energy errors. The authors introduce Spindrift, a variational density matrix method that learns the many-body fermionic density matrix self-consistently by minimizing a regularized Bloch residual using samples drawn from a restricted Worm algorithm. The approach exploits the simplicity of quantum mechanics at high temperature, where free-particle behavior dominates, and trains the density matrix through a temperature curriculum that progressively learns corrections to a free-particle reference, using a permutation-equivariant continuous normalizing flow combined with a Jastrow factor to guarantee exact fermionic antisymmetry. Applied to interacting fermions in a two-dimensional harmonic trap, the method demonstrates stable training in which the learned velocity field smoothly deforms the nodal structure away from the free-particle limit, lowering the restricted thermodynamic energy at each temperature. While the absence of a nodal action in the current estimator prevents absolute energy benchmarking, the work establishes a physics-informed framework in which the nodal surface is determined self-consistently rather than imposed externally.
items.citation: Jarvist Moore Frost. Spindrift: Learning quantum degeneracy from thermal purity in restricted path integral Monte Carlo. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Tartu Observatory Fiber-fed Echelle Spectrograph (TOFES) Data Reduction Pipeline
items.summary: The paper presents the data reduction pipeline developed for a fiber-fed echelle spectrograph installed at Tartu Observatory. The instrument is designed to connect to a large telescope via a four-channel adapter at the Cassegrain focus, offering broad wavelength coverage from the near-ultraviolet to the near-infrared in a single exposure at moderate-to-high spectral resolution. The pipeline is built upon an existing Python-based reduction package and was validated using solar spectra, with an additional custom toolbox developed to support spectral line identification and radial velocity measurements. The system is intended to address diverse astrophysical problems, including characterizing young stellar objects and their protoplanetary disk accretion, determining properties of exoplanet host stars relevant to upcoming space missions, and monitoring atmospheric variability in massive stars.
items.citation: Sandipan P. D. Borthakur, Tõnis Eenmäe, Nikolai Piskunov et al.. The Tartu Observatory Fiber-fed Echelle Spectrograph (TOFES) Data Reduction Pipeline. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic utility of cystatin C for early detection of acute kidney injury in patients with sepsis. The researchers systematically retrieved relevant studies from electronic databases, assessed their quality using the QUADAS-2 tool, and performed a random-effects meta-analysis along with construction of a summary receiver operating characteristic curve. Cystatin C demonstrated good overall diagnostic performance for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, with high values for both sensitivity and specificity and an area under the curve indicating strong discriminative ability. Subgroup analyses showed that studies applying the Sepsis 3.0 diagnostic criteria yielded higher specificity and diagnostic odds ratios with reduced heterogeneity, and combining cystatin C with other biomarkers further improved diagnostic accuracy. The authors conclude that cystatin C is a promising biomarker for the early clinical diagnosis of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury, despite acknowledging residual heterogeneity across included studies.
items.citation: Cheng L, Zhang B, Hu X et al.. Diagnostic value of cystatin C in acute kidney injury among patients with sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.
items.summary: This narrative review examined pancreatic stone protein as a potential biomarker for detecting and risk-stratifying sepsis in paediatric patients, particularly in nosocomial and postoperative contexts where distinguishing infection from sterile inflammation is difficult. The authors conducted a structured literature search across two major databases, identifying studies published over a recent multi-year period and screening them to produce a final evidence base meeting defined inclusion criteria. The review found that pancreatic stone protein levels rise significantly in children with sepsis compared to those with non-infectious systemic inflammation, and elevated levels were associated with bacteraemia, organ dysfunction, and mortality. Its diagnostic performance was reported as comparable to or exceeding that of conventional markers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin, including evidence from neonatal and other high-risk paediatric populations. The authors conclude that pancreatic stone protein is a promising early diagnostic and prognostic tool for paediatric sepsis, while noting that study variability necessitates larger multicentre prospective trials and integration into multimarker diagnostic frameworks.
items.citation: Ramírez Quintana A, Gaman EL, Badea M et al.. Pancreatic Stone Protein as an Emerging Biomarker in Paediatric Nosocomial and Postoperative Sepsis: An Integrative Review of Diagnostic and Prognostic Performance.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction, a marker of bone marrow thrombopoietic activity, for the early identification of sepsis. The authors searched two major databases and pooled data from studies meeting their inclusion criteria, calculating sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio, and summary receiver operating characteristic curves, with a subgroup analysis focused on adult populations. The meta-analysis found that immature platelet fraction demonstrated only moderate diagnostic accuracy, with pooled sensitivity and specificity both around seventy percent and moderate heterogeneity observed across the included studies. The authors conclude that immature platelet fraction may serve as a complementary rather than standalone biomarker for sepsis diagnosis, but emphasize that the small number of eligible studies and methodological variability limit confidence in these estimates. They call for larger, standardized prospective studies to clarify the clinical utility of this marker.
items.citation: Wiranata S, Manuaba IBAP, Supadmanaba IGP et al.. Early diagnostic accuracy of immature platelet fraction for sepsis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.. Hematology, transfusion and cell therapy. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated and compared the diagnostic accuracy of interleukin-27 (IL-27) and C-reactive protein (CRP) as biomarkers for neonatal sepsis, addressing inconsistencies in previous clinical studies. Following PRISMA guidelines, the authors searched major medical databases and included controlled studies involving neonates, applying pooled sensitivity, specificity, and summary receiver operating characteristic curve analyses. The results showed that IL-27 achieved higher pooled sensitivity and specificity than CRP for diagnosing neonatal sepsis, with a notably greater area under the curve. The authors conclude that IL-27 demonstrates superior diagnostic accuracy compared to CRP and may serve as a more reliable biomarker for the early and accurate identification of neonatal sepsis in clinical settings. However, the conclusion is based on a small number of included studies with a limited total patient population, which may affect the robustness and generalizability of the findings.
items.citation: Liu W, Zhang Y, Liu W et al.. Diagnostic performance of interleukin-27 and C-reactive protein in neonatal sepsis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Aligning neonatal sepsis triage diagnostics with WHO target product profiles in low- and middle-income countries.
items.summary: This paper examined the landscape of diagnostic tools and strategies for neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries, where the condition remains a major driver of infant death despite limited diagnostic progress. The authors synthesized evidence across a range of current and emerging approaches, including clinical algorithms, host-response biomarkers, haematological parameters, continuous monitoring, and artificial intelligence-based digital platforms, evaluating each against the WHO Target Product Profile for neonatal sepsis triage. The analysis assessed diagnostic performance alongside operational feasibility in resource-constrained settings, with particular attention to affordability, suitability for non-hospital use, and point-of-care applicability. The review identified promising advances, including more accurate host-response biomarkers and affordable technologies capable of enhancing existing predictive algorithms. Based on these findings, the authors advocate for integrated diagnostic strategies that combine point-of-care testing, routine clinical data, and digital decision support to enable earlier detection, more rational antibiotic use, and reductions in neonatal mortality.
items.citation: Gleeson B, Blumel B, Ibarz Pavon AB et al.. Aligning neonatal sepsis triage diagnostics with WHO target product profiles in low- and middle-income countries.. BMJ global health. 2026

items.title: Calprotectin as a Diagnostic Marker for Lower Respiratory Tract Infection and Sepsis in the Emergency Department.
items.summary: The study investigated whether calprotectin, a neutrophil activation marker measured in plasma, could serve as a useful diagnostic biomarker for sepsis and for identifying the source of infection in patients presenting to an emergency department. A prospective cohort of patients with suspected sepsis was enrolled at a university hospital, with calprotectin levels measured at admission and compared against established markers such as C-reactive protein. Calprotectin showed modest ability to distinguish sepsis from non-infectious systemic inflammation, but was not an independent predictor when combined with C-reactive protein in multivariable analysis. However, calprotectin demonstrated meaningful ability to differentiate lower respiratory tract infections from both upper respiratory tract infections and urinary tract infections, and adding it to C-reactive protein significantly improved discrimination for these comparisons. The authors conclude that calprotectin may add diagnostic value specifically in identifying lower respiratory tract infections among sepsis patients, though further research is needed to determine its role in routine clinical assessment.
items.citation: Wollmer M, Wessman T, Melander O et al.. Calprotectin as a Diagnostic Marker for Lower Respiratory Tract Infection and Sepsis in the Emergency Department.. Open forum infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: This paper presents the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign international clinical practice guidelines for the management of sepsis and septic shock in adults. The guidelines were developed by a large, geographically diverse multidisciplinary committee, including patient and family advisors, using the GRADE methodology and an Evidence to Decision framework to synthesize evidence and formulate recommendations across six clinical domains: screening and early management, infection, hemodynamics, respiratory support, adjunctive therapies, and goals and transitions of care. Recommendations address areas including sepsis screening in prehospital and hospital settings, early antimicrobial therapy, antimicrobial stewardship, fluid resuscitation, and respiratory and hemodynamic support. The guidelines provide both strong and conditional recommendations calibrated to the certainty of available evidence, with explicit attention to patient values, resource availability, and applicability in low- and middle-income country settings. The overarching aim is to support clinicians and health systems in making evidence-based decisions to improve early identification, treatment, and outcomes for patients with sepsis and septic shock.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026
items.summary: The abstract provided is too thin to summarize meaningfully, containing only background epidemiological context about sepsis and a brief statement about the importance of early identification and treatment, with no description of the guideline methodology, specific recommendations, or findings presented in the full document.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzanic et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and how its dysregulation contributes to a broad range of diseases. The authors synthesize the research history of lipid metabolism and focus particularly on how lipid functions, transport, and signaling pathways regulate the behavior of immune cells, including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils, in both innate and adaptive immunity. They explore how specific lipid metabolites influence immune cell proliferation, differentiation, and activation, and describe multilevel regulatory mechanisms spanning genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational processes. The review further connects dysregulated lipid metabolism to conditions such as autoimmune diseases, cancer, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and metabolic disorders. Finally, the authors survey therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism, ongoing clinical trial progress, and future directions including lipid-derived biomarkers and novel treatment approaches.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Sepsis
items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Exosomal Biomarker Discovery for Cardiovascular Diseases: Multi-Omics Integration, Reproducibility, and Translational Prospects
items.summary: This review examined the use of artificial intelligence to discover exosomal and extracellular vesicle biomarkers for cardiovascular diseases, addressing the challenge that these vesicles carry disease-relevant molecular cargo but generate highly heterogeneous, high-dimensional data that is difficult to analyze reproducibly. The authors conducted a comprehensive comparative analysis of machine learning, deep learning, and network-based approaches, evaluating how these methods integrate multi-omics profiles with clinical metadata for feature selection, disease subtyping, and interpretable model development. Ensemble methods such as random forest and gradient boosting showed the most consistent classification performance, while graph neural networks emerged as promising for pathway integration, and evolutionary neural networks demonstrated comparable discrimination of vesicle morphological features but with interpretability limitations. The review found that current evidence in conditions like acute myocardial infarction and heart failure remains largely exploratory, relying on small cohorts with limited external validation and lacking direct comparison to established clinical standards such as high-sensitivity troponin. The authors propose a practical framework specifying reproducibility criteria, standardized isolation protocols aligned with existing vesicle research guidelines, and transparent artificial intelligence reporting practices to advance exosomal diagnostics toward clinical implementation.
items.citation: Rasit Dinc, Nurittin Ardıç. Artificial Intelligence for Exosomal Biomarker Discovery for Cardiovascular Diseases: Multi-Omics Integration, Reproducibility, and Translational Prospects. Cells. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent innovations in microfluidic chip technology, commonly called lab-on-a-chip systems, and their applications in laboratory medicine. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of advances in chip design and fabrication methods, including three-dimensional printing and modular flexible substrates, as well as the integration of biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes in real time. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the development of smart diagnostic platforms with self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support capabilities. The review finds that these combined technologies have broadened clinical utility across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, personalized medicine, and emerging fields such as neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The authors also address persistent challenges in manufacturing, clinical validation, and system integration that must be overcome before next-generation microfluidic technologies can be widely implemented in routine clinical and public health settings.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Emulating the nonlinear effects of modified gravity on the matter power spectrum for reconstruction
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational challenge of incorporating nonlinear modified gravity effects into model-independent reconstructions of modified gravity functions, where repeated likelihood evaluations make direct calculations prohibitively expensive. The authors constructed a neural-network emulator trained on a very large set of samples to predict the nonlinear correction ratio of the modified gravity nonlinear matter power spectrum to its linear counterpart, using the CosmoPower framework. The emulator achieves agreement with reference calculations to within a few percent across the relevant scale ranges, with higher accuracy at large scales and modest degradation only at the smallest scales in extreme nonlinear scenarios. Validation through independent test sets and Markov chain Monte Carlo analyses with synthetic data confirms that the emulator reliably recovers standard cosmological parameters and the general relativity limits of reconstructed modified gravity functions, demonstrating its suitability for Stage-IV survey analyses. The authors further illustrate the emulator's utility in breaking near-degeneracies between models with similar linear power spectra, generating theory predictions for current photometric survey likelihoods, and forecasting combined survey constraints using principal component analysis.
items.citation: Lanyang Yi, Kazuya Koyama, Qi Xiong et al.. Emulating the nonlinear effects of modified gravity on the matter power spectrum for reconstruction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field
items.summary: This paper examines the production of dark photons as dark matter through the perturbative decay of a dark Higgs field that is displaced from its potential minimum via stochastic misalignment during inflation. The framework is notable for being simple and predictive, generating the observed dark photon relic abundance without requiring fine-tuned initial conditions. The scenario faces constraints from structure formation, because the produced dark photons are initially boosted rather than cold, and from inflationary isocurvature fluctuations, which force the dark Higgs quartic coupling to be small. The authors identify a viable parameter space spanning dark photon masses from roughly one hundred electron volts to one gigaelectronvolt with extremely small gauge couplings, a region that tightens considerably if kinetic mixing with the Standard Model photon is present. This favored region is potentially testable through future cosmic microwave background or Lyman-alpha forest observations, and via direct detection experiments or diffuse soft gamma-ray searches if kinetic mixing exists.
items.citation: James M. Cline, Gonzalo Herrera, Jean-Samuel Roux. Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography
items.summary: This paper investigates how many copies of an unknown quantum state are required to estimate or test its fundamental properties, specifically its spectrum, von Neumann entropy, and rank. The authors establish near-quadratic lower bounds on the sample complexity for these tasks in terms of the Hilbert space dimension, showing that the number of required copies is essentially as large as that needed for full quantum state tomography. To prove these lower bounds, the authors construct hard-to-distinguish pairs of quantum states using sandwiched products of Haar-random projectors, developing a novel normalization technique that yields explicit expressions for high-order tensor moments of these states in terms of symmetric functions of Jucys–Murphy elements in the symmetric group algebra. Indistinguishability between these hard instances is established through moment-matching and bounding an f-divergence via high-order components, while the non-vanishing high-order terms simultaneously certify that the instances genuinely differ in their spectra, entropies, and ranks. The results overturn any hope of achieving substantially more efficient algorithms than tomography for these natural unitarily invariant estimation and testing tasks.
items.citation: Marco Fanizza, Ryan O'Donnell, Chirag Wadhwa. Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ArcLP: A Matlab implementation of an $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n}L)$ arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming
items.summary: This paper presents a Matlab software implementation of an arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming that carries the best known polynomial complexity bound among interior-point methods for this problem class. The authors describe the software architecture, key functions, and implementation strategies, and demonstrate ease of use through a worked example. The implementation was extensively tested on standard Netlib benchmark linear programming problems spanning a wide range of problem sizes, including instances with tens of thousands of constraints and hundreds of thousands of variables, and it successfully found optimal solutions in all cases. Computational results were compared against the widely used Mehrotra predictor-corrector algorithm, and the authors conclude that their implementation is not only theoretically superior in terms of polynomial complexity but also competitive in practical performance.
items.citation: Yang, Yaguang. ArcLP: A Matlab implementation of an $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n}L)$ arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fermionic entropy: an efficiently measurable strong monotone for non-Gaussianity
items.summary: This paper studies fermionic non-Gaussianity as a quantum computational resource, focusing on how to rigorously and efficiently quantify departures from the classically tractable class of fermionic Gaussian states. The authors introduce the fermionic entropy, defined via the squared Frobenius norm of the correlation matrix, and prove it is a strong monotone under Gaussian operations for pure states, meaning it cannot increase under free-fermion manipulations. A central practical result is that the associated fermionic purity can be estimated from a number of two-copy measurements that is independent of system size, making the measure directly experimentally accessible. The authors further establish that fermionic entropy satisfies asymptotic continuity, giving it an operational interpretation as an upper bound on the rate at which non-Gaussian resource states can be distilled, and they derive improved sample complexity bounds for testing whether a state is Gaussian. As a further application, they prove that a linear number of non-Gaussian gates is necessary for Matchgate circuits supplemented with local non-Gaussian operations to approximate a quantum state design, matching known upper bounds up to logarithmic factors and quantifying the extensive non-Gaussianity cost required to emulate Haar-random quantum dynamics.
items.citation: Lorenzo Leone, Lennart Bittel. Fermionic entropy: an efficiently measurable strong monotone for non-Gaussianity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents
items.summary: This paper investigates whether procedural knowledge accumulated from past software repair tasks can be systematically reused to improve future repairs by large language model-driven coding agents, rather than treating each issue in isolation. The authors developed STAIR, a framework that converts historical repair trajectories into hierarchical, multi-level tree structures encoding experience at varying levels of abstraction, from fine-grained diagnostic actions to high-level repair strategies. When a new issue arrives, STAIR retrieves relevant plan nodes across abstraction levels, adapts them into issue-specific executable plans, and injects them into the agent's prompt. Evaluations on a standard software engineering benchmark show strong performance, and the generated plans generalize across structurally different agents without any code modification. Ablation studies confirm that combining multiple abstraction levels outperforms any single level, and that raw unabstracted trajectories transfer knowledge substantially less effectively than the hierarchical representation.
items.citation: Yisen Xu, Jiayuan Zhou, Ruiqi Pan et al.. Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Rapid diagnostics innovations for urinary tract infections using molecular biology, artificial intelligence and antimicrobial resistance surveillance: a comprehensive review.
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape and emerging innovations in diagnostic approaches for urinary tract infections, a globally prevalent bacterial infection complicated by high recurrence, polymicrobial complexity, biofilm formation, and rapidly spreading antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed molecular diagnostic technologies including nucleic acid amplification, biosensor-based platforms, microfluidic lab-on-chip systems, and omics-based approaches, evaluating their capacity for rapid and pathogen-specific detection compared to traditional culture-based methods. A central focus is the integration of these molecular tools with artificial intelligence and machine learning models to improve diagnostic speed, sensitivity, and precision in identifying uropathogens and their resistance profiles. The review highlights translational applications of these combined technologies for guiding targeted antimicrobial therapy and supporting antimicrobial resistance surveillance, while also addressing ethical, regulatory, and implementation challenges. The authors conclude that the convergence of next-generation molecular diagnostics and AI-assisted tools represents a transformative approach for improving antibiotic stewardship and clinical management of urinary tract infections.
items.citation: Goyal S, Sharma P, Aggarwal D et al.. Rapid diagnostics innovations for urinary tract infections using molecular biology, artificial intelligence and antimicrobial resistance surveillance: a comprehensive review.. Molecular biology reports. 2026

items.title: ERS/ESCMID state-of-the-science statement on the role of rapid diagnostic tests for the diagnosis and management of community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections.
items.summary: This paper presents a state-of-the-science statement from major European respiratory and infectious disease societies examining the role of rapid diagnostic tests in managing community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections. Produced in the context of a European Union–funded project aimed at combatting antimicrobial resistance, the work reviewed existing literature and current clinical practice surrounding rapid diagnostics, biomarkers, and clinical algorithms for these infections. The statement evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of rapid tests for identifying causative pathogens, assessed how the choice of diagnostic protocol influences understood disease aetiology, and examined how rapid testing can be integrated into antibiotic stewardship programs. The authors argue that optimizing antibiotic use through improved rapid diagnostics can reduce excess morbidity associated with respiratory infections and help limit the emergence of multidrug-resistant organisms.
items.citation: Polverino E, De Nardo P, Gentilotti E et al.. ERS/ESCMID state-of-the-science statement on the role of rapid diagnostic tests for the diagnosis and management of community-acquired lower respiratory tract infections.. The European respiratory journal. 2026

items.title: Novel Rapid Phenotypic Susceptibility Testing Techniques That Enhance Antimicrobial Stewardship and Clinical Decision-Making.
items.summary: This review paper examined emerging rapid phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing technologies and their role in addressing the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance. The authors surveyed the fundamentals of phenotypic testing approaches, with particular attention to growth-based methods, and synthesized evidence on how these technologies affect clinical and stewardship outcomes. Rapid phenotypic testing delivers actionable susceptibility results considerably faster than conventional methods, which is especially consequential in severe infections such as sepsis where treatment delays worsen morbidity and mortality. The review finds that these technologies can reduce time to effective therapy and support antimicrobial stewardship programs, though implementation barriers remain, including variability in test performance, absence of standardized protocols, and cost-benefit uncertainties. The authors conclude that rapid phenotypic susceptibility testing represents an important advance in bridging current diagnostic gaps and enabling more timely, evidence-based antimicrobial prescribing.
items.citation: Glover JS, Humphries R. Novel Rapid Phenotypic Susceptibility Testing Techniques That Enhance Antimicrobial Stewardship and Clinical Decision-Making.. Clinical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Rapid Multiplex Antimicrobial Resistance Profiling and Bacterial Identification by LAP-MALDI Mass Spectrometry Biotyping.
items.summary: This paper developed and evaluated a rapid multiplex diagnostic approach for simultaneously identifying bacteria and characterizing their antibiotic resistance profiles using liquid atmospheric pressure MALDI mass spectrometry. The method applies a beta-lactam antibiotic panel to small volumes of bacterial culture, detecting antibiotic degradation products alongside lipid and protein biomarkers within a few hours. Strains carrying clinically important resistance genes were reliably distinguished from susceptible isolates, while species identification was achieved with very high accuracy through both lipid and protein profiling. The technology's ability to generate multiply charged protein ions also enables tandem mass spectrometry protein sequencing, providing an additional layer of characterization beyond conventional MALDI biotyping. The authors argue this platform offers improved diagnostic capabilities for clinical microbiology and antimicrobial stewardship by combining resistance profiling, species identification, and protein sequencing in a single, rapid workflow.
items.citation: Adair LR, Iyer S, Jones IM et al.. Rapid Multiplex Antimicrobial Resistance Profiling and Bacterial Identification by LAP-MALDI Mass Spectrometry Biotyping.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: A rapid molecular assay for the detection of hypervirulent <i>Klebsiella pneumoniae</i> in the context of antimicrobial resistance surveillance.
items.summary: The study addressed the need for rapid, practical detection of hypervirulent *Klebsiella pneumoniae* (hvKP), an increasingly concerning pathogen as hypervirulence converges with multidrug resistance, rendering current diagnostic tools inadequate for routine surveillance. The researchers developed a multiplex real-time PCR assay targeting key virulence-associated loci, including siderophore systems and hypermucoviscosity regulators, and evaluated it against a panel of clinical isolates and blood cultures, using whole-genome sequencing and the string test as comparators. The assay showed high concordance with whole-genome sequencing for principal virulence determinants and performed particularly well against the string test, correctly identifying high-virulence profiles. Direct testing from blood culture pellets was technically feasible, though broader validation in this specimen type remains necessary. Overall, the assay is proposed as an accessible, rapid complement to whole-genome sequencing for hvKP surveillance and early virulence profiling, with the potential to support clinical management and limit spread of high-risk lineages, pending further workflow optimization.
items.citation: Dimartino V, Rotondo C, Petriccione I et al.. A rapid molecular assay for the detection of hypervirulent <i>Klebsiella pneumoniae</i> in the context of antimicrobial resistance surveillance.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Rapid Detection of Pathogens and Resistance Genes in Positive Blood Cultures Using BioFire<sup>®</sup> FilmArray BCID2.
items.summary: This study evaluated the performance of a molecular diagnostic panel for rapidly identifying pathogens and antimicrobial resistance genes directly from positive blood cultures. Researchers compared the BioFire FilmArray Blood Culture Identification panel against conventional culture-based methods, mass spectrometry identification, and automated susceptibility testing in a university hospital setting, with resistance gene findings confirmed by polymerase chain reaction. The panel successfully detected at least one microorganism in the vast majority of samples, demonstrating strong overall agreement with conventional methods, including complete concordance for certain key pathogens such as Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Resistance genes identified by the panel correlated well with phenotypic resistance results, and the molecular approach notably identified a high proportion of samples as polymicrobial. The authors conclude that the panel is a reliable and rapid complement to conventional diagnostics for bloodstream infections, though its interpretation requires clinical context, particularly for organisms like coagulase-negative staphylococci that may represent contamination.
items.citation: Çinar C, Çayci YT, Atakcan Z et al.. Rapid Detection of Pathogens and Resistance Genes in Positive Blood Cultures Using BioFire<sup>®</sup> FilmArray BCID2.. Polish journal of microbiology. 2026

items.title: Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
items.summary: The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines represent a comprehensive international update on the identification and management of sepsis and septic shock in adult patients, developed using GRADE methodology and covering evidence through mid-2025. The guidelines encompass a total of one hundred twenty-nine statements spanning screening, infection management, hemodynamic support, respiratory care, adjunctive therapies, and long-term outcomes, with the majority being conditional recommendations reflecting uncertainty in the evidence base. Notable new guidance includes conditional recommendations for prehospital sepsis screening and antibiotic administration in transport settings, targeted blood pressure management with lower thresholds in older patients, selective digestive tract decontamination in low-resistance environments, and active fluid removal in the post-resuscitation phase. Key changes from the 2021 guidelines include updated guidance favoring crystalloids alone over supplemental albumin for fluid resuscitation, a shift away from routine empirical antifungal therapy, and the downgrading of norepinephrine from a strong to a conditional first-line vasopressor recommendation relative to vasopressin and angiotensin II. Several recommendations were also upgraded in strength or certainty, including prolonged beta-lactam infusion and antimicrobial de-escalation, reflecting accumulating evidence supporting these practices.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzani et al.. Executive Summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026. Critical Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026
items.summary: The abstract provided is too thin to summarize meaningfully, containing only epidemiological background and a general statement about early identification and treatment, with no description of the guidelines' specific methods, recommendations, or findings.
items.citation: Hallie C. Prescott, Massimo Antonelli, Waleed Alhazzanic et al.. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the relationship between lipid metabolism and cellular homeostasis, with particular emphasis on how lipid metabolic processes govern immune cell function across both innate and adaptive immunity. The authors synthesize the historical development of lipid metabolism research and detail the roles of lipid transport, signaling pathways, and metabolites in regulating the proliferation, differentiation, and activation of immune cells including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils. The review also explores multilevel regulatory mechanisms — spanning genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational levels — that shape immune cell behavior through lipid metabolism. Dysregulation of these processes is discussed in the context of a broad range of diseases, including autoimmune conditions, cancer, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and metabolic disorders. The authors conclude by surveying therapeutic strategies that target lipid metabolism, ongoing clinical trial progress, and emerging opportunities such as lipid-derived biomarkers and novel treatment approaches.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: A comprehensive review of green synthesis methods and applications of nanoparticles derived from plant extracts and microorganisms
items.summary: This review examines the field of green synthesis, in which biological entities such as plants, bacteria, fungi, algae, and yeast serve as natural reducing and stabilizing agents to produce nanoparticles without relying on toxic chemicals or harsh physical and chemical processes. The authors surveyed a broad body of literature to critically assess advances in plant-mediated and microorganism-assisted fabrication strategies, covering the mechanisms by which nanoparticles form, how biological constituents influence particle size, morphology, and stability, and the characterization techniques commonly used to evaluate these materials. The review evaluates the functional performance of green-synthesized nanoparticles across biomedical, agricultural, catalytic, and environmental applications, with particular attention to their photocatalytic and pollutant degradation capabilities in the context of environmental remediation. The authors identify reproducibility, standardization, and scalability as persistent challenges that currently limit the translation of green nanotechnology from laboratory-scale studies to practical and industrial use. The review aims to provide a structured assessment of the field and guide future research toward overcoming these barriers.
items.citation: Shoaeb Mohammad Syed, Shivam Kulkarni, Mayur Patil et al.. A comprehensive review of green synthesis methods and applications of nanoparticles derived from plant extracts and microorganisms. Discover Green Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide as a multifunctional two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, exploring its synthesis chemistry, structural properties, and potential for addressing challenges in energy, environmental remediation, and healthcare. The authors survey how the layered architecture of graphene oxide enables extensive surface functionalization and tunable properties, spanning structural configurations from zero-dimensional to three-dimensional nanostructures, with an adjustable band gap, high surface area, and notable optoelectronic and mechanical characteristics. The review covers applications including adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of pollutants such as microplastics, pathogens, and volatile organic compounds, as well as energy-related uses such as carbon dioxide photoreduction, hydrogen production, and battery technologies. Sensing applications, including surface-enhanced Raman scattering for ultrasensitive molecular detection and environmental gas sensing, alongside healthcare platforms, are also discussed. The authors additionally identify persistent challenges facing the material, including scalability limitations, long-term stability concerns, and reproducibility issues, while proposing potential solutions to enable its sustainable industrial deployment.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026

items.title: Food and Medicine Homology Focus in 2026
items.summary: This perspective paper examines the anticipated trajectory of the food and medicine homology field as it transitions from traditional empirical knowledge toward rigorous scientific frameworks. The authors outline a conceptual roadmap centered on building scientific credibility through systematic evidence generation, expanding the verified substance directory, and establishing standardized regulatory systems grounded in empirical data. Research priorities identified include elucidating active components and their mechanisms of action, particularly through the lens of gut microbiota interactions, phase separation, and immunometabolic reprogramming. Applications are expected to shift toward precision and dynamic health management by integrating multidimensional personal data with artificial intelligence to address chronic disease and aging. The field is also projected to modernize its industrial foundations through synthetic biology, intelligent delivery systems, and sustainable manufacturing practices.
items.citation: Mengyao Li, Gui-Fen Wu, Feng Lu et al.. Food and Medicine Homology Focus in 2026. Food & medicine homology.. 2026

items.title: Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents
items.summary: This paper investigates whether procedural knowledge from past software repairs performed by large language model agents can be systematically reused to improve future repairs, rather than treating each issue in isolation. The authors developed STAIR, a framework that converts historical repair trajectories into hierarchical, multi-level tree structures capturing everything from fine-grained diagnostic actions to high-level repair strategies. When a new issue is encountered, STAIR retrieves relevant nodes from these abstraction hierarchies, adapts them into executable issue-specific plans, and injects them into the agent's prompt. Evaluated on a standard software engineering benchmark, the framework achieves strong performance and notably generalizes across structurally different agents without any code modification, improving repair success rates substantially. Ablation studies confirm that combining multiple abstraction levels outperforms using any single level, and that raw unabstracted trajectories transfer considerably less effectively than the hierarchical representations.
items.citation: Yisen Xu, Jiayuan Zhou, Ruiqi Pan et al.. Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of fragmented knowledge representation in HVAC fault detection and diagnostics, where heterogeneous data sources and inconsistent diagnostic outputs hinder effective system maintenance and interoperability. The researchers developed FDD-ON, a modular and extensible ontology designed to formally represent variable air volume HVAC system components, fault types, symptom statuses, fault impacts, and their interrelationships through structured semantic vocabulary. The ontology encodes explicit cause-fault-symptom-impact relationships to enable machine-interpretable querying of diagnostic knowledge and to bridge diverse FDD outputs across different systems and applications. FDD-ON was evaluated using publicly available datasets and demonstrated through practical FDD development applications. The authors conclude that FDD-ON provides a foundational semantic framework capable of supporting scalable, transparent, and interoperable fault detection solutions, including digital twin frameworks and artificial intelligence-driven maintenance decision-making systems.
items.citation: Yimin Chen, Brian Fricke, Bo Shen et al.. Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Bootstrapping Self-Supervised Learning of Binary Classification Using Error Bounds: A Case Study on a Robotic Insertion Task
items.summary: The paper investigated how to enable rapid deployment of robotic systems in flexible manufacturing without extensive upfront setup, focusing on a robotic insertion task where controlling error rates is critical. The authors developed a data engine comprising two classifiers — a fast model prediction and an expensive verification step — where the system decides whether to invoke the costly verification based on the confidence level of the initial prediction, allowing users to set tolerable error thresholds. The approach uses UMAP for dimensionality reduction of force data and Wilson-Score intervals to compute confidence bounds, enabling the system to bootstrap its own labeled training data through self-supervised learning while operating in the real world. Results on the robotic insertion task showed that the system progressively reduces its reliance on expensive verifications over time while maintaining the specified error rate, demonstrating that confidence-bound-guided self-improvement is a viable strategy for reliable robotic classification in manufacturing contexts.
items.citation: Zebin Duan, Norbert Krüger, Juan Heredia et al.. Bootstrapping Self-Supervised Learning of Binary Classification Using Error Bounds: A Case Study on a Robotic Insertion Task. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations
items.summary: This paper addresses limitations of both traditional static written assessments and conventional oral examinations, arguing that the former obscures diagnostic nuance while the latter introduces anxiety and power-related biases that distort measurement. The authors propose a theoretical framework for the "Socratic Test," an automated, computer-mediated conversational assessment designed to overcome these shortcomings. The framework integrates Dynamic Assessment principles, Bloom's Taxonomy for real-time cognitive monitoring, and the SOLO Taxonomy for evaluating structural response quality, while using graduated scaffolding to formally quantify a student's Zone of Proximal Development. A non-compensatory, additive grading architecture is introduced to reward demonstrated mastery rather than penalize errors, and human-AI alignment mechanisms are incorporated to enhance measurement reliability. The paper is primarily theoretical, presenting the conceptual and taxonomic foundations for this assessment approach rather than reporting empirical results.
items.citation: Ilya Mikhelson. The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Human-Centered Validation of the Explainability-Performance Coefficient
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of objectively evaluating the quality of explanations produced by explainable artificial intelligence methods, particularly for deep learning models deployed in high-risk settings. The authors propose a model-agnostic metric called the EPC score, an extension of the Explainability-Performance Coefficient, which quantifies explanation quality by balancing the trade-off between selecting fewer features and maintaining model performance. The metric was empirically validated across tabular, text, and image data modalities to examine how network activations, data dimensionality, and explainer behavior interact. Critically, the EPC score was also validated against human-generated explanations, including lexical sentiment judgments and spatial visual annotations. The results indicate that higher EPC scores consistently align with human understanding, suggesting the metric captures explanation quality in a human-centered manner.
items.citation: Christian Oliva, Luis F. Lago-Fernández. A Human-Centered Validation of the Explainability-Performance Coefficient. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the use of field RR Lyrae as Galactic probes:. IX. Radial velocities
items.summary: This paper presents a large, homogeneous catalog of radial velocity measurements for field RR Lyrae variable stars, drawing on both proprietary and publicly available spectroscopic data spanning fundamental-mode, first-overtone, and double-mode pulsators. Radial velocity curve templates for metallic and Balmer lines were applied to derive velocity amplitudes and barycentric gamma velocities, with accuracy varying depending on how well the radial velocity curves were sampled. The study finds that the metallicity dependence of radial velocity amplitudes is negligible for metallic lines but grows increasingly significant for higher-order Balmer lines, and that the scaling relations between photometric and radial velocity amplitudes differ between the two main pulsation modes, suggesting convection affects luminosity amplitudes more than velocity amplitudes across the instability strip. The spectroscopic Bailey diagram reveals a smooth, low-scatter transition from metal-poor to metal-rich stars at fixed period, and the catalog also provides evidence that Blazhko effect variables are preferentially found at intermediate to high metallicities.
items.citation: K. Baeza-Villagra, V. F. Braga, M. Fabrizio et al.. On the use of field RR Lyrae as Galactic probes:. IX. Radial velocities. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the state of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, with particular attention to electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic detection modalities relevant to both food safety and clinical diagnostics. The authors survey how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms to enable real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexed detection, effectively transforming conventional biosensors into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically identifies persistent challenges including matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies such as ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panel hubs, blockchain-based traceability, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, also known as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their growing role in laboratory medicine and clinical diagnostics. The authors surveyed innovations in chip design and fabrication approaches, including three-dimensional printing and flexible modular substrates, as well as the integration of advanced biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes in real time. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled so-called smart diagnostic platforms that can self-optimize, automate analysis, and support clinical decision-making. The review finds that these combined advances have expanded microfluidic applications across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, personalized medicine, and emerging areas such as neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The authors also address persistent challenges in manufacturing consistency, clinical validation, and system integration that must be overcome before next-generation microfluidic technologies can be widely adopted in routine clinical and public health settings.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Microfluidic and Paper-Based Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Systems for Decentralized Diagnostics and Biosurveillance.
items.summary: This review examines recombinase polymerase amplification as a nucleic acid amplification strategy suited to decentralized diagnostics, focusing on how its ability to operate rapidly at mild temperatures makes it advantageous over polymerase chain reaction in resource-limited settings. The authors surveyed recent advances in coupling this chemistry with microfluidic and paper-based platforms, including centrifugal chips, capillary-driven systems, electrochemical biosensors, CRISPR-assisted assays, and sample-to-answer cartridges, across biomedical, food safety, environmental, and One Health applications. They found that integration of smartphone imaging, artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation, digital partitioning, and cloud connectivity is progressively enhancing the portability and decision-making capacity of these systems. The review also identifies persistent challenges including robust sample preparation, multiplexing stability, quantitative reliability, reagent storage, and regulatory validation that must be addressed before widespread field deployment. The authors conclude that continued convergence of this amplification chemistry with advanced detection modalities and data-assisted interpretation will support more accessible and reliable molecular diagnostic workflows.
items.citation: Wang HM, Lee SZ, Fu LM. Microfluidic and Paper-Based Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Systems for Decentralized Diagnostics and Biosurveillance.. Micromachines. 2026

items.title: A quantitative rapid test for urine creatinine <i>via</i> Fenton's reaction and a self-driven microfluidic device.
items.summary: This paper developed a rapid, quantitative method for measuring creatinine in urine, which is important both as a kidney function indicator and for normalizing other urine biomarkers. The approach exploits creatinine's ability to inhibit hydroxyl radicals generated by Fenton's reaction, which would otherwise cleave an oligonucleotide linker connecting magnetic and polystyrene microparticles. By measuring how much creatinine is present through the degree of microparticle binding preserved, and then using magnetic separation on a self-driven microfluidic device to translate this into a visible bar length, the method produces a readable quantitative output. The system demonstrated a low detection limit, broad pH tolerance, and resistance to interfering substances. Validation against a standard clinical method using real urine samples showed strong concordance, supporting its accuracy and potential utility in clinical settings.
items.citation: Hartanto H, Li J, Szeto CC et al.. A quantitative rapid test for urine creatinine <i>via</i> Fenton's reaction and a self-driven microfluidic device.. Lab on a chip. 2026

items.title: Fabrication of photoresist SU-8 pyrolyzed carbon electrodes and their integration in a microfluidic hematocrit detection system
items.summary: This paper investigated the fabrication of carbon microelectrodes derived from the photoresist SU-8 through pyrolysis, addressing limitations of conventional two-step pyrolysis methods such as adhesion problems, geometric distortion, and insufficient surface area in planar electrode designs. The researchers developed a three-step pyrolysis protocol to produce low-aspect-ratio planar carbon electrodes with both micro- and millimeter-scale features, then integrated these electrodes into a PDMS-based microfluidic device for hematocrit determination by measuring electrical current responses of red blood cells in phosphate-buffered saline. Surface characterization revealed that the pyrolytic carbon electrodes had substantially greater roughness and thickness compared to platinum electrodes, resulting in increased electroactive surface area that reduced charge-transfer and concentration overpotentials. The hematocrit detection device achieved precision and accuracy comparable to previously reported platinum-based systems, with a linear correlation observed between current response and red blood cell concentration. The work demonstrates that this simplified fabrication approach can produce high-performance, low-cost carbon microelectrodes suitable for integrated biosensing without requiring noble metals or complex surface coatings.
items.citation: Lee HY, Rogers J, Kendrick C et al.. Fabrication of photoresist SU-8 pyrolyzed carbon electrodes and their integration in a microfluidic hematocrit detection system. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The authors survey advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that enable long-term comfort and integration with the body, alongside multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. The integration of artificial intelligence for signal processing and predictive health insights is also assessed. Despite significant progress, the review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of AI-generated outputs. The paper synthesizes current knowledge across materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies to provide a comprehensive overview of the field's state and outstanding obstacles.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Commercial Translation of Electrochemical Biosensors: Supply Chain Strategy, Scale-Up Manufacturing, and Regulatory–Quality Considerations
items.summary: This review examines why so few electrochemical biosensors successfully transition from laboratory demonstrations to commercial products, despite their analytical maturity. The authors surveyed academic and industrial literature to analyze the translational gap through the lenses of supply chain design, manufacturing scale-up, and regulatory-quality frameworks rather than analytical performance alone. They compare dominant manufacturing approaches such as roll-to-roll printing and semiconductor-derived microfabrication, arguing that material choices for biorecognition elements, conductive inks, and substrates critically determine reproducibility, long-term stability, and regulatory compliance. The review further contrasts regulatory pathways across the United States, European Union, and China, showing how differences in device classification, required evidence, and quality management systems shape both time-to-market and post-market flexibility. Using case studies spanning disposable glucose strips, cartridge-based blood analyzers, and continuous monitoring systems, the paper proposes that manufacturing should be treated as an upstream optimization problem and offers a systems-level framework for aligning research design with industrial and regulatory realities.
items.citation: Gao Zhou, Haibin Liu. Commercial Translation of Electrochemical Biosensors: Supply Chain Strategy, Scale-Up Manufacturing, and Regulatory–Quality Considerations. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Machine learning–empowered smartphone platforms for sustainable point-of-care bacterial detection
items.citation: Rzgar Sirwan Raza, Shilan Arif Fatah, Sameera Sh. Mohammed Ameen et al.. Machine learning–empowered smartphone platforms for sustainable point-of-care bacterial detection. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Exosomal Biomarker Discovery for Cardiovascular Diseases: Multi-Omics Integration, Reproducibility, and Translational Prospects
items.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence can accelerate the discovery and validation of exosomal and extracellular vesicle biomarkers for cardiovascular diseases. The paper addresses the central challenge that extracellular vesicle datasets are highly dimensional, heterogeneous, and poorly reproducible across studies due to non-standardized isolation and characterization workflows. The authors analyze and compare multiple AI approaches—including ensemble methods, deep learning, graph neural networks, and evolutionary neural networks—for their ability to integrate multi-omics data with clinical metadata to identify disease-relevant biomarker panels, particularly in acute myocardial infarction and heart failure. They find that ensemble methods show the most consistent classification performance while graph neural networks offer promise for pathway integration but require larger validation cohorts, and that most current evidence remains exploratory and based on very small cohorts with limited external validation. The review concludes by proposing a practical framework that combines standardized protocols aligned with established guidelines, direct comparison against clinical reference standards, and transparent AI reporting to move exosomal diagnostics toward clinical implementation.
items.citation: Rasit Dinc, Nurittin Ardıç. Artificial Intelligence for Exosomal Biomarker Discovery for Cardiovascular Diseases: Multi-Omics Integration, Reproducibility, and Translational Prospects. Cells. 2026

items.title: Release-free phononic crystal with strong microwave coupling
items.summary: The paper investigated whether release-free phononic crystal cavities could achieve strong electromechanical coupling, addressing a key limitation of conventional suspended designs that suffer from poor thermal anchoring and excess noise. The researchers fabricated lithium niobate phononic crystal cavities directly on silicon and sapphire substrates without suspension, and coupled them to high-impedance microwave resonators. They demonstrated an electromechanical coupling rate that exceeds both the mechanical and microwave loss rates, achieving a cooperativity well above unity on resonance, and the devices maintained high mechanical quality factors at millikelvin temperatures on both substrate types. These results show that release-free phononic crystals are viable for strong microwave-to-phonon transduction, offering a thermally anchored and scalable platform for quantum interconnects, sensing, and computing applications.
items.citation: Joey Frey, Paul Burger, Trond Hjerpekjøn Haug et al.. Release-free phononic crystal with strong microwave coupling. arXiv. 2026

items.title: GQ-FSL: Green Quantized Federated Split Learning
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of deploying large deep neural networks on energy- and resource-constrained mobile devices at the wireless edge. The authors propose a framework called GQ-FSL that combines federated split learning with stochastic quantization, allowing different numerical precision levels to be used independently on the client-side and server-side portions of a split neural network. They develop parameterized energy models for the split architecture and derive theoretical convergence guarantees under heterogeneous data distributions across devices. A joint optimization problem is then formulated to simultaneously determine where to split the network and what precision levels to assign, minimizing total energy consumption subject to a target accuracy constraint. The framework is shown to achieve better energy efficiency than both standard quantized federated learning and full-precision federated split learning, enabling large-scale model deployment on constrained devices.
items.citation: Idan Roth, Lutz Lampe. GQ-FSL: Green Quantized Federated Split Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents
items.summary: This paper investigates whether procedural knowledge accumulated from past software repair attempts can be systematically reused to improve future repairs by LLM-driven coding agents. The authors developed STAIR, a framework that transforms historical repair trajectories into hierarchical multi-level tree structures capturing everything from fine-grained diagnostic actions to high-level repair strategies, allowing experience to be encoded at multiple levels of abstraction. When a new issue arrives, STAIR retrieves relevant nodes from these abstraction hierarchies, tailors them into executable issue-specific plans, and injects them into the agent's prompt. The framework achieves strong performance on a standard software engineering benchmark and notably generalizes across structurally different agents without any code modification. Ablation studies confirm that combining multiple abstraction levels outperforms any single level, and that raw unprocessed trajectories transfer substantially less effectively than the hierarchically abstracted plans.
items.citation: Yisen Xu, Jiayuan Zhou, Ruiqi Pan et al.. Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of fragmented and poorly interoperable knowledge in HVAC fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) by developing a formal ontology called FDD-ON. The authors constructed a modular and extensible ontology that systematically represents variable air volume HVAC system components, fault types, symptom statuses, fault impacts, and their interrelationships through explicitly defined cause-fault-symptom-impact chains. FDD-ON integrates controlled vocabulary and comprehensive fault, symptom, and impact libraries to enable machine-interpretable querying of diagnostic knowledge and mapping of heterogeneous FDD outputs. The ontology was evaluated using publicly available VAV HVAC datasets and demonstrated through practical FDD development applications. The authors claim that FDD-ON provides a foundational semantic framework capable of supporting scalable, transparent, and interoperable FDD solutions, including digital twin frameworks and AI-driven maintenance decision-making systems.
items.citation: Yimin Chen, Brian Fricke, Bo Shen et al.. Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Continuous Tuning of the Charge-Phase Uncertainty in a Josephson Junction
items.citation: Irena Padniuk, Xianzhe Zeng, Juan Carlos Cuevas et al.. Continuous Tuning of the Charge-Phase Uncertainty in a Josephson Junction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations
items.summary: This paper proposes a theoretical framework for an automated conversational assessment system called the "Socratic Test," designed to address limitations in both traditional written exams and oral examinations. The authors argue that static assessments penalize ambitious attempts and obscure useful diagnostic information, while face-to-face oral exams introduce construct-irrelevant variance through anxiety and power imbalances. The proposed system integrates Dynamic Assessment principles, Bloom's Taxonomy, and the SOLO Taxonomy within a computer-mediated, multimodal environment to actively probe the boundaries of student understanding in real time. A key feature is the formalization of graduated scaffolding as a means of quantifying the Zone of Proximal Development, paired with an additive, non-compensatory grading architecture that rewards demonstrated mastery rather than penalizing errors. The paper also claims that human-AI alignment within this framework can achieve superior measurement reliability compared to conventional assessment approaches.
items.citation: Ilya Mikhelson. The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide, a two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, as a multifunctional platform with broad potential across energy, environmental, and healthcare applications. The authors survey its synthesis chemistry, property modification strategies, and structural characteristics, including its tunable band gap, high surface area, and capacity for surface functionalization that enables configurations ranging from zero-dimensional to three-dimensional nanostructures. The review covers applications in environmental remediation such as adsorption and photocatalytic degradation of pollutants, plastics, and pathogens, as well as energy-related uses including hydrogen production, carbon dioxide photoreduction, and battery technologies. Sensing applications, including surface-enhanced Raman scattering for detecting biological and organic molecules, are also discussed alongside healthcare platforms. The authors acknowledge that despite its considerable promise, graphene oxide faces practical challenges around scalability, long-term stability, and reproducibility, and they propose potential solutions to support its sustainable advancement toward real-world and industrial deployment.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026

items.title: Aptamer-gated luminescence enhancement and red-shift in a MOF: a ratiometric and color-tonality visual biosensor for pathogenic E. coli detection
items.citation: Shilan Arif Fatah, Sameera Sh. Mohammed Ameen, Payam B. Hassan et al.. Aptamer-gated luminescence enhancement and red-shift in a MOF: a ratiometric and color-tonality visual biosensor for pathogenic E. coli detection. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect priority foodborne pathogens, including *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which continue to threaten global public health. The authors survey advances across electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, emphasizing how functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering strategies have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into biosensor systems, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transforms conventional tools into smart diagnostic devices. The review critically addresses persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI frameworks. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-enabled traceability, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review paper examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, commonly known as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their applications in laboratory medicine. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of innovations in chip design and fabrication, including developments in three-dimensional printing, modular architectures, and flexible substrates, alongside progress in biosensor integration for detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the development of smart diagnostic platforms capable of self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support. The review finds that these combined advances have expanded clinical applications across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, and emerging areas such as neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The authors also identify persistent challenges in manufacturing, clinical validation, and system integration that must be addressed before next-generation microfluidic technologies can be widely adopted in routine clinical and public health practice.
