items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review paper examines candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by Candida species that represents a major source of hospital-acquired infections with high mortality and healthcare costs. The authors synthesize current knowledge on the epidemiology, species distribution, and origins of candidemia, alongside a critical evaluation of existing diagnostic methods and their limitations. The review addresses therapeutic strategies spanning empiric and targeted antifungal regimens, management of mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing challenge of antifungal resistance, including the potential role of combination therapy. Emerging diagnostic technologies, novel antifungal agents in clinical development, and compounds targeting new fungal pathways are highlighted as promising advances. The paper also looks toward future directions including artificial intelligence applications in diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment approaches, with the overall aim of guiding clinicians and researchers in managing this evolving clinical challenge.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Advancing non-faradaic impedance biosensors: sensitivity enhancement strategies using microfluidics, multiscale labeling, and CMOS technology
items.summary: This review examines non-Faradaic impedance biosensors, which detect biological targets by measuring changes in electrical properties without requiring electrochemical reactions, and addresses their historically limited sensitivity. The authors survey three complementary strategies for improving sensor performance: micro- and nanoparticle-based signal amplification, microfluidic integration to improve analyte transport to sensor surfaces, and CMOS on-chip integration for high spatiotemporal resolution. By combining these approaches, recent platforms have achieved detection limits reaching the femtomolar range for proteins and sensitivity down to single bacteria, representing substantial gains over conventional non-Faradaic methods. The review analyzes the individual strengths and limitations of each strategy alongside their synergistic potential, and outlines emerging directions in materials and system integration. The authors propose a roadmap for translating these advances into practical biosensing platforms for healthcare diagnostics, environmental monitoring, and biomedical research.
items.citation: Nam-Seog Kim, Jungkyu Kim. Advancing non-faradaic impedance biosensors: sensitivity enhancement strategies using microfluidics, multiscale labeling, and CMOS technology. Microsystems & Nanoengineering. 2026

items.title: Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.
items.summary: The study addressed the need for rapid and sensitive detection of *Escherichia coli* in neonatal sepsis, where conventional blood culture is slow and often insufficiently sensitive. Researchers developed a multiple cross-displacement amplification assay coupled with a lateral flow biosensor targeting the *uidA* gene, using a set of ten primers optimized to run at a fixed temperature for forty minutes. The assay achieved femtogram-level analytical sensitivity with no cross-reactivity against non-*E. coli* strains, and the complete workflow from nucleic acid extraction to visual readout was finished within approximately one hour. Clinical validation using sterile body fluid specimens from neonates with suspected *E. coli* infection showed complete agreement with quantitative PCR and substantially higher positivity rates than conventional culture. The authors conclude that this method offers a rapid, sensitive, and cost-effective tool for point-of-care *E. coli* detection, especially suited to resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Xiao R, Zou P, Zhou J et al.. Multiple cross displacement amplification coupled with a lateral flow biosensor for ultra-rapid and highly sensitive detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> in neonatal sepsis.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.
items.summary: The paper investigated a biosensor strategy for detecting *Salmonella typhimurium*, a major foodborne pathogen, at trace levels. The researchers designed a system that couples DNAzyme-catalysed amplification with hybridization chain reaction to convert target recognition into branched DNA nanowires bearing PAM sequences, which then activate CRISPR/Cas12a to cleave the nanowires and restore a quenched fluorescence signal. This cascaded target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment approach achieved an exceptionally low detection limit and a linear range spanning several orders of magnitude in bacterial concentration. The biosensor demonstrated straightforward operation and rapid response, and the authors propose that by swapping the recognition and primer sequences, the platform could be adapted for sensitive detection of other foodborne pathogens.
items.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
items.citation: Liu Y, Yue X, Li B et al.. Target-to-signal conversion and spatial enrichment cascade boost CRISPR/Cas12a biosensing for trace-level pathogen detection.. Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications. 2026

items.title: Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.
items.summary: This study addressed the need for rapid, accurate detection of *Escherichia coli* O157:H7, a major foodborne pathogen, by developing a one-pot CRISPR/Cas13-based biosensor. The system simultaneously targets two key genetic markers of the pathogen by exploiting the distinct collateral cleavage preferences of two different Cas13 proteins, creating dual fluorescence channels that enable serotype-specific identification within a single reaction tube. Target gene amplification via recombinase polymerase amplification, transcription, and CRISPR-mediated sensing were all integrated to eliminate complex equipment and reduce contamination risk. The biosensor achieved high sensitivity in controlled testing and was validated using fecal samples from a mouse infection model, with results consistent with standard PCR methods. The authors claim this dual-channel approach improves specificity and serotype discrimination over conventional CRISPR diagnostics, offering a simple, field-deployable tool for food safety, clinical diagnostics, and infectious disease surveillance.
items.citation: He Y, Lin X, Zhang X et al.. Simultaneous Dual-Gene Detection of <i>Escherichia coli</i> O157:H7 Based on a CRISPR/Cas13-Mediated Biosensor.. JACS Au. 2026

items.title: Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.
items.summary: This paper developed an electrochemical biosensor platform designed for rapid, point-of-care detection of antimicrobial resistance genes and emerging pathogen targets. The sensor uses disposable graphene foam electrodes functionalized with pyrene-modified peptide nucleic acid probes, which are attached via π-π stacking to preserve the material's electronic properties and high surface area without requiring on-surface chemical reactions. A key technical advance was a heat-assisted functionalization protocol that reduced sensor preparation time from many hours to just two minutes while maintaining detection performance. The platform achieved amplification-free and label-free detection of the colistin resistance gene with low picomolar sensitivity against bacterial plasmid targets, clearly discriminating complementary from non-complementary sequences, and was readily retargeted to a different resistance gene by simply swapping the probe. The biosensor demonstrated consistent reproducibility across independently fabricated devices, supporting its potential for scalable manufacture and decentralized diagnostic deployment against antimicrobial resistance and pandemic threats.
items.citation: Wang KY, Schulze H, Lozano Sanchez P et al.. Graphene foam biosensors for molecular diagnostics of antimicrobial resistance and emerging pathogen threats.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Advanced biosensing strategies for high-risk foodborne pathogens: a comprehensive review of <i>Salmonella</i> and <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>.
items.summary: This review examined advances in biosensor technologies specifically designed to detect two major foodborne pathogens, *Salmonella* spp. and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which are among the leading causes of foodborne illness and death globally. Rather than broadly surveying biosensing across many pathogens, the authors conducted a pathogen-specific analysis mapping trends in bioreceptor development and transducer selection for these two organisms. A distinctive contribution is the first examination of how artificial intelligence tools can accelerate biosensor design, optimization, and decision-making specifically for detecting these pathogens. The review also critically evaluates which biosensing strategies hold genuine potential for scalability, portability, and routine deployment in food industry settings, thereby addressing the gap between laboratory development and real-world application. The authors present the work as a practical roadmap intended to guide future biosensor research toward field-ready, industry-relevant detection solutions.
items.citation: Gumush SE, Al-Attar R, Sandbecker E et al.. Advanced biosensing strategies for high-risk foodborne pathogens: a comprehensive review of <i>Salmonella</i> and <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>.. Food chemistry. Molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Deep learning integrated plasmonic electrochemical sensing for fast and accurate pathogen detection.
items.summary: This paper investigated the detection of three bacterial pathogens — *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella typhimurium*, and *Staphylococcus aureus* — using a biosensing platform that combines plasmonic nanomaterials with deep learning-based signal analysis. The researchers fabricated a nanostructured electrochemical biosensor incorporating gold nanoparticle–graphene oxide hybrid nanocomposites to exploit localized surface plasmon resonance and enhance charge-transfer kinetics. Raw voltammetric signals from the sensor were processed by a hybrid deep neural network combining a MobileNet-Transformer architecture for feature extraction with a Gated Recurrent Unit for temporal noise reduction. The integrated system achieved extremely low limits of detection for all three pathogens using only a small sample volume and a rapid assay time, while outperforming baseline convolutional and recurrent neural network models in classification accuracy and discriminative performance. The authors claim this approach offers a scalable, portable, and AI-assisted biosensing solution suitable for food safety, environmental monitoring, and point-of-care diagnostics at performance levels comparable to laboratory benchtop systems.
items.citation: Mansour S, Negm N, Alhashmi AA et al.. Deep learning integrated plasmonic electrochemical sensing for fast and accurate pathogen detection.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field
items.summary: This paper examines the production of dark photons as a dark matter candidate through the perturbative decay of a dark Higgs field that is displaced from its potential minimum during inflation, a mechanism known as stochastic misalignment. The framework is predictive but faces constraints from two sources: structure formation, because the produced dark photons are initially relativistic and thus boosted, and inflationary isocurvature fluctuations, which demand small quartic self-couplings of the dark Higgs. By accounting for these constraints, the authors identify a viable parameter space spanning dark photon masses from hundreds of electron volts to around a gigaelectronvolt and very small gauge couplings consistent with the observed dark matter relic abundance. If kinetic mixing between the dark photon and the Standard Model photon is present at a generic level, this parameter space narrows further and becomes accessible to direct detection experiments and diffuse soft gamma-ray searches, while the broader favored region could be probed by future cosmic microwave background or Lyman-alpha observations.
items.citation: James M. Cline, Gonzalo Herrera, Jean-Samuel Roux. Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
items.summary: This paper studies the computational complexity of planted noisy k-XOR detection and recovery, as well as strong refutation of random k-XOR, focusing on the precise trade-off between the number of clauses, signal strength, and runtime. The authors analyze the Kikuchi hierarchy, a family of spectral algorithms indexed by a level parameter, which was conjectured to achieve a smooth curve relating clause count to runtime but had previously only been shown to do so up to polylogarithmic factors that degrade the running time exponent. By introducing a normalized variant of the Kikuchi matrix and developing sharp combinatorial counts of closed walks in the associated trace expansion, the authors prove that this normalized hierarchy exactly achieves the conjectured sharp trade-off at every arity of three or greater, eliminating all logarithmic losses. Their algorithms accomplish strong detection, weak and exact recovery, and strong refutation with sum-of-squares certificates, and they also establish matching lower bounds in the same model; additionally, a quantum variant yields a quartic speedup for detection and weak recovery. The results extend to more general planting laws and predicates, and the walk-counting techniques developed also resolve a longstanding conjecture on hypergraph Moore bounds.
items.citation: Alexander Schmidhuber, Matthew B. Hastings. The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of fragmented and poorly interoperable fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) systems in HVAC buildings by developing a structured semantic framework. The researchers constructed FDD-ON, a modular and extensible ontology designed to formally represent variable air volume HVAC system components, fault types, symptom statuses, fault impacts, and their interrelationships using well-defined controlled vocabulary. The ontology explicitly encodes contributing cause–fault–symptom–impact relationships to enable machine-interpretable querying of diagnostic knowledge and mapping of heterogeneous FDD outputs across diverse data sources and equipment types. FDD-ON was evaluated using publicly available VAV HVAC system datasets and demonstrated through practical FDD development applications. The authors conclude that FDD-ON provides a foundational semantic framework capable of supporting scalable, transparent, and interoperable FDD solutions, including digital twin frameworks and artificial intelligence-driven maintenance decision-making systems.
items.citation: Yimin Chen, Brian Fricke, Bo Shen et al.. Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Sgoldstino Phenomenology at SND@HL-LHC
items.summary: This paper investigates the prospects for detecting light scalar sgoldstinos — hypothetical particles arising from supersymmetry breaking — at the SND@HL-LHC experiment. The study covers the mass range from the dimuon threshold up to a few GeV, examining effective sgoldstino interactions with Standard Model particles, dominant production mechanisms through meson decays, and existing experimental constraints on the relevant parameter space. The authors analyze the geometry and kinematics of the proposed SND@HL-LHC detector, paying particular attention to the spatial separation of muon–antimuon pairs produced when sgoldstinos decay within the detector volume. Using two representative sets of supersymmetry-breaking parameters, they derive sensitivity estimates for the experiment. A key finding is that the efficiency with which the detector can resolve the two muon tracks must be carefully accounted for when designing or interpreting dimuon signal searches.
items.citation: D. Kalashnikov, E. K. Karkaryan. Sgoldstino Phenomenology at SND@HL-LHC. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CodeShrink: Adaptive Visual Compression for Efficient Multimodal Code Understanding
items.summary: This paper investigated how to reduce the computational cost of processing source code as images in multimodal large language models, where rendering code visually is appealing but wastes tokens on blank space and irrelevant content. The authors developed CodeShrink, a framework combining three components: a blank-free rendering approach that replaces whitespace-heavy layouts with compact representations, a reinforcement learning-trained agent that selects an optimal compression configuration per input, and an instruction-aware mechanism that prunes visual tokens irrelevant to the current task during inference. The framework was evaluated on code question answering, clone detection, and code completion benchmarks. CodeShrink achieved substantial reductions in visual token usage while matching or surpassing uncompressed text-only baselines and outperforming other text-based and visual compression methods across all tasks. The results demonstrate that combining layout compaction, adaptive configuration selection, and instruction-guided token pruning can make multimodal code understanding substantially more efficient.
items.citation: Wenxin Tang, Jingyu Xiao, Zhenyu Liu et al.. CodeShrink: Adaptive Visual Compression for Efficient Multimodal Code Understanding. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Unwithered Majorana fermions in the bulk of a quantum chain
items.summary: The paper investigates Majorana modes in a quantum spin chain when its parameters are tuned to lie along special parametric curves called disorder lines, where the ground state becomes disentangled and certain correlation functions lose their dependence on spatial separation. Using exact results for the XY spin chain in a transverse field, also known as the Kitaev chain in the Majorana representation, the study examines how Majorana modes behave in this disentangled regime. Single Majorana modes are found to remain localized near the ends of the chain, consistent with behavior away from the disorder lines, but multi-particle Majorana modes with two or more particles penetrate into the bulk without any attenuation — a phenomenon the authors call "unwithered" modes. These bulk-edge effects, arising from the interplay between disentanglement and Majorana physics, are predicted to be experimentally detectable in specially engineered optical chains and lattices.
items.citation: Gennady Y. Chitov. Unwithered Majorana fermions in the bulk of a quantum chain. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results.
items.summary: This study examined the clinical utility and economic implications of syndromic multiplex-PCR panel testing for acute infections across four anatomical syndromes over a nearly two-year period at a southern Italian hospital. Researchers retrospectively analysed all meningitis/encephalitis, upper respiratory, pneumonia, and gastrointestinal panel determinations, removing duplicate episodes to ensure each record represented a distinct diagnostic event. Nearly three-fifths of all determinations returned entirely negative results, with a striking variation by panel type: the meningitis/encephalitis and gastrointestinal panels were overwhelmingly negative, indicating substantial over-utilisation, while the pneumonia panel showed the highest diagnostic yield. Key findings included the dominance of viral pathogens in central nervous system infections, rhinovirus/enterovirus predominance in respiratory specimens, clustering of antimicrobial resistance markers in Enterobacterales co-infections on the pneumonia panel, and a surveillance gap created by failure to refer non-subtypeable influenza A specimens for sequencing. The authors recommend a series of stewardship interventions including gating criteria for cerebrospinal fluid and gastrointestinal testing, tiered respiratory algorithms, and mandatory reflex sequencing for unsubtypeable influenza A to address avoidable costs and zoonotic surveillance blind spots.
items.citation: Chirizzi D, Spedicato A, Bianco G et al.. Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results.. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.
items.summary: This study examined how the lifting of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions affected the detection patterns of respiratory pathogens in children presenting with fever or respiratory symptoms at a hospital in Guangzhou, subtropical southern China. Researchers retrospectively analyzed nasopharyngeal swabs from children tested using a consistent twelve-pathogen multiplex PCR panel, conducting a season-matched comparison between equivalent months before and after restrictions were lifted to minimize seasonal bias. Following the lifting of restrictions, detection rates of Influenza A, RSV, and human rhinovirus increased substantially in the season-matched comparison, while Influenza B and human metapneumovirus declined markedly. The post-restriction cohort also included a higher proportion of infants and greater rates of fever, wheezing, and lower respiratory tract diagnoses, though these clinical differences require cautious interpretation given potential changes in healthcare-seeking behavior and admission thresholds. The authors conclude that ongoing multiplex surveillance and age-targeted prevention strategies are warranted, while emphasizing that causal attribution to the lifting of restrictions is complicated by residual confounding from seasonality, SARS-CoV-2 circulation, and shifting healthcare utilization patterns.
items.citation: Hua L, Liang W, Li W et al.. Season-matched comparison of pediatric respiratory pathogen detection patterns before and after the lifting of COVID-19 restrictions in Guangzhou.. Frontiers in pediatrics. 2026

items.title: Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).
items.summary: This study investigated the causes of severe acute respiratory infections among hospitalized adults in northern Thailand during the post-COVID-19 pandemic period. Researchers retrospectively analyzed respiratory samples from adult patients admitted to a regional hospital in Chiang Mai with SARI symptoms, testing specimens using multiplex real-time PCR capable of detecting a broad panel of respiratory pathogens. Nearly half of patients tested positive for at least one respiratory pathogen, with adenovirus and rhinovirus being the most commonly identified viruses, and co-infections present in a notable proportion of cases. Seasonal patterns were observed, with influenza A and rhinovirus peaking in January while adenovirus and enterovirus circulated consistently throughout the study period. The authors conclude that the high rate of empiric antibiotic use underscores the need for broader and more rapid molecular diagnostics, and that enhanced pathogen-specific surveillance is essential for guiding evidence-based clinical management in the post-pandemic era.
items.citation: Kham-Kjing N, Kawila R, Tariyo P et al.. Etiology of severe acute respiratory infections among adults in northern Thailand using multiplex PCR: A post-COVID-19 surveillance study (2023-2024).. PloS one. 2026

items.title: VisPan: real-time visualisation of multiplex amplicon-based sequencing panels for rapid syndromic surveillance and pathogen detection.
items.summary: This paper addresses the bioinformatics bottleneck in real-time pathogen detection using Oxford Nanopore sequencing combined with multiplex PCR syndromic panels. The authors developed a visualisation tool adapted from existing RAMPART software that processes raw sequencing data and performs taxonomic assignment within minutes, providing dynamic tracking of sequencing runs and amplicon coverage through an interactive interface. Validation experiments using complex clinical and environmental samples demonstrated that the system reliably and accurately identified all pathogens present. The tool is designed to be accessible and user-friendly for deployment in both field and clinical settings, supporting rapid syndromic surveillance and outbreak management.
items.citation: Lechat P, Kwasiborski A, Vincent R et al.. VisPan: real-time visualisation of multiplex amplicon-based sequencing panels for rapid syndromic surveillance and pathogen detection.. Bioinformatics (Oxford, England). 2026

items.title: Performance evaluation of the BioFire respiratory panel 2.1 plus and exploratory analysis of Ct values for respiratory pathogen quantification.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of the BioFire FilmArray RP2.1 plus, a multiplex PCR panel capable of detecting twenty respiratory pathogens, and explored whether its cycle threshold values could serve as a semi-quantitative measure of pathogen load. Using retrospectively collected specimens, including serially diluted samples, the panel was compared against established commercial and in-house real-time PCR assays across hundreds of individual PCR results. The BioFire RP2.1 plus showed excellent qualitative agreement with comparator methods, with most discordant results occurring in specimens containing low pathogen loads and involving pathogens such as Bordetella pertussis and influenza viruses. Exploratory analyses revealed strong correlations between BioFire-derived cycle threshold values and those from reference assays, suggesting a reproducible quantitative relationship across platforms. However, the authors caution that the semi-quantitative findings should be interpreted carefully given the exploratory study design and the inherent challenges of cross-platform comparisons.
items.venue: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
items.citation: Vitale A, Mahler Z, Loup V et al.. Performance evaluation of the BioFire respiratory panel 2.1 plus and exploratory analysis of Ct values for respiratory pathogen quantification.. European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Standardization of a quantitative multiplex real-time PCR system for the detection of bovine respiratory disease pathogens in clinical samples of dairy cattle from southern Brazil.
items.summary: This study addressed the diagnostic challenge of bovine respiratory disease, a economically important syndrome caused by multiple interacting pathogens, by developing and validating a multiplex quantitative real-time PCR platform capable of simultaneously detecting ten viral and bacterial agents in a single assay panel. The researchers standardized the system using rigorous analytical performance testing, including standard curve analysis, repeatability, and reproducibility assessments across single and multiplex configurations, before applying it to nasal swab samples from dairy cattle in southern Brazil. Field application revealed that the majority of sampled cattle tested positive for at least one pathogen, with bacterial agents dominating detections and singular infections being the most common pattern, though complex multi-pathogen combinations were also identified. Pathogen occurrence was significantly associated with animal age, season, and farm-level factors, with specific pathogens showing distinct epidemiological distributions across these variables. The study presents this platform as the first validated multiplex quantitative PCR system for bovine respiratory disease diagnostics in Brazil, offering a more efficient and cost-effective tool for understanding the epidemiology and pathogenesis of this syndrome in the region.
items.citation: Rodriguez MC, Silva IV, Perotta JH et al.. Standardization of a quantitative multiplex real-time PCR system for the detection of bovine respiratory disease pathogens in clinical samples of dairy cattle from southern Brazil.. Journal of microbiological methods. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review paper examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, commonly known as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their applications in laboratory medicine. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of innovations in chip design and fabrication, including developments such as three-dimensional printing and flexible substrates, alongside the integration of advanced biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the creation of smart diagnostic platforms with capabilities for self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support. The review covers clinical applications spanning cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, personalized medicine, and emerging areas such as neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The authors also address ongoing challenges in manufacturing, clinical validation, and system integration, while outlining future directions for translating these technologies into routine clinical and public health practice.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Interplay of Microbiome, Oxidative Stress and Inflammation in Health and Disease
items.summary: This review examines the complex relationships among the human microbiome, oxidative stress, and inflammation in the context of both health and disease. The authors synthesize current evidence on how microbial metabolites and specific probiotic strains help maintain redox homeostasis through pathways involving immune regulation, inflammatory modulation, and antioxidant signaling. Conversely, oxidative stress and inflammation can reshape the microbiome by altering its diversity and functional capacity. These bidirectional interactions are proposed to form a self-reinforcing cycle in which disruptions to any component further destabilize homeostasis and contribute to disease development. The review underscores that a fuller understanding of this tripartite interplay is essential for explaining both physiological states and the pathogenesis of various conditions.
items.citation: Lourdes Herrera-Quintana, Pablo Iturbe-Sanz, Jorge Olivares-Arancibia et al.. Interplay of Microbiome, Oxidative Stress and Inflammation in Health and Disease. Antioxidants. 2026

items.title: STING controls glycolysis and histone lactylation to drive macrophage metabolic reprogramming in postoperative ileus
items.summary: The paper investigated how the innate immune signaling protein STING shapes macrophage metabolism and inflammatory polarization in the context of postoperative ileus, a condition marked by intestinal motility disruption driven by excessive muscular layer inflammation. Using LPS-stimulated macrophages and STING knockout cells, the researchers examined the relationship between STING signaling, glycolysis, and epigenetic regulation. They found that STING promotes glycolysis by stabilizing HIF1α, which drives lactate production and subsequent histone lactylation at the hexokinase 2 gene locus, thereby increasing chromatin accessibility. CUT&Tag sequencing further identified IRF3 as a transcription factor that binds the hexokinase 2 promoter in a manner dependent on this lactylation, creating a self-reinforcing glycolytic feedback loop that sustains pro-inflammatory macrophage activity. The study concludes that targeting STING to disrupt this metabolic-epigenetic circuit may represent a therapeutic strategy to reduce macrophage-driven inflammation and improve recovery following surgery.
items.citation: Kai Chen, Guofang Li, Ye Cheng et al.. STING controls glycolysis and histone lactylation to drive macrophage metabolic reprogramming in postoperative ileus. Communications Biology. 2026

items.title: Genomic analysis of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from Antarctica reveals multiple introductions from South America
items.summary: This study investigated the spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b into Antarctica, where it poses a serious threat to endemic wildlife. Researchers detected the virus in carcasses of eight species across the South Shetland Islands during two consecutive austral summers, encompassing both seabirds and marine mammals. Whole-genome sequencing, mutational profiling, and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the viral strains and reconstruct their origins. The analyses revealed at least two independent introduction events into Antarctica, with one viral lineage linked to H5N1 strains circulating in marine mammals along the South American coast and another lineage connected to strains previously detected in South Georgia. These findings demonstrate substantial epidemiological connectivity between South America and Antarctica, with South Georgia appearing to function as an intermediate stepping stone in the southward spread of the virus.
items.citation: Maria Ogrzewalska, Ralph Eric Thijl Vanstreels, Elisa Cavalcante Pereira et al.. Genomic analysis of high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses from Antarctica reveals multiple introductions from South America. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations
items.summary: The paper examines the dual nature of *Enterococcus* species as both potentially beneficial microorganisms and safety concerns, focusing on their roles in the gastrointestinal tract, food systems, and healthcare contexts. The authors conducted a comprehensive review synthesizing current knowledge on the probiotic properties, antimicrobial potential, and safety profiles of beneficial enterococci. These bacteria have demonstrated value as protective cultures and antibiotic alternatives, capable of controlling pathogens, modulating the microbiome, supporting food fermentation, and producing bioactive compounds such as bacteriocins with pathogen-inhibitory activity. However, their association with healthcare-associated infections and their capacity to spread antimicrobial resistance genes present significant safety concerns that complicate their wider application. The review concludes that rigorous safety evaluations are essential before enterococci can be reliably deployed as probiotics, antibiotic alternatives, or protective cultures in agrifood and clinical settings.
items.citation: Ojonugwa Precious John, Kayode Olayinka Afolabi, Anayochukwu Chibuike Ngene et al.. Enterococcus Species: Multifaceted Probiotic Potential and Safety Considerations. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Overcoming host restrictions to enable continuous passaging of GII.3 human norovirus in human intestinal enteroids
items.summary: This paper investigated the challenge of continuously propagating human norovirus in human intestinal enteroids, a model system that has previously required fresh patient stool samples as viral inocula because indefinite passaging was not achievable. Using RNA sequencing, the researchers identified specific chemokines as upregulated host restriction factors and tested whether blocking their receptors could enhance viral replication. Treatment with TAK-779, an antagonist targeting chemokine receptors CXCR3, CCR5, and CCR2, enabled successful serial passaging of a GII.3 human norovirus strain in two different enteroid lines and allowed generation of viral stocks, with sequencing revealing both a consensus capsid protein change and emergence of viral variants over passage. The compound also enhanced replication of other norovirus strains in a strain-specific manner, suggesting that distinct host-pathogen interactions govern different genotypes. This advance establishes a scalable in vitro propagation system for human norovirus and is expected to facilitate structural, biochemical, and antiviral therapeutic research.
items.citation: Gurpreet Kaur, Sue Crawford, Sara Javornik Cregeen et al.. Overcoming host restrictions to enable continuous passaging of GII.3 human norovirus in human intestinal enteroids. Science Advances. 2026

items.title: FriendBench: Benchmarking Dyadic Familiarity Inference in Humans and Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces FriendBench, a benchmark designed to test whether humans and multimodal large language models can infer from brief video clips whether two people in a dyadic conversation already know each other or are meeting for the first time. Because every pair responds to identical prompts, only behavioral cues rather than content can drive correct judgments. A large set of models spanning text, audio, and video modalities was compared against human panels across balanced dyads. The top-performing models matched human crowd accuracy statistically across all modalities, yet the two groups reached similar performance differently: humans distributed their responses evenly between the two answer categories, while the strongest models showed a systematic bias toward predicting strangers, suggesting a difference in implicit prior rather than discriminative ability. Notably, adding visual information to speech improved performance for humans but not for models, revealing a gap in how the two types of agents exploit multimodal behavioral signals.
items.citation: Jeffrey M. Girard, Jason Z. Zheng, Jacqueline R. Vertino et al.. FriendBench: Benchmarking Dyadic Familiarity Inference in Humans and Multimodal Large Language Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: DynoDINO: Harnessing Dynamic Latent Information from DINO Features for Multi-Phase Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: DynoDINO addresses the problem of accurately segmenting lesions in multi-phase contrast-enhanced computed tomography, where clinically meaningful enhancement patterns are spread across acquisition phases but inter-phase misalignment and missing data complicate analysis. The authors developed a unified framework that first performs slice-level alignment to establish anatomical correspondence between phases, then applies a Multi-phase Fusion Model that combines a Mix-attention mechanism with an Adaptive Gating Mechanism using difference-based residual learning. The Adaptive Gating Mechanism is designed to selectively retain diagnostically relevant contrast variations while suppressing artifacts from residual misalignment and preventing feature degradation during training. The framework was evaluated on three large-scale datasets covering liver tumors and related clinical scenarios under standard, phase-shifted, and missing-phase conditions. Results demonstrate that DynoDINO consistently improves boundary delineation and structural fidelity compared to conventional approaches that process phases independently or use simple fusion strategies.
items.citation: Yu-Pu Hsu, Jen-Jee Chen, Yu-Chee Tseng. DynoDINO: Harnessing Dynamic Latent Information from DINO Features for Multi-Phase Medical Image Segmentation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multi-User MIMO Enhancement using Metasurface Wavefront Bending (MWB)
items.summary: This paper investigates the use of metasurface wavefront bending to improve spatial multiplexing performance in radiative near-field multi-user MIMO systems. The core idea is that by increasing spherical-wave curvature, the metasurface strengthens range-dependent phase variations across receiver arrays, which reduces correlation between different users' channels and makes them easier to separate. The authors developed a curvature-dependent channel analysis framework, a synthesis procedure based on generalized sheet transition conditions, and a complete channel model incorporating the metasurface. Both a practical common-profile design and an ideal user-specific benchmark were evaluated, with results showing substantial gains in spectral efficiency and effective channel rank. A three-layer transmissive Huygens metasurface architecture was also proposed as a physically realizable implementation of the approach.
items.citation: Xiaolu Yang, Oscar Cespedes Vicente, Christophe Caloz. Multi-User MIMO Enhancement using Metasurface Wavefront Bending (MWB). arXiv. 2026

items.title: ALIVE: Warnings Before Exclusion in Budgeted Multi-Source Learning
items.summary: This paper studied how to responsibly authorize irreversible source exclusions versus reversible routing decisions in multi-source machine learning systems operating under a shared finite audit budget. The authors developed ALIVE, a control framework that separates non-persistent routing actions guided by heuristic warnings from persistent source exclusions that require stronger simultaneous certificate-based evidence, all governed by a randomized without-replacement auditing prefix. Under fixed support and label conditions, the framework provides an anytime familywise error bound on incorrectly acting against sources that satisfy a strict-majority-disagreement predicate. Empirical results showed that the persistent-action layer improved accuracy over routing-only approaches, though the full-system improvement against a case-based reasoning baseline did not meet the pre-specified multiplicity-adjusted significance threshold. The work frames the overall contribution as mapping a boundary among restraint, statistical power, audit cost, and downstream utility in budgeted multi-source learning.
items.citation: Xiyang Zhang, Hongzhi Wang, Yuanhe Tian. ALIVE: Warnings Before Exclusion in Budgeted Multi-Source Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: DualDiT: A Conditional Dual-Output Diffusion Transformer for Joint OCT Image and Segmentation Mask Generation
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of scarce annotated data in optical coherence tomography imaging of mouse retinas by developing a method to jointly synthesize realistic OCT images alongside anatomically accurate segmentation masks. The authors proposed DualDiT, a conditional dual-output Diffusion Transformer that encodes both image and mask modalities into a shared latent space using a pretrained variational autoencoder, then performs conditional diffusion over their concatenated latent representations. DualDiT was compared against U-Net-based diffusion baselines including a denoising diffusion probabilistic model and a latent diffusion model, with evaluation spanning generative quality metrics, segmentation performance when used for data augmentation, and perceptual realism assessed by domain experts. The transformer-based approach outperformed both baselines on generative fidelity metrics, and expert reviewers were unable to reliably distinguish synthetic from real samples, misclassifying each category at roughly comparable rates. Incorporating the synthetically generated image-mask pairs into training improved downstream segmentation scores, demonstrating the practical utility of DualDiT for alleviating annotation scarcity in medical imaging.
items.citation: Fernando García-Torres, Rocío del Amor, Sandra Morales et al.. DualDiT: A Conditional Dual-Output Diffusion Transformer for Joint OCT Image and Segmentation Mask Generation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Bistatic Integrated Sensing and Communications with Flexible Intelligent Metasurfaces
items.summary: The paper proposes a new channel model for integrated sensing and communications systems that incorporates flexible intelligent metasurfaces in high-mobility, doubly-dispersive environments using multiple-input multiple-output architectures. The authors extend this model to three multicarrier waveforms known to handle doubly-dispersive channels well, and formulate an achievable rate maximization problem subject to a sensing constraint, solving it through gradient ascent with closed-form gradients. Numerical results demonstrate that flexible intelligent metasurfaces substantially influence achievable communication rates, and that careful parameterization of the metasurface is critical for strong joint sensing and communication performance across all examined waveforms.
items.citation: Iván Alexander Morales Sandoval, Thushar Venkataramanaiah, Kuranage Roche Rayan Ranasinghe et al.. Bistatic Integrated Sensing and Communications with Flexible Intelligent Metasurfaces. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.
items.summary: This study evaluated a field-deployable serological test for detecting Usutu virus and West Nile virus antibodies in wild birds at bird-ringing sites in the Netherlands, where both viruses are of increasing public health concern. The researchers used a species-independent Lateral Flow Microarray ImmunoAssay capable of simultaneously detecting antibodies against both viruses, testing it on wild birds captured in the field and comparing results against the gold-standard neutralization test. The assay demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for Usutu virus detection, and successfully identified seroconversion in a Eurasian blackbird, which was independently confirmed by the reference method. Performance was also assessed using the WHO REASSURED framework, where the assay achieved a high proportion of the maximum possible score, indicating strong suitability for point-of-capture use. The authors conclude that the assay is feasible for on-site arbovirus surveillance in wild birds, particularly in resource-limited or field settings, though further optimization and broader validation are recommended.
items.citation: Godarzi B, Holicki CM, Chandler FD et al.. On-site serological screening of Usutu virus in wild birds: Field evaluation of a lateral flow microarray immunoassay using the WHO REASSURED framework.. Journal of virological methods. 2026

items.title: Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper investigated how the orientation of antibodies on gold nanoparticles affects the performance of lateral flow immunoassays used in point-of-care diagnostics. The researchers developed a one-pot, room-temperature method to synthesize phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles at large scale, producing uniform nanoparticles in substantial batch volumes within minutes. Unlike conventional citrate-capped gold nanoparticles, which rely on random antibody adsorption, the new particles exploit boronate-affinity interactions with carbohydrate moieties on antibody Fc fragments to achieve controlled, oriented antibody immobilization that keeps antigen-binding sites accessible. When tested for fecal occult blood detection, the functionalized nanoparticles demonstrated dramatically improved sensitivity compared to conventional citrate-capped counterparts. The authors conclude that this scalable synthesis approach offers a practical and cost-effective nanoplatform with strong potential for clinical translation into high-sensitivity diagnostic applications.
items.citation: Xu J, Li Q, Lu B et al.. Large-scale synthesis of phenylboronic acid-functionalized gold nanoparticles enables an oriented antibody interface for sensitive point-of-care diagnostics.. Colloids and surfaces. B, Biointerfaces. 2026

items.title: Dual-enhancement lateral flow immunoassay <i>via</i> gold-decorated ferritin nanoprobes and SpyTag/SpyCatcher site-directed conjugation.
items.summary: This paper addressed the limited sensitivity of conventional lateral flow immunoassays, which are hampered by weak optical signals, randomly oriented antibodies, and inconsistent nanoprobe production. The researchers developed a dual-enhancement approach combining gold-decorated ferritin nanocages with SpyTag/SpyCatcher chemistry, where engineered ferritin served as a uniform template for gold nanocluster growth while simultaneously presenting SpyTag peptides for site-directed, covalent antibody attachment. The gold deposition produced highly uniform core-shell nanostructures with amplified optical signal, and the oriented antibody conjugation markedly improved antigen-binding capacity compared to conventional random adsorption. Testing the system against human chorionic gonadotropin as a model target, the optimized assay achieved a limit of detection far lower than commercial gold nanoparticle-based strips, with strong linearity and reliable performance in urine samples. The authors conclude that this synergistic strategy offers a versatile route to substantially improving the sensitivity of point-of-care diagnostic platforms.
items.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
items.citation: Yuan X, Zhu X, Xu Y et al.. Dual-enhancement lateral flow immunoassay <i>via</i> gold-decorated ferritin nanoprobes and SpyTag/SpyCatcher site-directed conjugation.. Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications. 2026

items.title: Ag-rich Ag-Au nanoshells based lateral flow immunoassay for rapid and sensitive detection of bovine viral diarrhea virus.
items.citation: Ding Y, Zhang W, Huang Y et al.. Ag-rich Ag-Au nanoshells based lateral flow immunoassay for rapid and sensitive detection of bovine viral diarrhea virus.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: First implementation of a polymer-polymer aqueous two-phase system to improve lateral-flow immunoassay sensitivity via dextranase integration on paper.
items.summary: This paper investigated whether a polymer-polymer aqueous two-phase system (ATPS) could be integrated with lateral-flow immunoassays (LFAs) to improve their detection sensitivity, which is a known limitation of these otherwise widely used point-of-care diagnostics. The researchers used a poly(ethylene glycol)-dextran ATPS to preconcentrate protein targets into the dextran-rich phase, but had to overcome the problem of that phase's high viscosity preventing adequate fluid flow on the LFA membrane. To solve this, they introduced the enzyme dextranase to degrade the dextran polymer after preconcentration, reducing viscosity and restoring proper sample flow, and they further simplified the approach by dehydrating dextranase directly onto the LFA paper strip to minimize manual handling steps. Testing with the model protein transferrin spiked into artificial saliva demonstrated a tenfold improvement in the limit of detection compared to a conventional LFA. This work represents the first successful coupling of a polymer-polymer ATPS with an LFA platform, expanding the range of phase systems available for enhancing point-of-care assay sensitivity.
items.venue: Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry
items.citation: Nicklen FD, Hadeed CH, Zhang F et al.. First implementation of a polymer-polymer aqueous two-phase system to improve lateral-flow immunoassay sensitivity via dextranase integration on paper.. Analytical sciences : the international journal of the Japan Society for Analytical Chemistry. 2026

items.title: Self-Contained Lateral-Flow Microfluidic Bead-Based Assay for Rapid Quantification of Early-Stage Kidney Biomarkers.
items.summary: This paper developed a rapid, self-contained diagnostic system for detecting early-stage kidney disease biomarkers at the point of care. The researchers created the lateral-flow microfluidic bead-based assay, which integrates a microfluidic chip with paper-based components to automate immunoassays for two kidney biomarkers, neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and cystatin C, completing analysis in under half an hour from a very small blood or urine sample. The platform's modular design separates reagent storage and flow control from the binding and readout steps, providing design flexibility and enabling decentralized use outside centralized laboratories. Validated against standard laboratory ELISA methods, the system demonstrated comparable sensitivity with an extended dynamic range, and was successfully applied to neonatal mouse models of polycystic kidney disease, where biomarker elevations consistent with cyst progression were detected. The authors propose this scalable platform as a tool for preclinical research and decentralized clinical diagnostics of kidney disease.
items.citation: Porro G, Cristofori MS, Gagnieux C et al.. Self-Contained Lateral-Flow Microfluidic Bead-Based Assay for Rapid Quantification of Early-Stage Kidney Biomarkers.. Analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, including *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which remain persistent threats to global public health. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing platforms, emphasizing how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering have substantially improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into these platforms, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexing that transform conventional detection systems into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically assesses practical challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, scalability limitations, and the absence of regulatory standardization, while proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, and explainable AI frameworks. Looking ahead, the authors advocate for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen detection panels, blockchain-enabled traceability, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward deployable, regulation-ready food safety monitoring platforms.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, commonly called lab-on-a-chip systems, and their expanding role in laboratory medicine. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of innovations in chip design and fabrication, including developments such as three-dimensional printing and flexible modular substrates, alongside progress in biosensor integration for detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the creation of smart diagnostic platforms capable of automated analysis, self-optimization, and clinical decision support. These combined technologies show broad applicability across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, personalized medicine, and emerging areas such as neuroscience and microbiome profiling. The review also addresses persistent challenges in manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration that must be overcome to translate these technologies into routine clinical and public health use.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Analysis of the antimicrobial activity of zinc oxide nanoparticles against drug-resistant bacteria and their applications in the disinfection process
items.summary: Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs) were investigated as a potential antimicrobial agent against drug-resistant bacteria and for use in disinfection applications. The nanoparticles were synthesized using an eco-friendly method combining Phoenix dactylifera root extract with zinc acetate, then characterized and tested against a range of bacterial and fungal isolates through multiple assays, including evaluation against acid-fast bacilli and assessment of disinfection efficacy on water samples and surfaces. ZnO-NPs demonstrated broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms, with Gram-positive bacteria showing greater susceptibility, and MRSA producing the largest inhibition zone. The nanoparticles also achieved complete elimination of bacteria from laboratory surfaces within a short contact time and showed bactericidal effects against acid-fast bacilli isolates. The authors conclude that ZnO-NPs hold strong promise as versatile antimicrobial and disinfection agents for use against multidrug-resistant pathogens in both clinical and environmental contexts, and suggest future work explore their combination with conventional antimicrobials.
items.citation: Dalia Alqaffaf, Ali M. Atoom, Rana Abu Huwaij et al.. Analysis of the antimicrobial activity of zinc oxide nanoparticles against drug-resistant bacteria and their applications in the disinfection process. PLoS ONE. 2026

items.title: Electrochemical Biosensors for Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis Using Protein Biomarkers: Current Trends, Advances, and Clinical Translation Potential
items.summary: This review examines the use of electrochemical biosensors for detecting blood-circulating protein biomarkers in the context of cancer diagnosis and prognosis, with a particular focus on liquid biopsy approaches. The authors surveyed general strategies for electrochemical detection of serum proteins and catalogued recent advances in biosensor designs targeting cancer-related proteins, noting that many have demonstrated strong analytical sensitivity. The review critically evaluates the obstacles hindering clinical translation and commercialization, including matrix effects from complex biological samples, insufficient validation with real patient samples, interpatient variability, and practical challenges around manufacturing, cost, and long-term stability. Special emphasis is placed on the importance of rigorous preanalytical and analytical standardization, as well as the need for robust clinical validation frameworks to bridge the gap between laboratory performance and real-world diagnostic utility.
items.citation: Michael E. J. Lopez Mujica, Elena E. Ferapontova. Electrochemical Biosensors for Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis Using Protein Biomarkers: Current Trends, Advances, and Clinical Translation Potential. Sensors. 2026

items.title: Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives
items.summary: This review paper examined the dual role of reactive oxygen species in biological systems, where they act as essential signaling molecules at physiological levels but drive disease pathology when produced in excess or dysregulated. The authors synthesized current knowledge on the major types, sources, and physiological functions of reactive oxygen species, alongside the molecular pathways through which oxidative stress causes cellular damage and signaling disruption. The review also critically evaluated contemporary and emerging methods for detecting and quantifying oxidative stress in clinical and preclinical settings, including biochemical assays, fluorescent probes, biosensors, and advanced imaging techniques. The contribution of oxidative stress to a range of major disorders — including cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and inflammatory conditions — was examined. The authors conclude by advocating for precision redox medicine, emphasizing that advances in detection technologies combined with deeper mechanistic understanding could enable more targeted antioxidant-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
items.citation: Shehwaz Anwar, Hajed Obaid A. Alharbi, Ali Yousif Babiker et al.. Oxidative Stress in Health and Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Perspectives. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Spherical Nucleic Acids: Turning Synthetic Advances and Fundamental Discovery into Translational Breakthroughs in Chemistry, Materials Development, Biology, and Medicine
items.summary: Spherical nucleic acids (SNAs) are nanoconstructs composed of a nanoparticle core densely functionalized with a radially oriented shell of oligonucleotides, and this review examines their development over roughly three decades as a case study in how synthetic control and fundamental discovery drive translational innovation. The authors trace the evolution of SNAs from their origin as gold nanoparticle–DNA conjugates through the creation of dozens of SNA classes with tailored properties, including enhanced binding affinity to complementary DNA, resistance to enzymatic degradation, reduced immune activation, and efficient cellular uptake without transfection agents. These properties have enabled SNAs to function as intracellular and extracellular probes, gene regulation tools, vaccines, and gene editing platforms, particularly when coupled with CRISPR technology. In parallel, SNAs serve as programmable building blocks for DNA-mediated colloidal crystals, where sequence-specific interactions organize them into three-dimensional periodic structures with thousands of possible lattice variations, yielding materials with unusual optical and mechanical properties such as negative refractive indices and shape memory. The review presents SNAs as a broad framework illustrating how mastery of nanoscale synthesis and the uncovering of novel fundamental phenomena together catalyze advances across chemistry, biology, materials science, and medicine.
items.citation: Connor M. Forsyth, Rachel R. Chan, Tanner D. Fink et al.. Spherical Nucleic Acids: Turning Synthetic Advances and Fundamental Discovery into Translational Breakthroughs in Chemistry, Materials Development, Biology, and Medicine. Accounts of Chemical Research. 2026

items.title: Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents
items.summary: This paper investigated whether procedural knowledge accumulated from past software repairs could be systematically reused to improve the performance of large language model-driven coding agents on new repository-level issues. The authors developed STAIR, a framework that transforms historical repair trajectories into hierarchical, multi-level tree structures encoding experience at granularities ranging from fine-grained diagnostic actions to high-level repair strategies. When a new issue is encountered, STAIR retrieves relevant nodes from these abstraction hierarchies, adapts them into issue-specific executable plans, and injects them into the agent's prompt. The framework achieved strong performance on a standard software engineering benchmark and demonstrated cross-agent generalizability, improving a structurally different agent without any code modifications. Ablation studies confirmed that combining multiple abstraction levels outperforms using any single level, and that raw, unprocessed trajectories transfer substantially less effectively than the hierarchically abstracted plans.
items.citation: Yisen Xu, Jiayuan Zhou, Ruiqi Pan et al.. Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of fragmented knowledge representation in fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) for HVAC systems, where heterogeneous data sources and varied diagnostic outputs impede effective implementation. The authors developed FDD-ON, a modular and extensible ontology that formally represents variable air volume HVAC system components, fault types, symptom statuses, fault impacts, and their interrelationships through explicit cause-fault-symptom-impact chains. The ontology integrates controlled vocabulary and comprehensive fault, symptom, and impact libraries to make diagnostic knowledge machine-interpretable and interoperable across different FDD applications, including digital twin frameworks and AI-driven maintenance systems. FDD-ON was evaluated using publicly available VAV HVAC datasets and demonstrated through practical FDD development applications. The authors claim that FDD-ON establishes a foundational semantic framework capable of supporting scalable, transparent, and interoperable FDD solutions across diverse building system contexts.
items.citation: Yimin Chen, Brian Fricke, Bo Shen et al.. Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Elastic Curves via Geometric Mechanics
items.summary: The paper investigates elastic curves — the equilibrium shapes of thin elastic rods — by reinterpreting their theory through the lens of geometric mechanics rather than classical variational methods based on bending energy. The central insight is a lesser-known isoperimetric characterization, whereby a curve is elastic if and only if it is a critical point of arc length while holding fixed certain area and volume vector quantities. The authors show that these constraints transform naturally under orientation-preserving rigid body motions and can therefore be identified as momentum variables associated with those symmetries. Exploiting this structure, they construct a discrete theory for polygonal curves in which length, area, and volume vectors are all naturally defined and satisfy the same transformation laws exactly, yielding a definition of discrete elastic curves that is variational and structure-preserving without requiring any auxiliary discretization of curvature or material frames. The framework also carries the Marsden–Weinstein pre-symplectic structure to polygonal curves, opening new avenues for Hamiltonian dynamics on discrete space curves including tangent, vortex-filament, and modified Korteweg–de Vries flows.
items.citation: Oliver Gross, Rohit Jammula, Albert Chern. Elastic Curves via Geometric Mechanics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Revealing the Spin Hydrodynamics of a Spin-Imbalanced Unitary Fermi Gas
items.summary: This paper investigates spin transport in the hydrodynamic regime of strongly interacting quantum matter, a phenomenon that remains poorly understood despite the broader success of hydrodynamic frameworks in describing collective behavior across physical systems. The researchers used a spin-imbalanced unitary Fermi gas held in a uniform optical box trap and introduced a spatially periodic optical potential to simultaneously modulate density and spin polarization. By suddenly switching off this potential and observing the subsequent many-body relaxation, they extracted both the spin diffusivity and the spin Seebeck and Peltier coefficients of a homogeneous quantum gas. The results yield parameter-free benchmarks that microscopic theories can be directly tested against, and demonstrate that ultracold atomic systems can serve as a platform for studying spin caloritronics in strongly correlated matter.
items.citation: DeChao Zhang, Johannes Lang, J. E. Thomas. Revealing the Spin Hydrodynamics of a Spin-Imbalanced Unitary Fermi Gas. arXiv. 2026
