items.citation: Irena Padniuk, Xianzhe Zeng, Juan Carlos Cuevas et al.. Continuous Tuning of the Charge-Phase Uncertainty in a Josephson Junction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations
items.summary: This paper addresses fundamental limitations of both traditional written assessments and oral examinations, arguing that the former penalize ambition through deficit-based grading while the latter introduce construct-irrelevant variance through anxiety and power imbalances. The authors propose a theoretical framework for the "Socratic Test," an automated, computer-mediated conversational assessment designed to overcome these shortcomings. The framework integrates Dynamic Assessment principles, Bloom's Taxonomy for real-time proctoring, and the SOLO Taxonomy for structural evaluation within a multimodal workspace environment. A key feature of the proposed system is the formalization of graduated scaffolding to quantify a student's Zone of Proximal Development, enabling the assessment to actively map cognitive boundaries rather than simply record deficits. The paper further details a non-compensatory, additive grading architecture and human-AI alignment mechanisms intended to prioritize mastery and improve measurement reliability.
items.citation: Ilya Mikhelson. The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.
items.summary: This study examined the feasibility, acceptability, and diagnostic performance of point-of-care nucleic acid tests for both HIV detection and viral load monitoring in clinical and community settings in the United States. The researchers enrolled participants across two sites — a hospital-based clinic and an LGBTQ+ community center — where individuals seeking HIV testing, post-exposure prophylaxis, or pre-exposure prophylaxis received a qualitative point-of-care nucleic acid test alongside standard laboratory testing, while people already living with HIV received a semiquantitative version for viral load monitoring, with the latter group also participating in a randomized clinical trial. The study collected quantitative test result data, electronic medical records, acceptability surveys, and in-depth qualitative interviews, as well as time-and-motion observations to assess the impact on clinic workflow. The abstract describes study protocols and enrollment outcomes rather than final results, as analyses of test performance, viral suppression outcomes, and acceptability data are anticipated in future publications. The study represents one of the first prospective evaluations of point-of-care nucleic acid test implementation in diverse real-world settings in the United States.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Violette LR, Cornelius-Hudson A et al.. Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.. JMIR research protocols. 2026

items.title: Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.
items.summary: This study examined whether objective pharmacologic measures of antiretroviral therapy adherence could predict future HIV viremia among people with HIV in South Africa. Researchers compared three tenofovir-based adherence measures — a point-of-care urine antibody assay, quantitative urine tenofovir by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, and tenofovir-diphosphate concentrations in dried blood spots — and assessed their associations with current and subsequent viral load outcomes at 24 weeks using logistic regression. Dried blood spot tenofovir-diphosphate concentrations were significantly and negatively associated with viremia at 24 weeks, suggesting this measure can help predict future treatment failure, while neither urine-based measure showed a significant association with 24-week viral load. Participants with undetectable point-of-care urine tenofovir were more likely to be currently viremic and have low CD4 counts, characteristics consistent with recent antiretroviral therapy initiation rather than non-adherence alone. The findings suggest that dried blood spot tenofovir-diphosphate measurement may be the most useful pharmacologic tool for identifying patients at risk of future viremia and targeting adherence interventions.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Bodley N, Govender K, Moodley P et al.. Brief Report: Association Between Pharmacologic Tenofovir Adherence Measures and Subsequent 24-Week Viral Load Outcomes for People With HIV in South Africa.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: Feasibility of integrating a point of care triage test into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique: a qualitative evaluation
items.summary: This study explored the feasibility and acceptability of integrating a point-of-care triage test measuring IP-10, a chemokine correlated with HIV viral load, into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique. Using a qualitative design nested within a clinical evaluation at two primary healthcare facilities, the researchers conducted multiple rounds of interviews with people living with HIV, healthcare providers, and programme stakeholders to understand experiences, perceptions, and implementation considerations. Participants broadly valued routine viral load monitoring but described significant barriers including laboratory delays, access difficulties, and health system constraints that the triage test could help address. The IP-10 point-of-care test was found to be broadly acceptable, with same-day results perceived as reducing anxiety, supporting treatment adherence, and enabling more timely clinical decisions, while providers highlighted its potential to prioritise those needing confirmatory testing. The authors conclude that successful integration would depend on adequate training, workflow adaptation, quality assurance, and clear communication to patients about the continued need for confirmatory viral load testing.
items.citation: Myburgh H, Saura-Lázaro A, van den Bogaart E et al.. Feasibility of integrating a point of care triage test into routine antiretroviral therapy monitoring in Mozambique: a qualitative evaluation. 2026

items.title: Implementation bottlenecks of near point of care HIV viral load monitoring for children and young people in Tanzania: A Qualitative Study.
items.summary: This qualitative study examined the barriers and facilitators encountered by healthcare workers when implementing near point-of-care HIV viral load monitoring for children and young people living with HIV in Tanzania. Researchers conducted clinic observations and in-depth interviews with healthcare workers at multiple time points across intervention sites participating in a larger cluster-randomised trial in East Africa, analysing findings using a structured determinants-of-innovation framework. The approach revealed that near point-of-care testing meaningfully reduced result turnaround times and enabled same-day counselling, motivating both staff and patients, while implementation was further supported by compatibility with existing workflows, teamwork, and management commitment. However, significant bottlenecks emerged, including prolonged patient waiting times, shortages of physical infrastructure such as rooms and reliable electricity, staff shortages, and delays caused by transporting samples to nearby laboratories. The authors conclude that realising the full benefits of near point-of-care viral load monitoring requires prioritised investment in staff training, infrastructure, sample handling processes, and alignment with clinical guidelines.
items.citation: Msoka P, Mtenga A, Maro R et al.. Implementation bottlenecks of near point of care HIV viral load monitoring for children and young people in Tanzania: A Qualitative Study.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: The Impact of the Common Elements Treatment Approach on HIV Treatment Outcomes Among Women Experiencing Intimate Partner Violence in South Africa: A Randomized Trial.
items.summary: This study investigated whether the Common Elements Treatment Approach (CETA), a cognitive-behavioural-therapy-based intervention delivered by lay healthcare workers, could improve HIV treatment outcomes among women in South Africa experiencing intimate partner violence. The researchers conducted a randomized controlled trial enrolling women living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy who had experienced physical or sexual intimate partner violence and had either unsuppressed viral loads or poor medication adherence, randomly assigning them to receive CETA counselling sessions or weekly safety text messages as an active control. The primary outcome was viral suppression and retention in treatment at twelve months, assessed through routinely collected medical records. Overall, no meaningful difference in viral suppression or retention was found between the CETA group and the control group when analysed on an intention-to-treat basis, though a modest improvement was observed among participants who completed the full CETA intervention compared to controls. The authors conclude that CETA did not demonstrate a meaningful benefit over the active control in this population, and recommend further research to determine whether the intervention could be effective among those who fully complete it.
items.venue: Journal of the International AIDS Society
items.citation: Fox MP, Kane JC, Mngadi-Ncube S et al.. The Impact of the Common Elements Treatment Approach on HIV Treatment Outcomes Among Women Experiencing Intimate Partner Violence in South Africa: A Randomized Trial.. Journal of the International AIDS Society. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examined the longstanding question in exercise immunology of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper presented opposing arguments on several contested issues, including whether high-performance athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity apart from confounding factors such as sleep disruption, nutritional deficits, anxiety, and environmental extremes, and whether commonly used biomarkers and in vitro data adequately capture immune health in those performing arduous exercise. While there is general agreement that regular moderate-intensity exercise benefits immune defense, particularly in older adults and those with chronic disease, the picture is less clear for high-performance athletes and military personnel who engage in exercise greatly exceeding recommended guidelines. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in origin, but whether exercise per se is a causative factor of elevated infection risk in athletes remains unresolved, and the authors call for more rigorous empirical research to address this question.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and how its dysregulation contributes to a broad range of diseases. The authors survey the research history of lipid metabolism and focus specifically on how immune cells, including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils, depend on lipid metabolic processes for proliferation, differentiation, and activation in both innate and adaptive immunity. The review explores lipid functions, transport, and signaling pathways, as well as multilevel regulatory mechanisms spanning genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational control. The authors also discuss how lipid metabolic dysregulation underpins conditions such as cancer, cardiovascular disease, autoimmune disorders, neurodegeneration, and metabolic diseases. Finally, the review synthesizes current and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism, including progress in clinical trials and the potential of lipid-derived biomarkers as future diagnostic and treatment tools.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, commonly referred to as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their growing role in laboratory medicine. The authors surveyed innovations in chip design and fabrication—including three-dimensional printing and flexible, modular substrates—as well as the integration of advanced biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes in real time. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the development of "smart" diagnostic platforms that support automated analysis, self-optimization, and clinical decision support. The review finds that these combined advances have expanded clinical applications across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, and personalized medicine, with emerging utility in neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The authors also identify persistent challenges in manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration that must be addressed before next-generation microfluidic technologies can be broadly implemented in routine clinical and public health practice.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines exosomes, nanoscale extracellular vesicles that mediate intercellular communication by carrying diverse bioactive cargo including proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids. The authors synthesize current understanding of the molecular machinery governing exosome biogenesis and selective cargo loading, with particular attention to ESCRT complexes, lipid domains, RNA-binding proteins, and post-translational modifications that collectively drive exosomal heterogeneity. The review surveys advanced technologies and omics platforms used to characterize exosomal content, and evaluates the clinical utility of exosomes as liquid biopsy biomarkers across cancer, metabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases. Therapeutic applications are also addressed, encompassing both native and engineered exosomes for drug delivery, wound healing, and neuroregeneration, alongside an overview of ongoing clinical trials. The authors conclude that while exosome-based precision medicine is advancing rapidly through innovations such as synthetic mimetics and artificial intelligence–driven diagnostics, significant translational obstacles remain, including inconsistent isolation protocols, cargo variability, and regulatory hurdles.
items.citation: Victor U. Chigozie. Exosomal bioactive molecules: molecular regulation, functional heterogeneity, and translational implications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics. Clinical and Experimental Medicine. 2026

items.title: Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines
items.citation: Dong-il Kwon, Sachin Bhagchandani, Stephen A. Ehrenzeller et al.. Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines. Nature reviews. Immunology. 2026

items.title: Marginal generalized raking with parametric working models
items.summary: The paper extends the theory of generalized raking, a technique originally developed in survey statistics to incorporate auxiliary information, to the estimation of marginal estimands rather than regression coefficients. The authors develop an influence function-based framework called marginal generalized raking, which is designed to handle missing data settings including two-phase study designs common in biostatistics and epidemiology. They compare their proposed approach to a naive alternative that obtains marginal estimates by marginalizing a conditional generalized raking estimator of regression parameters. Performance is evaluated through fully synthetic simulations and an application to observational data from a cohort of persons living with HIV. The results establish a theoretical and empirical case for directly targeting marginal estimands with generalized raking rather than relying on indirect marginalization of conditional estimates.
items.citation: Brian D Williamson, Runjia Zou, Thomas Lumley et al.. Marginal generalized raking with parametric working models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Two-sided estimates of the blow-up time for a semilinear wave equation with fractional structural damping
items.summary: This paper studies a semilinear wave equation with fractional structural damping in a bounded domain, where a parameter interpolates continuously between external frictional damping and internal Kelvin–Voigt viscoelastic damping, thereby capturing a range of frequency-dependent dissipation mechanisms. For initial data with energy below the potential well depth and negative Nehari functional, the authors prove that solutions blow up in finite time and derive explicit upper bounds on the blow-up time using a concavity functional in which the fractional dissipation term vanishes identically, making the upper bound uniform across all damping parameter values. They also establish explicit lower bounds on the blow-up time for a range of nonlinear exponents that widens linearly with the damping parameter, quantifying how stronger internal damping expands the class of nonlinearities for which blow-up time guarantees can be computed. Together, the upper and lower bounds define a concrete interval within which the solution is guaranteed to exist and beyond which it is guaranteed to have failed. The results are formulated for energy solutions satisfying minimal abstract requirements, making them independent of any specific local existence theory and applicable to related operators arising in structural mechanics.
items.citation: Firas Kaabi. Two-sided estimates of the blow-up time for a semilinear wave equation with fractional structural damping. arXiv. 2026

items.title: pylhe: A Lightweight Python interface to Les Houches Event files
items.summary: The paper presents pylhe, a lightweight software library written in pure Python for working with Les Houches Event files, which are a standard data format used by Monte Carlo event generators in high-energy physics. The library supports reading and writing both standard and compressed event files, implements established features such as multiple event weights and generator metadata, and extends support to the newer HDF5-based format. By exposing events through an iterator-based interface, pylhe enables memory-efficient processing of large datasets without requiring entire files to be loaded into memory at once. The library also facilitates format conversion and integrates with modern columnar analysis tools and machine-learning workflows.
items.citation: Alexander Puck Neuwirth, Matthew Feickert, Lukas Heinrich et al.. pylhe: A Lightweight Python interface to Les Houches Event files. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Charging and Discharging a Hubbard-Holstein Quantum Battery: Specific Mechanisms and General Insights
items.summary: The paper investigates a Hubbard-Holstein dimer — a system combining strong electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions — as a model quantum battery in which correlations drive energy storage. The authors examined how ergotropy, the extractable work, behaves both with and without dissipation, finding that it can be robustly stored under certain conditions even when the system is coupled to an environment. While theoretically optimal work extraction can recover all stored energy, this requires precisely fine-tuned couplings that are not physically realistic, so the authors developed an alternative protocol based on matching the spectral properties of the battery to those of the load, which achieves substantial though suboptimal energy extraction. The study further suggests that the very microscopic mechanism responsible for storing energy in a quantum battery can inherently limit which classes of systems are capable of efficiently extracting it, implying that quantum batteries may not be universally applicable across different physical platforms.
items.citation: Emil Östberg, Arvid Steen, Najmeh Abiri et al.. Charging and Discharging a Hubbard-Holstein Quantum Battery: Specific Mechanisms and General Insights. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Bayesian fusion forests for heterogeneous treatment effects on survival from randomised and real-world data
items.summary: This paper develops a nonparametric Bayesian framework called the Bayesian fusion forest to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects on survival outcomes by combining randomised controlled trial data with real-world observational data. Rather than assuming the observational data is free of confounding, the method assumes that treatment effects transport across the two data sources, and it explicitly models confounding bias through a dedicated confounding function within an accelerated failure time decomposition. Each component of the survival model—including a shared baseline prognosis, source-specific deviations, treatment effects, and the confounding function—receives a Bayesian tree ensemble prior, while the error distribution is handled nonparametrically via a hierarchical Dirichlet process mixture. Simulation studies demonstrate that the fusion approach yields efficiency gains over trial-only analyses across varying levels of confounding and between-source heterogeneity. Applied to combining an HIV clinical trial with a cohort study, the method identifies a consistent benefit of combination antiretroviral therapy across nearly all patients, a conclusion that the trial data alone could not support.
items.citation: Tijn Jacobs, Stéphanie L. van der Pas, Wessel N. van Wieringen. Bayesian fusion forests for heterogeneous treatment effects on survival from randomised and real-world data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Revisiting Stress Analysis in a Three-Dimensional Elastic Hollow Sphere under Uniaxial Compression via the Inverse Laplace Transform Expressions within an Elastodynamic Framework
items.summary: This paper revisits the classical problem of stress distribution in a three-dimensional elastic hollow sphere subjected to uniaxial compression by recasting it within an elastodynamic framework rather than a purely static one. The authors applied the Laplace transform to expand the scalar and vector displacement potentials, enabling a systematic treatment of the governing equations. Static solutions for displacement and stress distributions were then recovered by taking the long-time limit of the inverse Laplace transform. A notable finding is that on the inner surface of the sphere, certain stress quantities reach a peak at the location where the surface normal is perpendicular to the applied compressive force, indicating localized stress concentration at that specific geometric position. The approach is presented as a robust analytical method with broader implications for material science and structural engineering applications involving hollow spherical geometries.
items.citation: Satoshi Takada, Shintaro Hokada. Revisiting Stress Analysis in a Three-Dimensional Elastic Hollow Sphere under Uniaxial Compression via the Inverse Laplace Transform Expressions within an Elastodynamic Framework. arXiv. 2026

items.title: 'It's Primarily Around Their Viral Load': Public Health Decision-Making and HIV Risk Assemblages in Ontario, Canada.
items.summary: This study examined how public health practitioners in Ontario, Canada determine when the behaviors of people living with HIV constitute "significant" risk warranting official intervention, including enforceable orders. Using assemblage theory as a conceptual framework, the researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with public health personnel and analyzed the data through reflexive thematic analysis. Findings revealed that risk assessments were shaped by the interplay of biomedical markers such as viral load, care continuity, co-infections, and compliance with public health directives, rather than by individual behavior alone. The study also found that the Undetectable = Untransmittable principle has meaningfully reshaped how risk is understood, yet its adoption was uneven across public health units, resulting in inconsistent and sometimes coercive approaches toward people living with HIV. The authors conclude that HIV risk is relationally and contextually produced rather than individually determined, and advocate for broader adoption of equity-based, nonpunitive public health practices.
items.citation: Daroya E, French M, Hastings C et al.. 'It's Primarily Around Their Viral Load': Public Health Decision-Making and HIV Risk Assemblages in Ontario, Canada.. Sociology of health & illness. 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *P. vivax* co-circulate, and where conventional HRP2-based tests are compromised by low parasite densities and gene deletions. Febrile patients attending health facilities during peak transmission season were tested using the new Bioline Malaria multi-antigen RDT alongside expert microscopy and quantitative PCR as reference standards. The multi-antigen RDT showed high specificity and strong agreement with microscopy, performing well for routine clinical diagnosis. However, when qPCR served as the reference, sensitivity was notably reduced, revealing that the RDT missed a meaningful proportion of submicroscopic, low-density infections that PCR detected but microscopy could not. The authors conclude that while the multi-antigen RDT is clinically useful, more sensitive diagnostic approaches are needed for malaria surveillance and elimination efforts in co-endemic settings.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.
items.summary: This study investigated circulating arboviruses in Haiti during a period when conventional surveillance was disrupted by political instability, using an unconventional sample source to overcome access challenges. Researchers extracted nucleic acids from discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes collected from febrile patients at healthcare centers across two Haitian departments, then screened these materials using a series of real-time PCR assays targeting flaviviruses, alphaviruses, and Oropouche virus, followed by next-generation sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. Dengue virus serotype three was identified as the predominant circulating arbovirus, with all positive detections occurring in samples from a single year, and no evidence of alphavirus or Oropouche virus circulation was found. Phylogenetic analysis placed the detected sequences within a cluster closely related to strains circulating across the Caribbean during the same period, consistent with a broader regional dengue outbreak. The findings establish that discarded malaria rapid diagnostic tests can serve as a practical and informative surveillance tool for arboviral pathogens in resource-limited or insecure settings where conventional public health monitoring is not feasible.
items.citation: Matulis GA, Smith HP, Hall G et al.. Characterization of arbovirus infections in patients within Haiti by screening discarded malaria rapid diagnostic test cassettes.. PLoS neglected tropical diseases. 2026

items.title: ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring
items.summary: This paper presents an IoT and AI-integrated wireless health monitoring framework designed for elderly and chronically ill patients in remote or auxiliary care environments. The system combines sensors tracking heart rate, body temperature, and blood oxygen levels with ZigBee-based low-power communication to transmit data to a cloud-based processing unit in real time. Multiple machine learning algorithms, including random forest, support vector machine, and logistic regression, were applied to detect health anomalies, with the random forest model achieving particularly strong classification performance. The system was evaluated in a real-world care facility setting, demonstrating very low transmission latency and minimal power consumption, making it suitable for sustained long-term deployment. The authors claim their framework addresses key shortcomings of existing telehealth systems—such as high latency, frequent false alarms, and poor integration—while offering a scalable architecture that can accommodate additional sensor types as patient needs evolve.
items.citation: B. V. Ravi Kumar, Mohammad Shahnawaz Shaikh. ZigBee Based Low Latency IoT and AI Integrated Framework for Real Time Telehealth Monitoring. Emerging Science Journal. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent developments in microfluidic chip technology, commonly referred to as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their growing role in laboratory medicine. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of innovations in chip design and fabrication, including advances such as three-dimensional printing and flexible modular substrates, alongside the integration of biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the creation of smart diagnostic platforms with capabilities for self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support. These technologies have demonstrated broad applicability across cancer diagnostics, infectious disease detection, point-of-care testing, personalized medicine, and emerging areas such as neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling. The review also identifies persistent challenges in manufacturing consistency, clinical validation, and system integration that must be addressed before next-generation microfluidic devices can be widely adopted in routine clinical and public health settings.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare
items.summary: This study evaluated the safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system embedded in electronic medical records across primary care clinics in Kenya. Trained physicians retrospectively reviewed over a thousand patient encounters to assess hallucination rates, guideline alignment, and the safety of recommendations generated by the system. The tool performed well on several metrics, with hallucinations being uncommon and clinical guidance aligning with local guidelines in nearly all cases. However, a meaningful proportion of encounters contained actively harmful recommendations from the system, and a concerning pattern emerged whereby clinicians were more likely to adopt harmful suggestions than to accept beneficial ones that could mitigate pre-existing risks in their notes. The authors conclude that while the tool shows promise for supporting healthcare quality in an African primary care setting, asymmetric uptake of outputs and residual safety risks highlight the need for improved usability, locally tailored safeguards, and prospective trials before broader deployment.
items.citation: Ambrose Agweyu, Paul Mwaniki, Wilkister Musau et al.. Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare. Nature Health. 2026

items.title: Emulating the nonlinear effects of modified gravity on the matter power spectrum for reconstruction
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational challenge of incorporating nonlinear modified gravity effects into model-independent reconstructions of modified gravity functions, where repeated evaluations of the nonlinear matter power spectrum are prohibitively expensive. The authors constructed a neural-network emulator trained on nearly a million samples to predict the nonlinear correction ratio between the nonlinear and linear modified gravity matter power spectra, using the CosmoPower framework. The emulator achieves sub-percent to low-percent level accuracy across the relevant scale ranges for standard cosmology and moderate modified gravity scenarios, with the accuracy maintained even for extreme nonlinear cases at intermediate scales. Validation through independent test sets and synthetic data analyses confirmed that the emulator reliably recovers standard cosmological parameters and the general relativity limits of reconstructed modified gravity functions, demonstrating its suitability for Stage-IV survey analyses. The authors further illustrated the emulator's utility in breaking degeneracies between models with similar linear power spectra, enabling likelihood analyses for current photometric surveys, and forecasting constraints from combined spectroscopic and imaging survey data using principal component analysis.
items.citation: Lanyang Yi, Kazuya Koyama, Qi Xiong et al.. Emulating the nonlinear effects of modified gravity on the matter power spectrum for reconstruction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field
items.summary: This paper examines the production of dark photons as dark matter candidates through the perturbative decay of a dark Higgs field that is displaced from its potential minimum during inflation via stochastic misalignment. The authors revisit this framework, which is notable for being simple and predictive in generating the correct dark photon relic abundance. They find that the scenario is constrained by structure formation, because the produced dark photons are initially relativistic, and by inflationary isocurvature fluctuations, which require the quartic self-coupling of the dark Higgs to be small. Their analysis identifies a viable parameter space spanning dark photon masses between the hundred-eV and GeV scales with correspondingly tiny gauge couplings, with further restrictions arising if kinetic mixing between the dark photon and the standard model photon is present at a generic level. The favored parameter region is predicted to be testable through future cosmological observations such as the cosmic microwave background or Lyman-alpha measurements, as well as through direct detection experiments and diffuse soft gamma-ray searches when kinetic mixing is included.
items.citation: James M. Cline, Gonzalo Herrera, Jean-Samuel Roux. Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography
items.summary: This paper investigates how many copies of an unknown quantum state are required to estimate or test certain fundamental properties that depend only on the state's eigenvalues. The authors study spectrum estimation, von Neumann entropy estimation, and rank-testing for quantum states in a d-dimensional Hilbert space, seeking tight lower bounds on the sample complexity of these tasks. They construct hard instances using sandwiched products of Haar-random projectors, with a novel normalization technique that enables explicit computation of high-order tensor moments expressed as symmetric functions of Jucys–Murphy elements in the symmetric group algebra. By analyzing the log-likelihood ratio between pairs of such hard instances and performing moment-matching to show indistinguishability, they establish that all three tasks require nearly as many samples as full quantum state tomography. The central finding is a sample complexity lower bound that scales nearly quadratically in the dimension for all three problems, demonstrating that these seemingly simpler property-estimation tasks are almost as hard as learning the entire quantum state.
items.citation: Marco Fanizza, Ryan O'Donnell, Chirag Wadhwa. Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ArcLP: A Matlab implementation of an $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n}L)$ arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming
items.summary: This paper presents a Matlab software implementation of an arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming that carries the best known polynomial complexity bound among interior-point methods for this class of problems. The authors describe the software architecture, key algorithmic strategies, and ease of use, and they validate the implementation through extensive testing on standard Netlib benchmark linear programming problems spanning tens of thousands of constraints and hundreds of thousands of variables. The algorithm successfully found optimal solutions for all tested problems. Computational results were compared against the widely used Mehrotra predictor-corrector algorithm, and the authors conclude that their implementation is not only theoretically superior in its complexity bound but also practically competitive in numerical performance.
items.citation: Yang, Yaguang. ArcLP: A Matlab implementation of an $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n}L)$ arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fermionic entropy: an efficiently measurable strong monotone for non-Gaussianity
items.summary: This paper studies fermionic non-Gaussianity as a computational resource, focusing on how to quantify it rigorously and measure it efficiently. The authors introduce the fermionic entropy, defined via the squared Frobenius norm of the correlation matrix, and prove it is a strong monotone under Gaussian operations for pure states, meaning it faithfully captures the non-Gaussian resource content. A key practical result is that the associated fermionic purity can be estimated from only a number of two-copy measurements independent of system size, making it experimentally accessible. The authors further establish that fermionic entropy satisfies asymptotic continuity, giving it an operational interpretation as an upper bound on the rate at which non-Gaussianity can be distilled, and they derive an improved sample complexity bound for testing whether a state is Gaussian. As an application, they show that a linear number of non-Gaussian gates is necessary for Matchgate circuits supplemented with local non-Gaussian operations to approximate a quantum state design, thereby pinning down the optimal resource overhead up to logarithmic factors.
items.citation: Lorenzo Leone, Lennart Bittel. Fermionic entropy: an efficiently measurable strong monotone for non-Gaussianity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents
items.summary: This paper investigates how procedural knowledge from past software repairs can be systematically reused by large language model-based coding agents, rather than discarded after each fix. The authors developed STAIR, a framework that converts historical repair trajectories into hierarchical, multi-level tree structures encoding repair experience at granularities ranging from fine-grained diagnostic actions to high-level strategies. When a new issue is encountered, STAIR retrieves relevant plan nodes across abstraction levels, customizes them into executable issue-specific plans, and injects them into the agent's prompt. Evaluation on a software engineering benchmark showed strong task resolution performance, and the generated plans generalized to structurally different agents without modification, improving their success rates as well. Ablation studies confirmed that combining multiple abstraction levels outperforms any single level, and that raw unabstracted trajectories transfer substantially less effectively than the hierarchically structured plans.
items.citation: Yisen Xu, Jiayuan Zhou, Ruiqi Pan et al.. Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviewed advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research over a five-year period and their translation into updated WHO policy guidance. The authors synthesized evidence on screening, diagnosis, and drug-resistance testing across diverse populations and specimen types, encompassing digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection, decentralised molecular platforms, novel specimen types such as tongue swabs, and approaches like sputum pooling. Key findings include expanded use of rapid nucleic acid amplification tests for decentralised settings, improvements in bacteriological confirmation for children and sputum-scarce populations through non-sputum specimens, and the recognition of targeted next-generation sequencing for comprehensive drug-susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level. Urine lipoarabinomannan assays offer diagnostic gains in people with HIV and advanced disease, while host blood transcriptomic and other biomarkers show promise for prognosis and triage but none yet meets WHO criteria for reliably distinguishing infection from disease at the point of care. The authors conclude that despite substantial progress, significant performance, implementation, and equity gaps remain, particularly for detecting subclinical tuberculosis.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.
items.summary: This review examines blood-based diagnostic approaches for tuberculosis, a persistent global health burden caused by *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*. The authors survey current serological biomarkers being investigated for TB diagnosis and discuss how advanced detection technologies can be integrated with these markers. The review focuses particularly on the value of serodiagnosis in clinical scenarios where conventional methods fall short, such as extrapulmonary TB and cases yielding negative sputum culture or molecular test results. The authors highlight serological approaches as attractive alternatives owing to their simplicity, speed, and cost-effectiveness, and argue that continued identification of novel biomarkers combined with advanced diagnostic platforms holds promise for improving TB detection across varied clinical settings.
items.citation: Yue C, Geng X, Sun X et al.. Emerging blood-based diagnostic strategies for tuberculosis.. Clinical chemistry and laboratory medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study compared two WHO-endorsed nucleic acid amplification tests — Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra — for detecting pulmonary tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance among presumptive TB patients in India, while also evaluating their operational feasibility and costs. In a prospective design, paired sputum specimens from over six hundred patients were tested on both platforms, with mycobacterial culture and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing serving as reference standards. Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra demonstrated higher sensitivity and specificity for both TB detection and rifampicin resistance, and produced substantially fewer invalid or indeterminate results compared to Truenat MTB Plus. Truenat, however, was considerably less expensive per test, making it more attractive for decentralized deployment, though its higher rates of invalid and indeterminate results create an added operational burden through the need for repeat testing. The authors conclude that the two platforms are complementary and advocate a tiered diagnostic strategy that exploits their respective strengths to broaden molecular testing access in high-burden settings.
items.citation: Sidiq Z, Anand A, Dwivedi KK et al.. Diagnostic accuracy, operational feasibility, and cost considerations of Truenat MTB Plus and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for pulmonary tuberculosis.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Feasibility and acceptability of pooled sputum testing for tuberculosis: a multicountry qualitative study of the Start4All project.
items.summary: This study investigated the real-world feasibility and acceptability of pooled sputum testing as a strategy to expand access to molecular tuberculosis diagnostics in high-burden settings. Using a multicountry qualitative design, the researchers conducted key informant interviews and focus group discussions with a range of stakeholders—including national tuberculosis programme representatives, laboratory technicians, people with tuberculosis, and international experts—across seven high-burden countries in Africa, Asia, and South America. Data were analysed using established feasibility and acceptability frameworks to capture perspectives from both facility and community settings. The study found that pooled testing was broadly regarded as feasible and acceptable, particularly in countries with prior implementation experience and robust laboratory infrastructure, with feasibility hinging on compatibility with existing diagnostic workflows, biosafety standards, and clear operating procedures. Acceptability required early engagement of national programme leadership to secure professional buy-in, as well as transparent communication with patients, and the authors conclude that pooled testing represents a pragmatic approach to optimising molecular testing capacity, though readiness varied across countries and some settings would require system strengthening before scale-up.
items.citation: Iem V, Vo LNQ, Codlin AJ et al.. Feasibility and acceptability of pooled sputum testing for tuberculosis: a multicountry qualitative study of the Start4All project.. BMJ open. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether molecular testing on saliva and oral swabs could serve as accurate, non-sputum diagnostic alternatives for pulmonary tuberculosis. Using a nested case-control design within a prospective cohort of adults and children at primary care centers in Colombia, researchers applied Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra testing to saliva and nylon-flocked oral swab samples, comparing results against sputum liquid mycobacterial culture as the reference standard. Saliva demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for culture-confirmed tuberculosis, exceeding the World Health Organization's target threshold of at least eighty percent sensitivity for a low-complexity, non-sputum diagnostic test, while oral swabs showed somewhat lower sensitivity but similarly high specificity. Saliva sensitivity was significantly higher than that of oral swabs, though the two methods did not differ significantly in specificity. The vast majority of participants found both collection methods acceptable, supporting the feasibility of these approaches as practical alternatives to sputum-based tuberculosis diagnosis.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Vargas DA, Fuertes-Bucheli JF, Sanchez-Hidalgo A et al.. Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Rapid Extensively Drug-Resistant (XDR) TB Diagnosis: An In-House DNA Biochip for Drug Resistance Detection and Mutation Profiling of <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i>.
items.summary: This paper studied the development and validation of an in-house DNA biochip for rapid detection of drug resistance mutations in *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*, targeting both multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant strains. The researchers designed a biochip carrying probes against resistance-associated mutations across six key genes linked to resistance to first-line drugs (rifampicin and isoniazid) and second-line drugs (fluoroquinolones and injectable agents), using multiplex PCR amplification and enhanced chemiluminescence for signal detection. The assay was evaluated against a panel of clinical isolates, with culture-based drug susceptibility testing as the reference standard and sequencing used to resolve discordant results. The biochip demonstrated high diagnostic sensitivity across all drugs tested and specificities exceeding the vast majority threshold, along with strong reproducibility and an analytical sensitivity of a thousand genome copies per assay. The authors conclude that this platform enables simultaneous profiling of multiple resistance mutations in a single test, offering a promising tool for early diagnosis, treatment guidance, and surveillance of drug-resistant tuberculosis in resource-limited settings.
items.venue: The Canadian journal of infectious diseases & medical microbiology = Journal canadien des maladies infectieuses et de la microbiologie medicale
items.citation: Jain B, Kulkarni S, Baghel NS. Rapid Extensively Drug-Resistant (XDR) TB Diagnosis: An In-House DNA Biochip for Drug Resistance Detection and Mutation Profiling of <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i>.. The Canadian journal of infectious diseases & medical microbiology = Journal canadien des maladies infectieuses et de la microbiologie medicale. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and how its dysregulation contributes to a broad range of diseases. The authors comprehensively survey the history of lipid metabolism research, covering lipid functions, transport, and signaling pathways, with particular emphasis on how lipid metabolites regulate immune cell proliferation, differentiation, and activation across macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils. The review also addresses multilevel regulatory mechanisms—spanning genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational control—that shape immune cell behavior through lipid metabolism. Disease contexts explored include autoimmune conditions, cancer, neurodegenerative and cardiovascular diseases, aging, and metabolic disorders. The authors conclude by synthesizing current and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism, including lipid-derived biomarkers and clinical trial progress, while identifying future research directions.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Sepsis
items.citation: Mervyn Singer, Derek C Angus, Djillali Annane et al.. Sepsis. The Lancet. 2026

items.title: Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options
items.summary: This review paper examines the molecular mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis, a chronic joint disorder characterized by pain, inflammation, and bone deterioration, with the goal of identifying more effective therapeutic targets. The authors analyzed how disease progression is driven by interconnected organelle dysfunctions, including mitochondrial damage with excessive reactive oxygen species production, lysosomal destabilization triggered by hydroxyapatite digestion, and unresolved endoplasmic reticulum stress that worsens cartilage degradation. The review also maps the nociceptive pathways connecting the knee joint to the central nervous system to clarify the basis of osteoarthritis-associated pain, alongside the roles of inflammatory cytokines and pathological changes in bone and chondrocyte biology. Based on these mechanistic insights, the authors propose a multimodal therapeutic framework targeting inflammatory cascades, organelle homeostasis restoration through strategies such as mitophagy enhancement and lysosomal integrity preservation, and attenuation of pain signaling. They additionally highlight advanced organelle-targeted drug delivery systems as a means to improve the efficacy and stability of these emerging treatments.
items.citation: Yi Zhang, Yanqi Han, Ying Sun et al.. Osteoarthritis: molecular pathogenesis and potential therapeutic options. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years
items.summary: The paper reports on the implementation and outcomes of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme, a national initiative that uses low-dose computed tomography to detect lung cancer early in high-risk individuals aged 55–74 who have a history of smoking and meet risk thresholds determined by multivariable models. The programme operates through regionally federated clinical infrastructure underpinned by centralized national protocols and was rolled out at scale from 2019 onward with full national coverage targeted by 2030. Over five years, more than two million people were invited, resulting in thousands of lung cancer diagnoses, the majority of which were detected at early tumor stages, representing a meaningful shift toward earlier-stage diagnosis across England. The programme demonstrated particular impact in socioeconomically deprived regions, though the authors note that inequalities in participation remain a challenge requiring further attention. The findings are presented as evidence supporting broader adoption of lung cancer screening across the United Kingdom and internationally, with the programme's logistical framework offered as a practical model for adaptation elsewhere.
items.citation: Richard W. Lee, Arjun Nair, Haval Balata et al.. Implementation of the NHS England Lung Cancer Screening Programme over 5 years. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, commonly called lab-on-a-chip systems, and their applications in laboratory medicine. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of innovations in chip design and fabrication, including three-dimensional printing and flexible substrates, alongside developments in biosensor integration and artificial intelligence. These technologies have enabled miniaturized, automated diagnostic platforms capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes in real time with minimal sample volumes. The convergence of microfluidics with machine learning has produced smart diagnostic systems that support self-optimization and clinical decision-making across areas including cancer diagnostics, infectious disease, point-of-care testing, and emerging fields such as neuroscience and microbiome profiling. The review also identifies persistent challenges in manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration that must be addressed before widespread adoption in routine clinical and public health settings.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic literature review examined how different forms of exercise influence the expression of Toll-like receptors (TLRs), immune cell receptors whose dysregulated signalling is linked to chronic low-grade inflammation and non-communicable diseases associated with sedentary behaviour. The authors searched multiple databases and identified studies in which exercise served as an isolated intervention in human participants, ultimately including dozens of articles categorised by exercise type and duration. Key patterns emerged across exercise modalities: acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise generally produced neutral or downregulatory effects, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programmes predominantly left TLR levels unchanged or reduced them, whereas chronic aerobic training yielded more mixed results with most measurements showing no significant change. The authors conclude that exercise does interact with TLR signalling in a modality-dependent manner, but caution that substantial heterogeneity in study designs limits firm conclusions and that further research is needed to clarify underlying mechanisms and clinical implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Emulating the nonlinear effects of modified gravity on the matter power spectrum for reconstruction
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational challenge of incorporating nonlinear structure formation information into model-independent reconstructions of modified gravity functions, which is necessary to improve cosmological constraints but prohibitively expensive with standard tools. The authors built a neural-network emulator trained on nearly a million samples using the CosmoPower framework to rapidly predict the nonlinear correction ratio of the modified gravity matter power spectrum to its linear counterpart. The emulator achieves agreement with reference calculations to within a few percent across the relevant range of scales and cosmological parameters, and synthetic data tests confirm it reliably recovers standard cosmological parameters and general relativity limits within posterior uncertainties. Beyond validation, the authors demonstrate that the emulator can break near-degeneracies between models with similar linear power spectra, enable likelihood analyses for current photometric surveys, and support forecasting of constraints from upcoming Stage-IV surveys through principal component analysis. The work establishes this emulator as an accurate and efficient tool for exploiting nonlinear information in modified gravity searches with next-generation cosmological surveys.
items.citation: Lanyang Yi, Kazuya Koyama, Qi Xiong et al.. Emulating the nonlinear effects of modified gravity on the matter power spectrum for reconstruction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field
items.summary: This paper investigates the production of dark photons as dark matter candidates through the perturbative decay of a dark Higgs field that is displaced from its potential minimum during inflation via stochastic misalignment. The authors analyze the constraints on this scenario arising from structure formation, since the produced dark photons are initially relativistic and boosted, and from inflationary isocurvature fluctuations, which limit the allowed quartic self-coupling of the Higgs field. They identify a viable parameter space in dark photon mass and gauge coupling consistent with generating the observed relic abundance. The scenario becomes more constrained when kinetic mixing between the dark photon and the Standard Model photon is included, and the authors suggest that the favored parameter region could be probed by future cosmic microwave background or Lyman-alpha observations, as well as direct detection experiments and diffuse soft gamma-ray searches.
items.citation: James M. Cline, Gonzalo Herrera, Jean-Samuel Roux. Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography
items.summary: This paper investigates how many copies of an unknown quantum state are required to estimate or test its fundamental unitarily invariant properties, specifically spectrum estimation, von Neumann entropy estimation, and rank-testing. The authors prove near-quadratic sample complexity lower bounds in the dimension of the state for all three tasks, establishing that these problems are nearly as hard as full quantum state tomography. To construct hard instances, they develop a novel technique based on sandwiched products of Haar-random projectors and analyze the resulting high-order tensor moments using symmetric functions of Jucys–Murphy elements from the symmetric group algebra. Indistinguishability between hard instance distributions is demonstrated through moment-matching of log-likelihood ratios and bounding an f-divergence using high-order components, while concentration arguments on Haar-random unitaries confirm that the hard instances are genuinely separated in spectrum, entropy, and rank. Together, these results tightly characterize the sample complexity of these central quantum property estimation tasks and show that no approach can substantially outperform tomography for them.
items.citation: Marco Fanizza, Ryan O'Donnell, Chirag Wadhwa. Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ArcLP: A Matlab implementation of an $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n}L)$ arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming
items.summary: This paper presents a Matlab software implementation of an arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming that carries the best known polynomial complexity bound among interior-point methods for this class of problems. The authors describe the software architecture, key algorithmic strategies, and ease of use, illustrating the implementation with a worked example. The software was extensively tested on standard Netlib benchmark linear programming problems, including large instances with tens of thousands of constraints and hundreds of thousands of variables, and successfully found optimal solutions in all cases. Numerical results were compared against Mehrotra's predictor-corrector algorithm, a widely used reference method, and the new implementation proved computationally competitive. The authors conclude that the arc-search algorithm combines its theoretical optimality in polynomial complexity with practical computational performance.
items.citation: Yang, Yaguang. ArcLP: A Matlab implementation of an $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n}L)$ arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fermionic entropy: an efficiently measurable strong monotone for non-Gaussianity
items.summary: This paper investigates how to quantify fermionic non-Gaussianity, the resource that enables quantum computation beyond classically simulable free-fermion dynamics. The authors introduce and analyze the fermionic entropy, defined via the squared Frobenius norm of the correlation matrix, proving it is a strong monotone under Gaussian operations for pure states and that it satisfies asymptotic continuity. A key practical result is that the associated fermionic purity can be estimated from a number of two-copy measurements that is independent of system size, making this monotone experimentally accessible. The asymptotic continuity further establishes an operational interpretation: the fermionic entropy upper bounds the rate at which non-Gaussianity can be distilled asymptotically. As applications, the authors derive improved sample complexity bounds for tolerant testing of Gaussian states and prove that generating approximate unitary designs with Matchgate circuits requires a linear number of non-Gaussian gates, pinning down the optimal doping level up to logarithmic factors.
items.citation: Lorenzo Leone, Lennart Bittel. Fermionic entropy: an efficiently measurable strong monotone for non-Gaussianity. arXiv. 2026

items.summary: This paper investigates whether procedural knowledge accumulated from past software repairs can be systematically reused to improve LLM-driven coding agents, rather than treating each issue from scratch. The authors developed STAIR, a framework that converts historical repair trajectories into hierarchical multi-level tree structures encoding experience at multiple granularities, from fine-grained diagnostic actions to high-level repair strategies. When a new issue arrives, STAIR retrieves relevant plan nodes across abstraction levels, adapts them into issue-specific executable plans, and injects them into the agent's prompt. Evaluations on a software engineering benchmark show strong task completion performance, and the generated plans generalize across structurally different agents without any code modification, substantially improving their success rates. Ablation studies confirm that combining multiple abstraction levels outperforms any single level, and that raw unabstracted trajectories transfer considerably less effectively than the hierarchical representations.
