items.title: Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).
items.summary: This pilot study examined the utility of point-of-care testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis among men who have sex with men attending a non-governmental organisation-led clinic on the outskirts of Beirut, alongside an assessment of their sexual health knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Using a cross-sectional design over four months, a physician conducted sexual health consultations, administered STI and HIV tests, and collected anonymous survey data covering demographics, condom use, chemsex, sexual violence, and perceived stigma. The cohort was predominantly young, educated Lebanese and Syrian men, among whom a notable proportion were living with HIV. Despite high levels of STI and HIV awareness, participants frequently reported condomless sex and recreational drug use, with perceived community stigma identified as a significant barrier to testing. The findings suggest that integrating point-of-care testing into sexual health services enables same-day counselling and rapid linkage to care, while underscoring the need to address HIV-related stigma as a driver of risk behaviour in this population.
items.citation: Abou Shahla W, Rossoni I, Padovese V. Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.
items.summary: This study examined the cost of integrating point-of-care screening for three curable sexually transmitted infections into antenatal care in Harare, Zimbabwe, compared with the standard syndromic management approach. The researchers implemented screening at two primary healthcare clinics and collected detailed economic cost data using staff interviews, time-and-motion studies, and other sources, then modelled implementation in a low-volume routine care setting over a twelve-month period. A substantial proportion of pregnant women screened tested positive for at least one of the targeted infections, confirming the clinical relevance of the intervention. Test kit and personnel costs dominated the overall expenditure, and the incremental cost per person treated was considerably higher for point-of-care testing than for syndromic management. The authors conclude that reductions in the cost of point-of-care diagnostics will be essential for this screening strategy to be economically viable in similar settings.
items.citation: Martin K, Bath D, Nyamwanza R et al.. Point-of-care screening for curable sexually transmitted infections in antenatal care in Zimbabwe: a costing study.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.
items.summary: This study examined whether a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections is cost-effective compared with standard laboratory-based testing in remote Australian First Nations communities, where the burden of chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and trichomonas is disproportionately high. Researchers constructed a decision analytic model comparing costs and health outcomes over a ten-year horizon for young women and men seeking care, using quality-adjusted life years as the primary outcome measure. The model found that the point-of-care programme was cost-effective relative to standard care, with the incremental cost per quality-adjusted life year falling well below the nominated willingness-to-pay threshold. The programme was also predicted to meaningfully reduce rates of pelvic inflammatory disease and preterm or low birth weight births among those with an infection, with the cost-effectiveness results being most sensitive to the probability of infection and the likelihood of receiving treatment within two days. The authors conclude that sustained, scaled point-of-care testing in remote primary care settings is a cost-effective strategy likely to improve reproductive health outcomes in these communities.
items.citation: Watts CG, Causer LM, Matthews SJ et al.. Cost-effectiveness of a decentralised molecular point-of-care testing programme for sexually transmitted infections in remote primary care health services in Australia.. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections.
items.summary: This review examines the epidemiology, pathogenic mechanisms, diagnosis, and prevention of anorectal bacterial sexually transmitted infections, focusing primarily on chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and syphilis. The authors synthesize current understanding of why these infections frequently persist without symptoms, attributing this to bacterial adaptation to rectal tissue and dampened local immune responses that remain below the threshold required to produce clinical manifestations, a phenomenon especially prominent among men who have sex with men. Molecular diagnostics have improved detection considerably, yet challenges remain in distinguishing viable from non-viable organisms, expanding point-of-care testing, and reconciling thorough screening with antimicrobial stewardship goals. Treatment is complicated by evolving antimicrobial resistance, particularly for gonorrhoea, while prevention is advancing through approaches such as doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis, which has shown meaningful reductions in chlamydia and syphilis incidence, alongside emerging artificial intelligence applications. The review identifies key knowledge gaps and outlines research priorities needed to strengthen control of these infections globally.
items.citation: Latt PM, Kong FYS, Khosropour CM et al.. Mechanisms, management and prevention of anorectal sexually transmitted infections.. Nature reviews. Gastroenterology & hepatology. 2026

items.title: Use of point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing for chlamydia and gonorrhea in community outreach settings in Dallas, Texas, USA.
items.summary: This study examined the implementation of rapid point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing for chlamydia and gonorrhea in non-clinical, community outreach settings in an urban environment. Researchers conducted a program evaluation and retrospective data review, using a commercial assay capable of delivering results within thirty minutes, and analyzed demographic and symptom-based correlates of test positivity using chi-squared and Fisher's exact tests. The testing program successfully diagnosed multiple cases of both infections rapidly, with all positive cases referred for treatment within one day. No statistically significant associations were found between test positivity and demographic characteristics or symptom presence, though the authors note this finding was constrained by a small sample size. The study concludes that point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing is feasible in outreach settings and supports rapid diagnosis and referral, while calling for further investigation into scalability, cost, and treatment completion.
items.citation: Blanchard HL, Gonzalez E, Chow J. Use of point-of-care nucleic acid amplification testing for chlamydia and gonorrhea in community outreach settings in Dallas, Texas, USA.. Sexual health. 2026

items.title: The International Guideline for the Definition, Classification, Diagnosis and Management of Urticaria
items.summary: This paper presents an updated international clinical guideline for urticaria, a mast cell-driven disease characterized by wheals, angioedema, or both. The guideline was developed using Cochrane methods and the GRADE framework, with input from a large multinational consensus process involving delegates from numerous national and international societies across dozens of countries. It covers the definition and classification of urticaria, distinguishing between acute and chronic forms, with chronic urticaria further categorized as spontaneous or inducible. The guideline provides expert-guided and evidence-based recommendations for diagnosing and managing the different subtypes of urticaria, noting that novel therapies are now available for what can be a disabling condition with significant impacts on quality of life and daily functioning.
items.citation: T. Zuberbier, Z. Abdul Hameed Ansari, A. H. Abdul Latiff et al.. The International Guideline for the Definition, Classification, Diagnosis and Management of Urticaria. Allergy. 2026

items.title: Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines
items.citation: Dong-il Kwon, Sachin Bhagchandani, Stephen A. Ehrenzeller et al.. Harnessing mucosal immunity for protective vaccines. Nature reviews. Immunology. 2026

items.title: Technological effects on gender studies: An intersectional perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the relationship between digital transformation and gender dynamics, asking whether technologization represents a fundamental shift in how gender identities are constructed, performed, and contested. Through a systematic literature review of high-impact recent research, the authors draw on sociology, feminist theory, communication studies, health informatics, and STEM education to map the current state of scholarship at this intersection. The analysis finds that digital technologies carry genuine emancipatory potential by enabling anonymity, accessibility, and broader public participation, yet simultaneously replicate and intensify patriarchal structures through mechanisms including cyberviolence, algorithmic bias, digital exclusion, and women's underrepresentation in STEM fields. The review further identifies geographic and disciplinary gaps in the scholarly literature and establishes that digital spaces are not ideologically neutral but are contested terrains where power relations are renegotiated in novel forms. The authors conclude by calling for intersectional, gender-sensitive policies and multi-stakeholder collaborations to resist the reproduction of masculine dominance and foster genuinely equitable technological ecosystems.
items.venue: Feminist Encounters A Journal of Critical Studies in Culture and Politics
items.citation: Şevki Işıklı, Esra Fatma FAZLIOĞLU. Technological effects on gender studies: An intersectional perspective. Feminist Encounters A Journal of Critical Studies in Culture and Politics. 2026

items.title: An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening
items.summary: This thesis examined methods for identifying and controlling sexually transmitted diseases, with particular focus on contact tracing and screening strategies for conditions including gonorrhoea, HIV, and chlamydia. The work evaluated how effectively contact tracing routines identified asymptomatic infected individuals, compared epidemiological characteristics of chlamydia-infected women from different clinical settings, and assessed whether contact tracing data could inform mathematical models of partner choice and disease spread. Screening of asymptomatic patients at family planning clinics revealed a meaningful prevalence of chlamydia, with infection risk significantly associated with younger age, shorter relationship duration, lack of condom use, and no prior genital infection history. Contact tracing integrated into HIV care identified large numbers of previously undetected cases, and strengthened follow-up measures for chlamydia reduced reinfection rates. The study found that partner choice was not well described by a purely random mixing model, with steady partner selection being relatively restricted and casual partner selection following a more random pattern, and concluded that differences between patient groups from screening versus clinical settings were insufficient to justify different approaches to partner management.
items.citation: Kristina Ramstedt. An epidemiological approach to sexually transmitted diseases – with special reference to contact tracing and screening. Acta Dermato Venereologica. 2026

items.title: Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions
items.summary: This paper presents a broad narrative review of compulsive sexual behavior disorder and problematic pornography use, two constructs that remain contested in terms of their nature and classification. Drawing on contributions from experts across psychology, psychiatry, sexology, addiction science, and neuroscience, the authors synthesized current empirical and theoretical knowledge across eleven key thematic areas, ranging from historical context and conceptualization through to etiology, assessment, co-occurring disorders, treatment, and policy. The review also addresses underrepresented groups, including adolescents, women, and LGBTQ+ individuals, as well as the role of cultural factors. The authors identify persistent methodological challenges and conceptual controversies that have hindered progress in the field. The work aims to consolidate interdisciplinary understanding, guide clinical practice, and set priorities for future research and public health efforts in this area.
items.citation: Campbell Ince, Stephanie Antons, Sarah Ashton et al.. Compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD) and problematic pornography use (PPU): A comprehensive, interdisciplinary, and expert-informed narrative review with suggested future directions. Journal of Behavioral Addictions. 2026

items.title: Integrative Proteomics Reveal Neuroimmune and Dopaminergic Alterations Across the Nociceptive Neuraxis in Neuropathic Pain
items.summary: This study investigated the molecular changes occurring across the entire pain-processing neuraxis in neuropathic pain, from peripheral nerve to cortex, with particular attention to neuroinflammatory and neuromodulatory mechanisms. Using a chronic constriction injury rat model, the researchers applied high-resolution quantitative proteomics to simultaneously profile the sciatic nerve, spinal cord, and orbitofrontal cortex, supplementing these findings with behavioral assessments and immunofluorescence validation. Proteomic analysis revealed that neuroinflammatory pathways were activated across all three regions, with S100 proteins showing consistent upregulation alongside markers of astrocyte and microglial activation, indicating a widespread inflammatory state spanning peripheral and central compartments. Notably, the orbitofrontal cortex exhibited pronounced upregulation of dopamine-regulating proteins, implicating reward-related analgesic circuitry in the affective dimension of chronic pain. The authors propose that neuropathic pain is sustained by an interconnected neuroimmune and dopaminergic axis, and identify glial-derived S100 proteins and dopamine modulators as candidate therapeutic targets.
items.citation: Shreyasi Majumdar, Santosh Kumar Prajapati, Aishwarya Dande et al.. Integrative Proteomics Reveal Neuroimmune and Dopaminergic Alterations Across the Nociceptive Neuraxis in Neuropathic Pain. Cells. 2026

items.title: Emulating the nonlinear effects of modified gravity on the matter power spectrum for reconstruction
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational bottleneck of calculating nonlinear matter power spectra for modified gravity models when performing model-independent reconstruction of modified gravity functions. The authors built a neural-network emulator using a large training set of nearly a million samples to predict the nonlinear correction ratio between the nonlinear and linear modified gravity matter power spectra, trained with an established machine-learning framework for cosmological power spectra. The emulator achieves sub-percent to percent-level accuracy across the relevant scale ranges for standard and moderate modified gravity scenarios, and recovers the correct cosmology in synthetic data analyses, demonstrating its reliability for upcoming Stage-IV surveys. Beyond enabling faster likelihood evaluations in high-dimensional parameter spaces, the authors demonstrate additional applications including breaking degeneracies between models with nearly identical linear power spectra, enabling theory predictions for current photometric survey likelihoods, and forecasting constraints from next-generation spectroscopic and imaging surveys using principal component analysis.
items.citation: Lanyang Yi, Kazuya Koyama, Qi Xiong et al.. Emulating the nonlinear effects of modified gravity on the matter power spectrum for reconstruction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field
items.summary: This paper examines a mechanism for producing dark photons as dark matter through the perturbative decay of a dark Higgs field that is displaced from its potential minimum during inflation, a process known as stochastic misalignment. The framework is constrained by two considerations: structure formation limits arising because the produced dark photons are initially relativistic and boosted, and isocurvature fluctuations generated during inflation that require the quartic self-coupling of the dark Higgs to be small. The analysis identifies a viable parameter space spanning dark photon masses between the hundreds-of-eV to GeV range and extremely feeble gauge couplings consistent with generating the observed dark matter relic abundance. The scenario becomes more tightly constrained when a generic level of kinetic mixing between the dark photon and the Standard Model photon is included, opening the possibility of detection through direct detection experiments or diffuse soft gamma-ray searches. Future cosmic microwave background or Lyman-alpha observations are identified as promising probes of the favored parameter region.
items.citation: James M. Cline, Gonzalo Herrera, Jean-Samuel Roux. Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography
items.summary: This paper studies how many copies of an unknown quantum state are needed to estimate or test key properties that depend only on the state's eigenvalues, specifically its spectrum, von Neumann entropy, and rank. The authors prove sample complexity lower bounds showing that these tasks require nearly as many samples as full quantum state tomography, which is known to require a number of copies quadratic in the Hilbert space dimension. To establish these lower bounds, they construct hard-to-distinguish pairs of quantum states built from sandwiched products of Haar-random projectors and develop a novel normalization technique that yields explicit formulas for high-order tensor moments of these states, expressed in terms of symmetric functions of Jucys–Murphy elements from the symmetric group algebra. Indistinguishability of the hard instances is then demonstrated by matching low-order moment components to zero and bounding an appropriate f-divergence using the high-order components, while concentration properties of Haar-random unitaries confirm that the instances genuinely differ in spectrum, entropy, and rank. The results imply that estimating these seemingly simpler unitarily invariant properties is nearly as hard as full tomography, settling questions about the fundamental difficulty of these inference tasks.
items.citation: Marco Fanizza, Ryan O'Donnell, Chirag Wadhwa. Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ArcLP: A Matlab implementation of an $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n}L)$ arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming
items.summary: This paper presents a Matlab software implementation of an arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming that carries the best known polynomial complexity bound among interior-point methods for this problem class. The authors describe the software architecture, key algorithmic strategies, and ease of use, illustrating the latter through a simple worked example. The implementation was extensively tested on the widely used Netlib benchmark suite of linear programming problems, including instances with tens of thousands of constraints and hundreds of thousands of variables, and successfully found optimal solutions for all test cases. Numerical performance was compared against the popular Mehrotra predictor-corrector algorithm, and the authors conclude that their implementation is computationally competitive with that well-established method while also possessing the superior theoretical complexity guarantee.
items.citation: Yang, Yaguang. ArcLP: A Matlab implementation of an $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{n}L)$ arc-search infeasible interior-point algorithm for linear programming. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Fermionic entropy: an efficiently measurable strong monotone for non-Gaussianity
items.summary: This paper studies fermionic non-Gaussianity as a quantum resource, focusing on how to quantify and measure the departure from classically tractable Gaussian states. The authors introduce the fermionic entropy, defined via the squared Frobenius norm of the correlation matrix, and prove it is a strong monotone under Gaussian operations for pure states, meaning it cannot increase under free-fermion processing. A key practical result is that the associated fermionic purity can be estimated with a number of two-copy measurements that is independent of system size, making it experimentally accessible. The authors further establish that fermionic entropy satisfies asymptotic continuity, giving it an operational interpretation as an upper bound on the rate at which non-Gaussianity can be distilled asymptotically, and they derive an improved sample complexity bound for testing whether a state is Gaussian. As an application, they prove that a linear number of non-Gaussian gates is necessary for Matchgate circuits to approximate a quantum state design, matching known upper bounds up to logarithmic factors and revealing the extensive non-Gaussianity cost of generating Haar-random-like dynamics in this setting.
items.citation: Lorenzo Leone, Lennart Bittel. Fermionic entropy: an efficiently measurable strong monotone for non-Gaussianity. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The IACOB project XIX. Revisiting massive-star evolution with empirical TAMS constraints: updated models, overshoot calibration, and the population of blue supergiants
items.summary: This paper investigates the physical processes governing massive-star evolution, with a particular focus on convective boundary mixing and its effect on the main-sequence width, using observational data from the IACOB database of Galactic massive stars. The authors computed multiple grids of stellar evolution models with varying overshoot calibrations, angular momentum transport treatments, initial masses, and rotation rates, then generated synthetic populations for direct comparison with observations. A mass-dependent convective overshoot efficiency was found to be necessary to reproduce the empirical location of the terminal-age main sequence, and models incorporating only hydrodynamical instabilities successfully reproduced the observed rotational properties of the stellar populations, an improvement over previous model grids attributed to updated wind prescriptions. However, the models cannot account for the observed dependence of the terminal-age main sequence location on rotation velocity. Furthermore, single-star evolution models are insufficient to explain the observed population of blue supergiants lying to the right of the terminal-age main sequence, implying that binary interactions are required to account for these objects.
items.citation: Luca Sciarini, Abel de Burgos, Sophie Rosu et al.. The IACOB project XIX. Revisiting massive-star evolution with empirical TAMS constraints: updated models, overshoot calibration, and the population of blue supergiants. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.
items.summary: The paper developed and validated a diagnostic assay for detecting *Shigella flexneri 2a*, the most prevalent cause of shigellosis and a significant public health problem in developing countries. The researchers designed two guide RNAs targeting genes unique to the *S. flexneri 2a* serotype and combined recombinase polymerase amplification with CRISPR-Cas12a collateral cleavage, allowing results to be read via fluorescence or lateral flow without specialized equipment. The assay achieved a detection limit comparable to conventional PCR and demonstrated complete analytical specificity with no cross-reactivity against other bacteria, completing the isothermal reaction within one hour at room temperature. Clinical validation using a large cohort of stool specimens showed diagnostic sensitivity and specificity comparable to PCR, confirming the assay's accuracy in real patient samples. The authors conclude that this approach offers a rapid, simple, and accurate tool well suited for point-of-care diagnostics and field-based surveillance in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Liao J, Su Y, Jiang F. CRISPR-Cas12a assay for rapid and specific detection of <i>Shigella flexneri 2a</i> in clinical samples.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.
items.summary: This review examines a decade of progress in applying CRISPR-Cas technology to infectious diseases across three domains: diagnostics, therapeutic genome editing, and vaccine development. The authors surveyed key platforms and strategies, including rapid pathogen detection tools, CRISPR-Cas9-based approaches to directly targeting viral genomes and antimicrobial resistance, and the engineering of live-attenuated and personalized neoantigen vaccines. They found that diagnostic applications have advanced furthest toward clinical use, while therapeutic and personalized vaccine approaches remain at earlier, more exploratory stages, constrained by challenges in delivery efficiency and safety. The review critically assesses the technical, regulatory, and ethical barriers facing each area and argues that CRISPR-based diagnostics have outpaced therapeutics partly because the latter face greater hurdles around delivery and off-target effects. The authors conclude that although CRISPR-Cas holds transformative potential for managing infectious diseases, substantial challenges must be overcome to achieve safe and equitable clinical translation.
items.citation: Mayuri K, Saravanan KM, Somala CS et al.. CRISPR-Cas and Infectious Diseases: A Decade of Translational Advances in Molecular Biotechnology.. Biochemical genetics. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the current landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the need for decentralized, accessible testing outside conventional laboratory settings. The authors organized their analysis around the three core operational steps of such diagnostics: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. They surveyed extraction strategies including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic approaches, emphasizing designs that are simplified and equipment-free. Amplification methods such as PCR and several isothermal alternatives were assessed for their adaptation to rapid, portable, and low-power conditions. For detection, the review covers a spectrum from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensor platforms incorporating CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch mechanisms, which offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: Improving the Precision of Etiological Diagnosis in Bacterial Infections Using Molecular Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of Platforms, AI Integration, and Point-of-Care Deployment.
items.summary: This review examined the landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies for bacterial infections, with particular emphasis on their role in addressing the challenges posed by antimicrobial resistance and the limitations of conventional culture-based methods. The authors conducted a structured comparative analysis of major platforms including various forms of PCR, isothermal amplification, next-generation sequencing, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and digital PCR, evaluating each against key performance parameters such as sensitivity, specificity, detection limits, turnaround time, and multiplexing capacity. The review also critically assessed the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into molecular diagnostic workflows for resistance prediction and clinical decision support. Additionally, the translational potential of these technologies for point-of-care deployment was considered alongside clinical validation requirements and real-world operational constraints. The authors conclude that advancing culture-independent bacteriological diagnostics requires carefully balancing analytical performance with clinical interpretability, and they outline remaining challenges and future directions for the field.
items.citation: Cotelici AM, Bălășoiu AT, Boldeanu MV et al.. Improving the Precision of Etiological Diagnosis in Bacterial Infections Using Molecular Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of Platforms, AI Integration, and Point-of-Care Deployment.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026

items.title: Wax-in-a-Tube: A Simple, Rapid, One-Pot Platform for Molecular Detection.
items.summary: This paper developed a one-pot molecular detection platform called wax-in-a-tube (WIAT) that combines recombinase polymerase amplification with CRISPR-based detection for nucleic acid identification. The platform uses a molded wax separator integrated directly into the reaction tube to physically partition different reaction components, which melt away during the assay through the wax's phase-change properties, eliminating the need for manual mixing steps such as vortexing or centrifugation that are typical of conventional two-step CRISPR assays. The approach was designed to reduce aerosol contamination risks and simplify workflow while maintaining high sensitivity. Testing against HSV-2 DNA demonstrated detection sensitivity comparable to standard two-step assays, and clinical validation using patient swab samples showed performance on par with PCR. The authors conclude that the WIAT platform represents a simple, rapid, and sensitive approach well suited for point-of-care infectious disease detection.
items.citation: Hou C, Yang R, Guan X et al.. Wax-in-a-Tube: A Simple, Rapid, One-Pot Platform for Molecular Detection.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: Topology-Gated λ Exonuclease Enables Amplification-Free Signal Boosting.
items.summary: This paper investigated a previously unrecognized topological property of λ exonuclease in which duplex DNA substrates bearing 5' phosphates at both ends undergo self-sustained cyclic cleavage and reforming, enabling signal amplification without external nucleic acid amplification steps. Through biochemical and structural analyses, the researchers elucidated this topology-gated mechanism and exploited it by designing a dumbbell-shaped probe that sequesters 5' phosphates within dual RNA hairpin loops until target recognition by CRISPR/Cas13 cleaves the loops and exposes the phosphates, triggering the cyclic enzymatic reaction. The resulting platform, called Topo-CRISPR, achieves attomolar detection sensitivity within a short timeframe and without preamplification. When applied to clinical samples, the system sensitively and specifically detected enterovirus RNA, a microRNA, and a circular RNA, with performance comparable to conventional RT-qPCR, and was further extended to non-nucleic-acid targets through aptamer-based conformational gating. This work repositions λ exonuclease as a topology-driven cyclic signal transducer and provides a broadly applicable framework for ultrasensitive molecular diagnostics.
items.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
items.citation: Feng H, Wang Y, Zhao J et al.. Topology-Gated λ Exonuclease Enables Amplification-Free Signal Boosting.. Journal of the American Chemical Society. 2026

items.title: Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future directions of biosensing technologies designed to detect high-priority foodborne pathogens, including *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Listeria monocytogenes*, which continue to threaten global public health. The authors survey electrochemical, optical, and microfluidic sensing modalities, emphasizing how advances in functional nanomaterials, aptamers, nanozymes, and surface engineering have improved sensor sensitivity, specificity, and performance in complex food matrices. A central theme is the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning with these biosensing platforms, enabling real-time analytics, intelligent pattern recognition, and high-throughput multiplexed detection that transform conventional systems into smart diagnostic tools. The review critically addresses persistent challenges such as matrix interference, bioreceptor instability, manufacturing scalability, and the absence of regulatory standardization, proposing mitigation strategies including ratiometric sensing, microfluidic pre-treatment, explainable AI, and printable electronics. Looking ahead, the authors outline a vision for self-powered biosensors, modular pathogen panel hubs, blockchain-integrated data management, and standardized validation pipelines as pathways toward regulation-ready platforms for next-generation food safety monitoring.
items.citation: Purshottam J. Assudani, Balakrishnan . P., Anny Leema A et al.. Biosensing technologies for foodborne pathogen detection and healthcare: principles, emerging materials, and intelligent platforms. Microchimica Acta. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, commonly known as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their growing role in laboratory medicine. The authors surveyed innovations in chip design and fabrication approaches, including three-dimensional printing, modular architectures, and flexible substrates, alongside the integration of advanced biosensors capable of detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes in real time. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has produced smart diagnostic platforms able to automate analysis, self-optimize, and support clinical decision-making across applications ranging from cancer diagnostics and infectious disease detection to point-of-care testing and personalized medicine. The review also highlights emerging uses in neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling as indicators of the technology's broad clinical potential. The authors additionally address persisting challenges in manufacturing scalability, clinical validation, and system integration, and outline future directions for translating these next-generation platforms into routine clinical and public health practice.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Therapeutic Potential of Extracellular Vesicles: From Biogenesis, Isolation and Molecular Characterization to Addressing Translational Gaps and Regulatory Barriers
items.summary: This review examines extracellular vesicles as intercellular communication mediators that carry lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids reflecting the physiological and pathological state of their originating cells. The paper synthesizes current knowledge spanning EV biogenesis, molecular composition, and classification into major subtypes, alongside advances in isolation techniques, molecular characterization, and omics-based profiling approaches. The authors explore the roles of EVs in viral infection, inflammation, immune regulation, and cancer biology, with particular attention to the therapeutic promise of mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs in regenerative medicine and oncology, as well as modulation of EV signaling through photobiomodulation. The review further addresses the translational obstacles that must be overcome for clinical implementation, including challenges of standardization, scalability, and regulatory validation under existing oversight frameworks. The authors conclude that resolving these barriers through harmonized quality controls and robust safety evaluation will be critical to realizing the transformative potential of EVs as diagnostic and therapeutic tools in precision medicine.
items.citation: Dragan Primorac, Petar Brlek, Luka Bulić et al.. Therapeutic Potential of Extracellular Vesicles: From Biogenesis, Isolation and Molecular Characterization to Addressing Translational Gaps and Regulatory Barriers. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines nanoparticle-based phototherapy systems, which use light-activated mechanisms to modulate cellular pathways across a broad range of diseases. The authors survey the core components and classification of these systems, including gold nanoparticles and hybrid constructs used in photothermal and photodynamic therapy, as well as delivery platforms such as liposomes and dendrimers that refine biodistribution and drug release. At the molecular level, the review details how light-triggered interventions generate reactive oxygen species, induce localized heating, and engage apoptotic, autophagic, and immune signaling cascades relevant to cancer and chronic conditions including cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, metabolic, and autoimmune disorders. The authors also critically evaluate regulatory-approved agents and recent clinical trial data, identifying key barriers to clinical translation such as nanoparticle optimization, effective light delivery, and regulatory challenges. They conclude that nanoparticle-based phototherapy represents a transformative, noninvasive therapeutic strategy with broad potential across disease areas.
items.citation: Deepak S. Chauhan, Rajendra Prasad, Mukesh Dhanka et al.. Nanoparticles-based phototherapy systems: molecular mechanisms and clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Cell death in cancer
items.summary: This review examines the diverse cell death programs relevant to cancer biology and their implications for treatment. The paper consolidates knowledge across apoptosis and more recently characterized modalities—including necroptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis—into a unified framework describing how these programs influence tumor development, progression, and therapeutic response. While apoptosis remains central to conventional radiation and chemotherapy, non-apoptotic programs are shown to drive inflammatory responses and shape interactions between tumor cells, stromal components, and the immune system, with consequences for immunotherapy efficacy. Ferroptosis is highlighted as a distinct mechanism driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation arising from metabolic perturbations rather than a canonical induction signal. The review also addresses how cancer cells evade these death programs and how such evasion contributes to immune suppression and treatment resistance.
items.citation: Marcus Conrad, Andreas Strasser, Philipp J. Jost et al.. Cell death in cancer. Cell. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions
items.summary: This review examined candidemia, a serious bloodstream infection caused by *Candida* species that represents a major source of hospital-acquired infections with high mortality and significant healthcare burden. The authors synthesized current knowledge across the full spectrum of candidemia management, encompassing epidemiology, species distribution, and infection origins, with particular attention to the shortcomings of conventional diagnostic methods and the challenges of optimizing antifungal treatment. The review evaluated both established and emerging diagnostic technologies alongside therapeutic strategies ranging from empiric to susceptibility-guided regimens, while also addressing mixed infections, host-drug interactions, and the growing problem of antifungal resistance. Combination therapy and novel antifungal agents currently in clinical development, including compounds directed at new fungal targets, were highlighted as promising avenues for overcoming resistance. The authors additionally identified future directions including artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, vaccine-based prophylaxis, and synergistic treatment approaches as areas with potential to transform candidemia management.
items.citation: Haojie Dong, Minghui Song, Jingfang Sun et al.. Comprehensive Review on Candidemia: Epidemiology, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Future Directions. iFungi. 2026

items.title: Online Shadow Tomography Matching the Classical Bounds
items.summary: This paper studies Online Shadow Tomography, the quantum analogue of the classical Adaptive Data Analysis problem, where one must sequentially estimate expectation values of adaptively chosen bounded observables on an unknown quantum state using as few copies as possible. Prior algorithms for this problem were suboptimal in all relevant parameters compared to the best classical rates. The authors introduce two new algorithms that match the classical bounds, achieving improved dependence on the number of measurements, the dimension of the state, and the estimation accuracy, with one result also improving known bounds in the offline setting. The central technical contribution is a new framework for quantifying the disturbance caused by quantum measurements, built on a quantum analogue of the Efron–Stein decomposition. One of the resulting bounds is known to be optimal among dimension-independent bounds and substantially improves upon previous work.
items.citation: Sitan Chen, Ryan O'Donnell, Angelos Pelecanos et al.. Online Shadow Tomography Matching the Classical Bounds. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field
items.summary: This paper investigates dark photons as a dark matter candidate produced through the perturbative decay of a dark Higgs field that is displaced from its potential minimum during inflation via stochastic misalignment. The authors analyze the relic abundance generated in this framework and identify the constraints it must satisfy, including limits from structure formation arising because the dark photons are initially relativistically boosted, and from inflationary isocurvature fluctuations that require small quartic couplings. They map out viable regions of parameter space in terms of dark photon mass and gauge coupling that are consistent with all constraints, and further restrict these regions when kinetic mixing with the Standard Model photon is allowed. The study finds that the favored parameter space could be probed by future cosmic microwave background or Lyman-alpha observations, and, if kinetic mixing is present, by direct detection experiments or diffuse soft gamma-ray searches.
items.citation: James M. Cline, Gonzalo Herrera, Jean-Samuel Roux. Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Lean-verified lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of odd cycles
items.summary: This paper establishes new lower bounds on the Shannon capacity of several small odd cycles, a long-standing open problem in information theory and combinatorics. The bounds were derived using an iterative computational procedure that builds on recently developed methods for constructing independent sets in graph tensor products. The results span odd cycles from length seven to twenty-three, improving upon previously known values. Crucially, all bounds were fully formalized and machine-verified using the Lean proof assistant, providing a high level of mathematical certainty for the numerical claims.
items.citation: Pjotr Buys, Sven Polak, Jeroen Zuiddam. Lean-verified lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of odd cycles. arXiv. 2026

items.title: TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving
items.summary: This paper investigates the overhead of tokenization in large language model serving systems, specifically in agentic settings where models repeatedly process long transcripts with small appended tool results. The authors analyze real-world agent traffic and find that re-tokenizing full request text on every call becomes a significant bottleneck, accounting for up to nearly two-thirds of time to first token at high prompt-cache hit rates. To address this, they introduce TokTier, a stateful tokenization service that maintains session context and performs incremental repair by re-tokenizing only a small window around newly appended text, with a correctness guarantee that output token IDs are always identical to full reference tokenization. For requests lacking reusable prefixes, TokTier decomposes the tokenization pipeline to run exact pre-tokenization and byte-pair encoding on a GPU. The system is validated with zero divergence across extensive differential testing and demonstrates dramatic throughput and latency improvements over both standard and cache-optimized baselines, with median time to first token dropping substantially and sustained request throughput increasing by more than an order of magnitude under a strict latency objective.
items.citation: Zhenyu Zhang, Zhichao Cao. TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR
items.summary: This paper studies the computational complexity of planted noisy k-XOR detection and random k-XOR refutation, problems where a conjectured smooth trade-off between sample complexity and runtime is parameterized by the level of the Kikuchi hierarchy. Prior spectral analyses of sparse k-XOR consistently incurred polylogarithmic losses relative to this conjectured curve, which degraded the running time exponent. The authors introduce a normalized variant of the Kikuchi hierarchy and prove that it achieves the sharp conjectured trade-off with no logarithmic loss at every arity k≥3, enabling strong detection, weak recovery, exact recovery, and strong refutation with sum-of-squares certificates. They also establish matching computational lower bounds in the same model, extend the results to more general planting laws and predicates, and present a quantum algorithm achieving a quartic speedup over classical spectral methods for detection and weak recovery. The technical core relies on a careful normalization of the sparse Kikuchi matrix and a sharp combinatorial count of closed walks in its trace expansion.
items.citation: Alexander Schmidhuber, Matthew B. Hastings. The Kikuchi Hierarchy is Sharp for $k$XOR. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents
items.summary: This paper investigates whether procedural knowledge from past software repair attempts can be systematically reused to improve future automated repairs, rather than discarding that experience after each fix. The authors introduce STAIR, a framework that transforms historical repair trajectories into hierarchical, multi-level tree structures capturing everything from fine-grained diagnostic actions to high-level repair strategies. When a new issue is encountered, STAIR retrieves relevant nodes across abstraction levels, adapts them into issue-specific executable plans, and injects these plans into the agent's prompt. Evaluated on a standard software engineering benchmark, the approach achieves strong task resolution rates and notably generalizes across structurally different agents without any modification to the agents themselves. Ablation studies confirm that blending multiple abstraction levels outperforms relying on any single level, and that raw, unabstracted trajectories transfer considerably less effectively than the hierarchical representations.
items.citation: Yisen Xu, Jiayuan Zhou, Ruiqi Pan et al.. Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.
items.summary: This study investigated whether a low-cost, noninvasive electronic nose could reliably detect SARS-CoV-2 infection as an alternative to conventional diagnostic methods. The device used an array of commercially available metal-oxide gas sensors to analyze volatile organic compounds present in both saliva and exhaled breath samples, which shift in composition in response to viral infection. Several machine learning algorithms were trained and compared to classify infected versus non-infected samples from a real-world hospital cohort. Detection performance varied across algorithms and sample types, with exhaled breath yielding slightly better discrimination than saliva, and the K-Nearest Neighbors algorithm achieving the strongest results overall. The findings support the proof-of-concept feasibility of this approach for point-of-care SARS-CoV-2 screening, though performance remains below the threshold typically required for clinical deployment.
items.venue: The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases
items.citation: Fialkovitz G, Sousa PL, Hidifira AM et al.. Noninvasive SARS-CoV-2 detection using a low-cost electronic nose.. The Brazilian journal of infectious diseases : an official publication of the Brazilian Society of Infectious Diseases. 2026

items.title: Multiniche mycobiome profiling identifies distinctive fungal dysbiosis in common variable immunodeficiency.
items.summary: This study investigated the fungal microbiome (mycobiome) across multiple body compartments in patients with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), a condition previously linked to bacterial dysbiosis but not well characterized in terms of its fungal communities. Using ITS1 amplicon sequencing of saliva, sputum, and stool samples from adults with CVID and healthy controls, the researchers performed diversity analyses, differential abundance testing, and machine learning classification. They found that mycobiome composition differed substantially between CVID patients and controls across all three body sites, with reduced fungal richness and evenness particularly in respiratory and oral samples. A consistent pattern of enrichment in opportunistic yeasts, especially *Candida albicans*, was observed in CVID patients regardless of whether they had immune dysregulation or infectious-only manifestations, while commensal and environmental fungi were depleted. Fungal signatures demonstrated strong discriminatory power in distinguishing CVID patients from healthy controls, supporting their potential as non-invasive biomarkers and implicating *C. albicans* as a possible pathobiont in this immunodeficiency.
items.citation: Cabanero-Navalon MD, Carda-Diéguez M, Mira A et al.. Multiniche mycobiome profiling identifies distinctive fungal dysbiosis in common variable immunodeficiency.. Frontiers in immunology. 2026

items.title: Salivary exosomal <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i> DNA enables sensitive detection of paucibacillary tuberculosis: a molecular diagnosis study.
items.summary: This study investigated whether tuberculosis could be diagnosed using salivary exosomal DNA as a non-sputum-based approach, particularly in patients with paucibacillary disease who are difficult to detect by conventional methods. The researchers developed an exosomal nucleic acid assay that integrates salivary exosome enrichment, nucleic acid extraction, and dual-target quantitative PCR melting curve analysis, reducing turnaround time substantially compared to standard methods. In a pilot clinical study enrolling adults with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis, the majority of whom had negative smear microscopy results, the assay demonstrated moderate sensitivity and specificity against both standard and extended microbiological reference standards. Salivary exosomal DNA was identified as the predominant detectable form of Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA in saliva, and diagnostic performance was maintained in the smear-negative subgroup. The authors conclude that this non-invasive, rapid saliva-based assay shows promise for tuberculosis diagnosis but requires multicenter validation in more diverse populations before clinical implementation.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Ma J, Zheng X, He Y et al.. Salivary exosomal <i>Mycobacterium tuberculosis</i> DNA enables sensitive detection of paucibacillary tuberculosis: a molecular diagnosis study.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that enable long-term comfort and stable integration with the body, alongside multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. The role of artificial intelligence in enhancing signal processing and generating predictive health insights is also addressed. The review identifies persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and clinical interpretability that must be overcome for broader deployment. Overall, the paper synthesizes developments across materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies to map the landscape of next-generation biosensor systems.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration
items.summary: This review paper examines recent advances in microfluidic chip technology, commonly referred to as lab-on-a-chip systems, and their growing role in laboratory medicine and clinical diagnostics. The authors conducted a comprehensive review of innovations in chip design and fabrication approaches, including three-dimensional printing and flexible and modular substrates, alongside developments in biosensor integration for detecting circulating tumor cells, nucleic acids, and exosomes. A central focus is the convergence of microfluidics with artificial intelligence and machine learning, which has enabled the creation of smart diagnostic platforms capable of self-optimization, automated analysis, and clinical decision support across applications ranging from cancer diagnostics and infectious disease detection to point-of-care testing and personalized medicine. The review also highlights emerging uses in neuroscience diagnostics and microbiome profiling, demonstrating the broad clinical potential of these systems. The authors additionally address ongoing challenges related to manufacturing, clinical validation, and system integration, and outline future directions for bringing next-generation microfluidic technologies into routine clinical and public health settings.
items.citation: Hong Cai, Dongxia Wang, Yiqun Zhao et al.. Recent Advances in Microfluidic Chip Technology for Laboratory Medicine: Innovations and Artificial Intelligence Integration. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Therapeutic Potential of Extracellular Vesicles: From Biogenesis, Isolation and Molecular Characterization to Addressing Translational Gaps and Regulatory Barriers
items.summary: This review examines extracellular vesicles as mediators of intercellular communication and their potential as diagnostic and therapeutic tools in human disease. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning EV biogenesis, molecular composition, and classification into major subtypes, alongside advances in isolation techniques, molecular characterization, and omics-based profiling approaches. Particular attention is given to the roles of EVs in viral infection, inflammation, immune regulation, and cancer biology, as well as the therapeutic promise of mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs in regenerative medicine and oncology. The review also highlights the emerging use of photobiomodulation as a means of therapeutically modulating EV signaling. Finally, the authors address translational barriers including the need for standardization, scalability, and harmonized regulatory frameworks under existing FDA and EMA oversight, framing EVs as transformative candidates for next-generation precision medicine applications.
items.citation: Dragan Primorac, Petar Brlek, Luka Bulić et al.. Therapeutic Potential of Extracellular Vesicles: From Biogenesis, Isolation and Molecular Characterization to Addressing Translational Gaps and Regulatory Barriers. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. 2026

items.title: The Oral Microbiome and Systemic Health: Current Insights into the Mouth–Body Connection
items.summary: This narrative review examined the relationship between the oral microbiome and systemic health, focusing on how disturbances in oral microbial communities may contribute to disease beyond the mouth. The authors conducted a comprehensive database search spanning recent years, ultimately synthesizing evidence from dozens of studies including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and mechanistic investigations. The review found clear associations between oral dysbiosis and conditions such as cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic respiratory infections, and adverse pregnancy outcomes, with emerging links also identified for neurodegenerative disorders, chronic kidney disease, autoimmune diseases, and cancer. Proposed mechanisms underlying these connections include bacteraemia, systemic inflammation driven by microbial metabolites and endotoxins, immune homeostasis disruption, molecular mimicry, and modulation of host metabolic pathways. The authors caution that most current evidence is observational and that establishing causal relationships will require longitudinal and interventional studies, while highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting oral microbial activity and host inflammatory responses.
items.citation: Ana Glavina, Dora Martić, Mark Perko et al.. The Oral Microbiome and Systemic Health: Current Insights into the Mouth–Body Connection. Life. 2026

items.title: Gastroduodenal Disorders
items.summary: This paper presents a classification framework for gastroduodenal disorders based on symptom patterns attributable to the gastroduodenal region. The authors organized these conditions into five main categories encompassing functional dyspepsia, nausea and vomiting disorders, excessive belching disorders, inability to belch syndrome, and rumination syndrome, with several categories further divided into subcategories. Notable features of the classification include the distinction between meal-related and non-meal-related dyspeptic symptoms, the separation of different nausea and vomiting syndromes including cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome, and the introduction of inability to belch syndrome as a new diagnostic category. The framework provides structured diagnostic criteria for each condition, aiming to improve clinical recognition and categorization of functional gastroduodenal symptoms.
items.citation: H. Tornblom, Florencia Carbone, William L. Hasler et al.. Gastroduodenal Disorders. Gastroenterology. 2026

items.title: Electrochemical Biosensors for Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis Using Protein Biomarkers: Current Trends, Advances, and Clinical Translation Potential
items.summary: This review examines electrochemical biosensors designed for the detection of cancer-related protein biomarkers in blood, with the goal of enabling early cancer diagnosis and prognosis through non-invasive liquid biopsy approaches. The authors critically survey general electrochemical detection strategies for serum proteins and catalog recent advances in biosensors targeting circulating cancer-associated proteins, noting that many have demonstrated impressive analytical sensitivity. The review then turns to the substantial challenges that impede clinical translation and commercialization, including matrix effects from complex biological samples, insufficient validation with real patient specimens, interpatient variability, and practical hurdles such as manufacturing scalability, cost, and device stability. Particular emphasis is placed on the analytical and clinical validation steps necessary to move these technologies from the laboratory toward routine clinical use. The authors conclude that while the field has advanced considerably, rigorous standardization and more extensive patient-based validation remain critical unmet needs before electrochemical biosensors can achieve widespread clinical adoption.
items.citation: Michael E. J. Lopez Mujica, Elena E. Ferapontova. Electrochemical Biosensors for Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis Using Protein Biomarkers: Current Trends, Advances, and Clinical Translation Potential. Sensors. 2026

items.title: Online Shadow Tomography Matching the Classical Bounds
items.summary: This paper studies Online Shadow Tomography, the quantum generalization of the classical Adaptive Data Analysis problem, where one must estimate expectation values of adversarially chosen observables on an unknown quantum state using as few copies of that state as possible. Prior quantum algorithms for this task were suboptimal in all relevant parameters compared to the best classical rates, and this work closes that gap entirely by presenting two algorithms that match classical bounds. One algorithm achieves improved dependence on all three key parameters simultaneously, also yielding improvements in the offline setting, while the other achieves a result known to be optimal among dimension-independent bounds and substantially improves upon the previous best result by a polynomial factor in the number of measurements. The central technical contribution is a new framework for bounding the disturbance caused by quantum measurements, built upon a quantum analogue of the Efron–Stein decomposition.
items.citation: Sitan Chen, Ryan O'Donnell, Angelos Pelecanos et al.. Online Shadow Tomography Matching the Classical Bounds. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Emulating the nonlinear effects of modified gravity on the matter power spectrum for reconstruction
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational bottleneck in constraining modified gravity through nonlinear cosmological observables, where repeated evaluations of the nonlinear matter power spectrum are prohibitively expensive for exploring high-dimensional parameter spaces. The authors built a neural-network emulator trained on nearly a million samples using the CosmoPower framework to predict the ratio of the nonlinear to linear modified gravity matter power spectrum, thereby capturing the nonlinear correction efficiently. The emulator achieves sub-percent to low-percent level accuracy across the relevant scales for standard cosmology and moderate modified gravity scenarios, with slightly reduced but still acceptable accuracy at smaller scales in extreme nonlinear cases. Validation through independent sample sets and synthetic data Markov chain Monte Carlo analyses confirms the emulator reliably recovers standard cosmological parameters and the general relativity limits of reconstructed modified gravity functions, demonstrating readiness for Stage-IV survey analyses. The authors further illustrate practical applications including breaking degeneracies between models with nearly identical linear spectra, enabling current photometric survey likelihood analyses, and forecasting joint survey constraints using principal component analysis.
items.citation: Lanyang Yi, Kazuya Koyama, Qi Xiong et al.. Emulating the nonlinear effects of modified gravity on the matter power spectrum for reconstruction. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field
items.summary: This paper examines a mechanism for producing dark photons as dark matter through the perturbative decay of a dark Higgs field that is displaced from its potential minimum during inflation, a process known as stochastic misalignment. The authors analyze the constraints on this framework arising from structure formation, since the produced dark photons are initially relativistic and boosted, and from inflationary isocurvature fluctuations, which require small quartic couplings in the Higgs potential. They identify a viable parameter space of dark photon masses and gauge couplings consistent with the observed dark matter relic abundance, finding that the allowed region becomes more restricted when kinetic mixing with the Standard Model photon is included. The study concludes that the favored parameter space could be probed by future cosmic microwave background or Lyman-alpha observations, and, if kinetic mixing is present, by direct detection experiments or diffuse soft gamma-ray searches.
items.citation: James M. Cline, Gonzalo Herrera, Jean-Samuel Roux. Dark Photons from Perturbative Decay of a Misaligned Higgs Field. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Lean-verified lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of odd cycles
items.summary: The paper establishes new lower bounds for the Shannon capacities of several small odd cycles, a long-standing open problem in information theory and combinatorics concerning the zero-error capacity of noisy communication channels. The bounds were derived using an iterative computational procedure built on a previously developed method, applied to odd cycles with specific numbers of vertices. A key contribution is that all bounds have been fully formalized and verified using the Lean proof assistant, providing machine-checked certificates of correctness for the numerical results.
items.citation: Pjotr Buys, Sven Polak, Jeroen Zuiddam. Lean-verified lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of odd cycles. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography
items.summary: This paper investigates how many copies of an unknown quantum state are required to estimate or test its fundamental properties, specifically its spectrum, von Neumann entropy, and rank. The authors establish lower bounds on sample complexity for these tasks in terms of the dimension of the quantum state, showing that nearly quadratically many copies are needed—approaching the known complexity of full quantum state tomography. To construct hard instances, they developed a novel technique involving sandwiched products of Haar-random projectors and analyzed high-order tensor moments using symmetric functions of Jucys–Murphy elements from the symmetric group algebra. Indistinguishability between constructed state mixtures was demonstrated through moment-matching and bounding an f-divergence, with concentration arguments confirming that the hard instances genuinely differ in their spectra, entropies, and ranks. The results suggest that estimating even these seemingly simpler, unitarily invariant properties is nearly as difficult as full state tomography.
items.citation: Marco Fanizza, Ryan O'Donnell, Chirag Wadhwa. Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography. arXiv. 2026

items.title: TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving
items.summary: This paper addresses the performance bottleneck of tokenization in large language model serving systems, particularly for agentic workloads where a long conversation transcript is resubmitted with each new tool result. The authors observed that in real agent deployments, most calls append only a small amount of text to an existing session, yet standard systems re-tokenize the entire input from scratch each time, which can consume a substantial fraction of time to first token when prompt caching is otherwise highly effective. To solve this, they developed TokTier, a stateful tokenization service that maintains session context and repairs only the token boundary region around a new text append, with a correctness guarantee that output token IDs are always identical to full reference tokenization. For cases without a reusable prefix, they decompose the tokenization pipeline and execute it on a GPU, achieving dramatic speedups over CPU-based methods. The system was validated across many tokenizer families with extensive differential testing and showed large reductions in median and tail latency when integrated with a production serving framework, while supporting far higher request throughput than a stateless front end under tight latency objectives.
items.citation: Zhenyu Zhang, Zhichao Cao. TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Why Andes hantavirus is not the next SARS-CoV-2: contrasting viral shedding, transmissibility and genomic patterns.
items.summary: The paper examined why Andes hantavirus, despite a cruise ship-associated outbreak raising concerns about respiratory spread, should not be considered analogous to SARS-CoV-2 in terms of pandemic potential. The authors compared the two viruses across multiple dimensions, including routes of transmission, pathogenesis, diagnostic approaches, and genomic evolutionary patterns. They argue that although Andes virus can enter via the respiratory route and spread between humans under close contact, it differs fundamentally from SARS-CoV-2 in being rodent-borne with vascular rather than respiratory pathogenesis, diagnosed through blood-based methods, and with genetic diversity driven by reservoir ecology and geography rather than sustained human-to-human transmission and immune selection. The paper concludes that these contrasting biological and epidemiological characteristics preclude Andes hantavirus from posing the kind of pandemic risk represented by SARS-CoV-2.
items.venue: Euro surveillance : bulletin Europeen sur les maladies transmissibles = European communicable disease bulletin
items.citation: Bal A, Sauvage V, Bouscambert-Duchamp M et al.. Why Andes hantavirus is not the next SARS-CoV-2: contrasting viral shedding, transmissibility and genomic patterns.. Euro surveillance : bulletin Europeen sur les maladies transmissibles = European communicable disease bulletin. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for decentralized, rapid, and accessible testing. The authors organize their analysis around the three core operational steps of such diagnostics: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, they evaluate approaches including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic methods with an emphasis on simplicity and portability. They survey amplification technologies such as PCR and several isothermal alternatives that have been adapted for low-power and field-deployable conditions, then review detection platforms ranging from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensors incorporating CRISPR/Cas systems and toehold switch principles. The review concludes that ongoing innovations across all three steps are converging to make sensitive, selective, and economically viable nucleic acid diagnostics increasingly feasible outside conventional laboratory settings.
items.citation: Hatem H, Mysara M, Ramadan R. Trends of nucleic acid - based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases.. Journal of biological engineering. 2026

items.title: Performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A for detection of <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i> from pediatric pleural fluids.
items.summary: The paper investigated whether the Xpert Xpress Strep A, a rapid quantitative PCR assay originally designed for throat swabs, could effectively detect *Streptococcus pyogenes* from pediatric pleural fluid specimens, where standard bacterial culture often yields falsely negative results. Researchers evaluated a convenience sample of pleural fluid specimens against a composite reference standard combining bacterial culture and a laboratory-developed PCR assay targeting a separate gene. Xpert detected all confirmed positive specimens, achieving perfect agreement with the composite reference standard, whereas culture alone identified only a minority of those same positive cases. The substantial gap in sensitivity between Xpert and culture was attributed largely to prior antibiotic exposure in patients before sample collection. The authors conclude that Xpert Xpress Strep A offers superior sensitivity over culture for diagnosing invasive Group A streptococcal pneumonia from pleural fluid, with the added benefit of faster turnaround time to guide clinical management and public health chemoprophylaxis decisions.
items.citation: Amaral G, Gadkar VJ, Almodahka A et al.. Performance of the Xpert Xpress Strep A for detection of <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i> from pediatric pleural fluids.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research
items.summary: This review paper examines graphene oxide as a multifunctional two-dimensional carbon-based nanomaterial, surveying its synthesis chemistry, property modification strategies, and potential across a broad range of applications in energy, environment, and healthcare. The authors highlight how the layered structure of graphene oxide enables extensive surface functionalization and tunability of properties, including adjustable band gap, high surface area, and optoelectronic and mechanical characteristics, allowing configurations spanning zero- to three-dimensional nanostructures. The review covers applications including photocatalytic degradation of pollutants and microplastics, adsorption of toxic substances and pathogens, carbon dioxide photoreduction, hydrogen production, battery technologies, and ultrasensitive sensing via surface-enhanced Raman scattering. The authors also assess graphene oxide's role in healthcare platforms and emphasize its broader industrial relevance as a sustainable nanomaterial. Alongside this expansive potential, the review acknowledges persistent challenges such as scalability, long-term stability, and reproducibility, and proposes possible solutions to support its sustainable future deployment.
items.citation: S.N. Thakur, Ayush Badoni, Rupam Sharma et al.. Graphene oxide as smart sustainable nanomaterial: a versatile multifunctional material with transformative potential in advanced materials science research. npj Materials Sustainability. 2026
