items.title: Infectious disease diagnostic competencies of medical students as a fundamental basis for physicians' resilience in addressing future infectious disease challenges.
items.summary: This paper examines the role of infectious disease diagnostic competencies in medical education, arguing that these skills are foundational to building a resilient medical workforce capable of responding to future infectious disease challenges. The authors contend that training in medical microbiology, virology, and hygiene must encompass a broad understanding of epidemiology, prevention, diagnostics, and therapy within a One-Health framework that considers impacts on individuals, society, animals, and ecosystems. They emphasize that proficiency in rapid and appropriate infection diagnostics underpins rational antimicrobial therapy and is therefore critical to combating the development of multidrug-resistant pathogens. The paper argues that competencies such as correct sample collection, appropriate test selection, and critical interpretation of microbiological findings cannot be acquired through self-directed learning alone but require structured, hands-on, practice-oriented education. The authors conclude that time- and cost-intensive practical courses in this field are indispensable and should not be displaced by competing educational offerings.
items.citation: Brandt C, Becker K, Ciesek S et al.. Infectious disease diagnostic competencies of medical students as a fundamental basis for physicians' resilience in addressing future infectious disease challenges.. GMS infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: From Control to Eradication: The Role of Point-of-Care Testing in Modernising Australia's Bovine Viral Diarrhoea (BVD) Disease Management.
items.summary: This review examines the current state of Bovine Viral Diarrhoea Virus management in Australia and evaluates the potential of point-of-care diagnostics to shift national strategy from disease control toward eradication. The authors analyse how Australia's decentralised, non-compulsory biosecurity framework has produced a fragmented approach that leaves the burden of management to individual producers, hindering coordinated action. The review focuses on persistently infected animals as the primary transmission reservoir and argues that their rapid identification through field-deployable technologies—including lateral flow assays, nucleic acid amplification tests, and biosensors—is essential for any effective eradication program. The authors propose that integrating these point-of-care tools with robust biosecurity protocols and optimised vaccination strategies would provide a scientifically sound and commercially viable pathway to systematic national eradication of the disease.
items.citation: Ogada S, Naseem MN, Ranjbar S et al.. From Control to Eradication: The Role of Point-of-Care Testing in Modernising Australia's Bovine Viral Diarrhoea (BVD) Disease Management.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: The International Guideline for the Definition, Classification, Diagnosis and Management of Urticaria
items.summary: This paper presents an updated international clinical guideline for urticaria, a mast cell-driven disease characterized by wheals, angioedema, or both. The guideline was developed using Cochrane methods and the GRADE framework, with input from a large multinational consensus conference involving delegates from numerous national and international societies across dozens of countries. The document addresses the definition, classification, diagnosis, and management of urticaria, covering both acute and chronic forms, including chronic spontaneous and chronic inducible subtypes. The guideline emphasizes that chronic urticaria significantly impairs quality of life and functioning, while noting that novel therapeutic options are now available. The resulting recommendations are expert-guided and evidence-based, and have received formal acknowledgment from the European Union of Medical Specialists.
items.citation: T. Zuberbier, Z. Abdul Hameed Ansari, A. H. Abdul Latiff et al.. The International Guideline for the Definition, Classification, Diagnosis and Management of Urticaria. Allergy. 2026

items.title: EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update
items.summary: These updated guidelines address the management of rheumatoid arthritis using synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, incorporating the most recent clinical evidence. An international task force conducted systematic literature reviews on the efficacy and safety of these agents and used a structured voting process to revise and consolidate the recommendations. The update reduced the total number of recommendations and reaffirmed a treat-to-target strategy beginning with methotrexate, ideally combined with short-term glucocorticoids, followed by the addition of a biologic agent if response is insufficient after several months. Janus kinase inhibitors remain an option after careful consideration of individual patient risks, including major cardiovascular events, malignancies, and thromboembolic events, and switching between drug classes is supported when initial therapies fail. The recommendations also address tapering of therapy in sustained remission while cautioning that complete discontinuation frequently leads to disease flare.
items.citation: Josef S. Smolen, Christopher J. Edwards, Victoria Konzett et al.. EULAR recommendations for the management of rheumatoid arthritis with synthetic and biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs: 2025 update. Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases. 2026

items.title: Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease
items.summary: This review examines the role of lipid metabolism in maintaining cellular homeostasis and how its dysregulation contributes to a broad range of diseases. The authors surveyed the research history of lipid metabolism and focused particularly on how lipid metabolites regulate the proliferation, differentiation, and activation of immune cells including macrophages, T cells, B cells, and neutrophils, thereby influencing both innate and adaptive immunity. The review discusses lipid transport, signaling pathways, and multilevel regulatory mechanisms spanning genetic, epigenetic, posttranscriptional, and posttranslational processes that govern immune cell function. The paper further explores how aberrant lipid metabolism contributes to conditions such as autoimmune diseases, cancer, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, metabolic disorders, and aging. Finally, the authors outline current and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism, survey ongoing clinical trials, and propose lipid-derived biomarkers and novel treatment approaches as future directions.
items.citation: Zhili Li, Wende Deng, Lanxuan Yang et al.. Lipid metabolism in homeostasis and disease. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Food and Medicine Homology Focus in 2026
items.summary: This perspective paper examines the current trajectory and anticipated future directions of the food and medicine homology field, which integrates traditional knowledge about substances that serve both nutritional and therapeutic purposes. The authors argue that the field is shifting toward greater scientific rigor, calling for systematic mechanistic research into active components, gut microbiota interactions, phase separation, and immunometabolic reprogramming. They envision precision medicine approaches that use multidimensional personal data and artificial intelligence to develop individualized interventions for chronic diseases and aging populations. The paper also anticipates industrial transformation through synthetic biology, intelligent delivery systems, and sustainable manufacturing to create a more transparent and evidence-based regulatory framework. Overall, the perspective outlines a roadmap for modernizing the field by bridging empirical tradition with contemporary scientific and technological methodologies.
items.citation: Mengyao Li, Gui-Fen Wu, Feng Lu et al.. Food and Medicine Homology Focus in 2026. Food & medicine homology.. 2026

items.title: Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration
items.summary: This review examines the current state of smart wearable and implantable biosensors designed for continuous, real-time monitoring of biophysical and biochemical signals in the context of personalized and preventive healthcare. The paper surveys advances in flexible, stretchable, and biocompatible materials that enable long-term comfort and integration with the body, alongside multimodal and multi-analyte sensing approaches that improve measurement robustness. It also reviews how artificial intelligence is being applied to enhance signal processing and generate predictive health insights. The authors identify persistent challenges including motion artifacts, energy autonomy, data privacy, and the clinical interpretability of sensor outputs. The review synthesizes progress across materials science, device architecture, and AI-assisted strategies to outline the landscape and remaining obstacles in the field.
items.citation: Thirumalaisamy Suryaprabha, Chunghyeon Choi, Yanfang Wu et al.. Smart wearable and implantable biosensors for continuous health monitoring: materials, biocompatibility, and AI integration. npj Flexible Electronics. 2026

items.title: Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents
items.summary: This paper investigates whether procedural knowledge accumulated from past software repairs can be systematically reused to improve future repairs by LLM-driven coding agents. The authors introduce STAIR, a framework that converts historical repair trajectories into hierarchical, multi-level tree structures capturing experience ranging from fine-grained diagnostic actions to high-level repair strategies. When a new issue arises, STAIR retrieves relevant nodes from these abstracted plans, adapts them into issue-specific guidance, and injects them into the agent's prompt. Evaluated on a standard software engineering benchmark, the approach achieves strong repair success rates and notably transfers to structurally different agents without any code modification. Ablation studies confirm that combining multiple abstraction levels outperforms any single level and that raw, unabstracted trajectories transfer substantially less effectively than the hierarchical representations.
items.citation: Yisen Xu, Jiayuan Zhou, Ruiqi Pan et al.. Reusing Past Repairs Through Hierarchical Trajectory Abstraction for Coding Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of fragmented and non-interoperable knowledge in HVAC fault detection and diagnosis by developing a formal ontology called FDD-ON. The researchers constructed a modular and extensible ontology specifically designed to represent variable air volume HVAC system components, fault types, symptom statuses, fault impacts, and their interrelationships using well-defined controlled vocabulary. FDD-ON explicitly encodes cause-fault-symptom-impact relationships to enable machine-interpretable querying of diagnostic knowledge and to bridge heterogeneous data sources and diverse equipment types. The ontology was evaluated using publicly available VAV HVAC datasets and demonstrated through practical FDD application development. The authors claim that FDD-ON provides a foundational semantic framework capable of supporting scalable, transparent, and interoperable fault detection and diagnosis solutions, including digital twin frameworks and AI-driven maintenance systems.
items.citation: Yimin Chen, Brian Fricke, Bo Shen et al.. Development of FDD-ON: an Ontology for VAV HVAC System Fault Detection and Diagnostics. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations
items.summary: This paper develops the theoretical basis for a novel assessment approach called the "Socratic Test," which aims to overcome the limitations of both traditional written exams and face-to-face oral examinations. The authors argue that static assessments penalize ambitious attempts while oral exams introduce biases stemming from anxiety and power imbalances between students and evaluators. Their proposed solution is an automated, computer-mediated conversational assessment that integrates Dynamic Assessment principles, Bloom's Taxonomy for real-time monitoring of cognitive engagement, and the SOLO Taxonomy for evaluating structural quality of responses. The framework formalizes graduated scaffolding as a means of quantifying a student's Zone of Proximal Development, thereby mapping the boundaries of their current knowledge rather than simply measuring fixed performance. The paper also details a non-compensatory, additive grading architecture designed to reward demonstrated mastery and improve measurement reliability through human-AI alignment.
items.citation: Ilya Mikhelson. The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the use of field RR Lyrae as Galactic probes:. IX. Radial velocities
items.summary: This paper presents a large, homogeneous catalog of radial velocity measurements for field RR Lyrae variable stars, drawing on both proprietary and publicly available spectroscopic observations spanning fundamental mode, first overtone, and double-mode pulsators. Radial velocity curve templates for metallic and Balmer lines were applied to derive velocity amplitudes and systemic barycentric velocities, with accuracy depending on how well the radial velocity curves were sampled. The study finds that metallicity has negligible influence on radial velocity amplitudes measured from metallic lines but an increasingly significant effect for higher Balmer lines, interpreted as evidence that convection differentially affects luminosity and radial velocity amplitudes across the instability strip. Scaling relations between photometric and radial velocity amplitudes are linear for first-overtone pulsators but nonlinear for fundamental-mode pulsators regardless of spectroscopic diagnostic used. Additionally, the spectroscopic Bailey diagram reveals a smoother period–amplitude relationship with reduced scatter when accounting for metallicity, and the metallicity distribution of Blazhko-effect RR Lyrae stars appears skewed toward more metal-rich compositions.
items.citation: K. Baeza-Villagra, V. F. Braga, M. Fabrizio et al.. On the use of field RR Lyrae as Galactic probes:. IX. Radial velocities. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Spindrift: Learning quantum degeneracy from thermal purity in restricted path integral Monte Carlo
items.summary: This paper addresses the fixed-node error problem in restricted path integral Monte Carlo, where the quality of results depends critically on an externally supplied nodal surface for the fermionic density matrix. The authors introduce Spindrift, a variational density matrix method that learns the many-body fermionic density matrix self-consistently by minimizing a regularized Bloch residual evaluated on samples from a restricted Worm algorithm. The approach uses a temperature curriculum, exploiting the fact that quantum statistics become simpler at high temperatures, and progressively learns corrections to a free-particle reference as temperature decreases; the density matrix is parameterized using a permutation-equivariant continuous normalizing flow with a Jastrow factor, ensuring exact fermionic antisymmetry throughout training. Applied to interacting fermions in a two-dimensional harmonic trap, the method demonstrates stable training and produces a learnt nodal structure that smoothly deforms away from the free-particle reference, lowering the variational thermodynamic energy at each temperature. While absolute energy benchmarking is currently limited by the absence of a nodal action in the estimator, the work establishes a physics-informed framework for self-consistently learning nodal surfaces in finite-temperature quantum Monte Carlo.
items.citation: Jarvist Moore Frost. Spindrift: Learning quantum degeneracy from thermal purity in restricted path integral Monte Carlo. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The Tartu Observatory Fiber-fed Echelle Spectrograph (TOFES) Data Reduction Pipeline
items.summary: The paper presents the data reduction pipeline developed for a fiber-fed echelle spectrograph installed at a coudé room and designed to connect to a telescope through a multi-channel instrument adapter. The spectrograph covers a broad optical-to-near-infrared wavelength range in a single exposure at moderate-to-high spectral resolution. The pipeline is built upon an existing Python-based reduction package and was validated using solar spectra, with an additional custom toolbox developed to support spectral diagnostics and radial velocity measurements. The instrument and its pipeline are intended to support scientific programs including the characterization of young stellar objects and their protoplanetary disk accretion, the study of exoplanet host stars relevant to a space mission, and monitoring of atmospheric variability in massive stars.
items.citation: Sandipan P. D. Borthakur, Tõnis Eenmäe, Nikolai Piskunov et al.. The Tartu Observatory Fiber-fed Echelle Spectrograph (TOFES) Data Reduction Pipeline. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Prior therapy defines mutation profiles in childhood cancer at relapse
items.summary: This study investigated the extent of DNA damage caused by chemotherapy and radiotherapy in childhood cancers by analyzing whole-genome-sequenced tumors from a large multi-institutional cohort with carefully recorded treatment histories. The researchers applied mutational signature analysis to compare treatment-naive tumors with post-therapy relapsed tumors, tracking how different therapeutic exposures shaped the genomic landscape of cancers. They found that chemotherapy and radiotherapy were the dominant sources of DNA mutation in relapsed tumors, with post-therapy cancers carrying approximately three times as many private mutational signatures and roughly double the overall somatic mutation burden compared to untreated tumors. Platinum-based chemotherapies were particularly mutagenic, generating the highest variant counts in most patients, and detectable platinum-associated mutational signatures emerged within one year of treatment in more than a third of cases. The authors conclude that chemotherapy is a critical driver of tumor evolution in childhood cancer and that these findings open possibilities for treatment de-escalation and early monitoring of resistant clones before they expand.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention because it demonstrates that chemotherapy—especially platinum-based regimens—dramatically reshapes the mutational landscape of childhood cancers by the time of relapse, suggesting that treatment itself is actively driving tumour evolution and pointing toward potential strategies for safer, de-escalated therapies.

items.title: A vector-based strategy for olfactory navigation in Drosophila
items.summary: This paper investigated how fruit flies navigate through structured odor environments, specifically asking whether they use simple reflexive responses or more complex memory-based strategies to track odor plumes. Using a virtual-reality olfactory paradigm with head-fixed flies exploring chemical landscapes, the researchers combined behavioral modeling, calcium imaging, and neural perturbations to dissect the underlying mechanisms. They found that flies track an appetitive odor corridor through an "edge tracking" strategy, alternating between rapid counter-turns away from the plume and directed returns to its boundary. This strategy depends on vector-based computations in the central complex, where flies store and update directional memories of the plume boundary's location, with specific neurons in the fan-shaped body encoding the goal direction when flies are outside the plume. The findings demonstrate that odor plume tracking engages conserved navigational circuitry capable of supporting memory-guided, spatially directed movement through complex chemical environments.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention by revealing that flies employ a memory-based vector strategy to navigate odour plumes and locate scent sources, a finding demonstrated through virtual reality experiments that shed new light on the neural mechanisms underlying olfactory-guided behaviour.
items.citation: Andrew F. Siliciano, Sun Minni, Chad Morton et al.. A vector-based strategy for olfactory navigation in Drosophila. Nature. 2026

items.title: The planktonic microbiome of the Great Barrier Reef
items.summary: This paper characterized the planktonic microbiome of the Great Barrier Reef by generating a comprehensive genomic database of prokaryotes, picoeukaryotes, and viruses from reef seawater. The researchers combined Nanopore long-read and Illumina short-read sequencing to overcome limitations of standard short-read approaches, which systematically miss certain dominant marine lineages due to strain heterogeneity and low-GC-content sequencing bias. The resulting database includes thousands of prokaryotic genomes, chromosome-level picoeukaryote assemblies, and hundreds of thousands of viral genomes, among them a newly described clade of marine viruses. The authors also demonstrated a practical application of this resource by identifying microbial indicator taxa capable of reliably predicting the ecological effects of reef management practices, including the establishment of marine protected zones.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it delivers a comprehensive genomic database spanning prokaryotes, viruses, and eukaryotes from one of the world's most iconic and ecologically significant marine ecosystems. The resource is notable for its potential to advance both fundamental research into marine microbial communities and practical efforts in reef management and conservation.

items.title: A global molecular code for birth order and neuronal identity in Drosophila
items.summary: This study investigated how molecular identity and neuronal diversity are established during nervous system development in *Drosophila melanogaster*, focusing on the nerve cord as a central hub for sensorimotor circuits. The researchers generated a high-resolution developmental transcriptional atlas of the nerve cord using single-cell transcriptomics, achieving extensive coverage that allowed robust alignment to an existing adult connectome. They identified three overarching developmental principles: the timing of neurogenesis shapes molecular diversification, with embryonic-born neurons diverging more rapidly than larval-born neurons; a set of transcription factors common across all lineages encodes a global molecular identity code based on birth order; and sex-specific differences arise through female-specific apoptosis and transcriptional divergence. By linking transcriptional profiles to connectome data, the atlas provides a framework for understanding how molecular mechanisms govern the development, organization, and evolution of neural circuits.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention by revealing that a unified transcriptional code governs both when neurons are born and what identities they acquire, offering a broadly applicable framework for understanding how neuronal diversity is organized during development.
items.citation: Sebastian Cachero, Myrto Mitletton, Isabella R. Beckett et al.. A global molecular code for birth order and neuronal identity in Drosophila. Nature. 2026

items.title: Subnuclear genome compartmentalization controls bivalent chromatin activity
items.summary: This paper investigated how the three-dimensional organization of the genome within the nucleus regulates gene expression during human brain development. The researchers generated high-resolution maps of genomic interactions with two subnuclear compartments—the nuclear lamina and nuclear speckles—in neurogenic cells isolated from the developing human cortex. They found that during cortical neurogenesis, hundreds of genes, including key neurodevelopmental genes carrying bivalent chromatin marks, are repositioned from the repressive lamina environment to active speckles, where their chromatin state resolves toward active monovalency and their transcription increases dramatically. Critically, the study demonstrated that it is physical proximity to the nuclear periphery, rather than the presence of the repressive histone mark H3K27me3, that maintains bivalent genes in a poised, lowly expressed state, an effect associated with spatial exclusion of the transcriptional elongation machinery from the nuclear lamina. The findings establish that subnuclear genome compartmentalization is a fundamental determinant of epigenomic regulation and gene activity during human development.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention because it demonstrates that where a gene is physically located within the nucleus is a key factor in understanding how its epigenomic regulation operates, particularly for bivalent chromatin. The findings suggest that subnuclear compartmentalization—not just chemical marks alone—controls gene activity in ways not previously fully appreciated.
items.citation: Sajad Hamid Ahanger, Evan R. Semenza, Chujing Zhang et al.. Subnuclear genome compartmentalization controls bivalent chromatin activity. Nature. 2026

items.title: Imaging of nanoscale polar textures in quantum paraelectric SrTiO3
items.summary: This study investigated the low-temperature polar structure of the quantum paraelectric material strontium titanate, which has long resisted direct structural characterization despite extensive research. Using cryogenic scanning transmission electron microscopy down to very low temperatures, the researchers directly imaged the real-space arrangement of polar domains in a strontium titanate lamella across a range of temperatures. They found that below approximately one hundred and five kelvin, nanoscale polar domains spontaneously self-organize into a periodic, modulated structure extending over tens of nanometres, consistent with earlier hints from anomalous phonon dynamics. However, upon entering the quantum paraelectric regime at lower temperatures, this periodically ordered nanodomain structure breaks apart into smaller, disordered clusters rather than developing long-range ferroelectric order. The authors propose that the remarkable physical properties associated with quantum paraelectricity in strontium titanate, including its giant dielectric permittivity, proximity to ferroelectricity, and unconventional superconductivity, may be intimately connected to this temperature-dependent cycle of polar nanodomain ordering and fragmentation.
items.why_notable: The work draws attention because it provides direct nanoscale imaging evidence that a material long considered a quantum paraelectric actually develops structured polar domains at low temperatures, before those domains break apart at even lower temperatures. This connects the material's unusual macroscopic electrical behavior to concrete nanoscale structural phenomena, resolving a longstanding question about the microscopic origin of quantum paraelectricity.
items.citation: Yang Zhang, Suk Hyun Sung, Nishkarsh Agarwal et al.. Imaging of nanoscale polar textures in quantum paraelectric SrTiO3. Nature. 2026

items.title: Exceptional brain and ecological diversity in the earliest snakes
items.summary: This paper investigated the early evolution of snakes, a topic previously hampered by a poor fossil record and disagreements about the ecology of early snake lineages. The researchers described a new species of exceptionally preserved Cretaceous snake from Brazil, using high-resolution micro-CT scanning to reconstruct cranial nerves, inner ear structures, and brain anatomy in unprecedented detail. Analyses of the brain endocast revealed a neuroanatomy distinct from both other early-diverging and living snakes, indicating that substantial diversity in brain morphology and probably sensory function arose very early in snake evolution. Convergent evidence from brain shape and bone microstructure supported a fossorial lifestyle for the new species but a non-fossorial lifestyle for another early snake, demonstrating that major ecological transitions occurred near the base of the snake tree. The findings indicate that early snakes were far more ecologically and neuroanatomically diverse than previously recognized, and that known stem species should not be treated as proxies for the ancestral condition of all living snakes.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because a remarkably well-preserved fossil snake reveals that early snakes already possessed surprising diversity in both their ecological adaptations and brain morphology, pushing back evidence of this complexity to the Late Cretaceous.
items.citation: Tiago R. Simões, Gabriela Sobral, Simone Macrì et al.. Exceptional brain and ecological diversity in the earliest snakes. Nature. 2026

items.title: Brown bullhead catfish melanoma represents a novel transmissible cancer
items.summary: The paper investigated unusually high rates of melanoma in brown bullhead catfish from a shared lake, testing whether this disease represents a transmissible cancer rather than one caused by environmental contaminants. Using whole-genome sequencing of tumour and matched non-tumour host tissues, the researchers compared mitochondrial and nuclear genomes across affected fish. They found that tumour genomes were far more closely related to one another than to the host fish in which they resided, with hundreds of thousands of genetic variants shared among tumour samples but absent from hosts — a pattern inconsistent with conventional cancers. These findings indicate that the melanomas arise from clonally transmissible cancer cells spreading between individual fish as parasitic entities. This discovery establishes the brown bullhead catfish melanoma as the fourth documented naturally occurring transmissible cancer in animals, joining examples in dogs, Tasmanian devils, and several bivalve species.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it identifies a previously unknown form of naturally occurring transmissible cancer, discovered through genomic analysis of a wild fish species, adding to the rare category of cancers known to spread between individual animals.
items.citation: Emily Curd, Samuel F. M. Hart, James Lubkowitz et al.. Brown bullhead catfish melanoma represents a novel transmissible cancer. Nature. 2026

items.title: Genetic background sets the trajectory of experimental cancer evolution
items.summary: This paper investigated how germline genetic variation shapes the trajectory of tumour evolution, a question difficult to address in humans due to uncontrolled genetic and environmental diversity. The researchers re-ran early tumour evolution hundreds of times across diverged inbred mouse strains under controlled conditions for sex, environment, and carcinogenic exposure, generating matched histology, whole-genome, and transcriptome data that captured genetic variation comparable to that seen across human populations. By exploiting the nested hierarchical structure of strain, litter, animal, and tumour relationships, they were able to isolate the effects of genetic background on cancer development. Their analyses revealed that epistatic interactions between germline genetic background and acquired somatic mutations drive population-specific patterns of disease progression, including differences in driver mutation selection, whole-genome duplication frequency, and subclonal dynamics that correspond to cancer susceptibility and tumour growth rates. They conclude that even modest levels of genetic divergence, similar to that observed across human ancestry groups, can substantially alter the selective pressures governing cancer risk and the path of tumour evolution.
items.why_notable: This work draws attention because it demonstrates that inherited genetic background—not just acquired cancer mutations alone—fundamentally shapes how tumors evolve from their earliest stages, a finding with broad implications for understanding cancer risk and progression across individuals with different genetic ancestries.

The method offers specificity for the desired three-dimensional arrangement of atoms, addressing a key challenge in carbohydrate-based synthesis. The authors claim this route provides a more accessible pathway to an important class of pharmaceutical compounds.

items.title: Background genetics and new mutations interact to direct cancer evolution
items.summary: The paper investigated how inherited genetic background and newly acquired mutations jointly influence the trajectory of cancer evolution following DNA damage. Using mouse models, the researchers experimentally reran tumour evolution to examine how these two factors interact to shape genome stability and the selection of cancer-driving changes. The findings demonstrate that genetic ancestry plays a meaningful role in determining which mutational paths a tumour takes, with inherited genomic context and somatic mutations working together rather than independently. This work provides experimental evidence that cancer evolution is not driven solely by acquired mutations but is substantially guided by the pre-existing genetic constitution of an organism.

items.title: Fly neurons carry a molecular ‘timestamp’ that encodes their birth order
items.summary: This paper studied how neurons in the fly nervous system acquire and encode their positional identity during development. By constructing a single-cell gene-expression atlas of the fly nerve cord and mapping it onto the wiring diagram, the researchers identified a shared molecular code present across neurons throughout the central brain and nerve cord. They found that this gene-expression code functions as a "timestamp," allowing neurons to retain a molecular memory of the sequence in which they were born from their parent stem cells. This birth-order code appears to be universal across the stem cells that generate the fly central nervous system and contributes to shaping neuronal diversity.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals that fly neurons retain a molecular record of the sequence in which they were born from a parent cell, encoded in a shared gene-expression code. This molecular "timestamp" appears to be a fundamental mechanism shaping neuronal diversity, discovered by integrating a single-cell gene-expression atlas with the nerve cord's wiring diagram.

items.title: Geomagnetic storms caused by solar wind might be more extreme than previously thought
items.summary: The paper investigated whether geomagnetic storms — disturbances in Earth's outer atmosphere driven by solar wind — truly have an upper limit in their severity. The prevailing understanding had been that geomagnetic storm intensity plateaus as solar wind strength increases, implying a natural ceiling on disturbance magnitude. The authors argue that this apparent upper limit is a statistical artifact arising from regression to the mean, whereby measurement uncertainty in solar wind strength causes extreme true values to appear more moderate than they are. Correcting for this bias removes the evidence for any such ceiling, suggesting that geomagnetic storms could be far more severe than previously thought.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it challenges the long-accepted idea that geomagnetic storms have a natural upper limit in severity, showing instead that this apparent ceiling is a statistical artifact caused by measurement uncertainty and regression to the mean. The implication is that geomagnetic storms could be far more extreme than current models assume.
